title: Recreation Aide-Fitness
description:
WE'RE HIRING!

Recreation Aide - Fitness

Join Our Team and Make a Difference in the Community!

The Fitness Recreation Aide is responsible for the supervision of the fitness areas specifically for providing adult and youth orientations, assisting with general fitness related questions, monitoring participants as they work out, general cleaning of the fitness center and equipment, and other duties as specified by supervisor on duty.

If you are an energetic, organized, and community-minded individual who loves creating memorable recreational experiences, we would love to hear from you!

Please apply on the City's website www.richmondheights.org by the application deadline.

Help us bring our community together through recreation, creativity, and fun!

At Bigham Cable Construction, Inc., as a Fiber Splicer, you’ll complete the process of fusing optical fibers, to maintain our telecommunication networks.Your splicing work is essential for keeping strong and reliable connections, ensuring data travels seamlessly through our continually growing network.

title: Senior Salesforce Platform Engineer
description:

AutoRABIT is an enterprise platform for Salesforce DevSecOps that enables organizations to manage AI-accelerated Salesforce development with greater security, governance, visibility, and control. Its integrated product suite supports the complete Salesforce DevSecOps lifecycle through AutoRABIT ARM for CI/CD and release management, CodeScan for static code analysis and application security, Vault for data backup and recovery, and Guard for security posture management. The platform helps enterprises automate deployments, improve code quality, protect critical Salesforce data, monitor access risks, and strengthen compliance. Purpose-built for complex enterprise Salesforce environments, AutoRABIT helps development teams increase productivity, accelerate delivery, and innovate without compromising security or reliability.

- Strong written communication and attention to detail.

title: Business Process Analyst
description:
What It Means to Be a Consultant at Crowe :

Consulting is a dynamic business focused on solving problems for our clients and serving our core markets through innovative solutions. As technology and AI continue to reshape the consulting landscape, we are looking for individuals who are curious, adaptable, and eager to learn. At Crowe, consultants are expected to build both technical and transferable skills, think critically, and use technology to solve real business problems. You are expected to contribute to account planning, identify opportunities to add value, and ensure high-quality delivery. As your responsibilities expand, you take on broader account ownership, balancing project leadership with growing involvement in client strategy and solution development.

Success in this role comes from a growth mindset, strong communication skills, advanced critical thinking, and the ability to navigate new challenges with confidence.

Crowe's Microsoft Consulting Practice is hiring an Agentic Business Process Analyst to help clients rethink how work gets done in the AI era. This is not a traditional business analyst role focused only on documenting requirements, writing user stories, or mapping current-state processes. This role is for someone who can diagnose business problems, understand root causes, redesign processes, and identify where AI agents, automation, data, and human judgment should come together.

The ideal candidate is deeply functional, process-oriented, and comfortable enough with technology to work side by side with engineers, architects, and client IT teams. This person should be able to bridge business and technology, helping clients move from legacy workflows to intelligent, agent-enabled processes.

This role also has an internal transformation mandate. The person will help upskill Crowe Consulting teams that may be used to traditional ERP, CRM, or business application delivery. They will help consultants develop a more modern mindset: start with problems, then processes, then technology.

What you will do :

- Lead discovery sessions with clients to understand business goals, pain points, process breakdowns, data issues, user needs, controls, and operating constraints.

- Map end-to-end business processes, including inputs, outputs, roles, systems, decisions, handoffs, exceptions, controls, and performance measures.

- Diagnose root causes across people, process, data, and technology before recommending solutions.

- Identify opportunities for AI assistance, agentic augmentation, workflow orchestration, automation, knowledge retrieval, decision support, and process improvement.

- Partner with technical architects and engineers to translate process opportunities into solution designs, prototypes, functional specifications, user stories, and delivery roadmaps.

- Define business value measures for agentic solutions, such as time saved, cycle time reduction, first-time-right rate, SLA performance, adoption, override rate, CSAT, cost per transaction, revenue lift, and compliance improvement.

- Help clients decide where humans should stay in control, where AI should assist, and where agents can safely orchestrate or automate work.

- Support workshops, demos, process redesign sessions, executive presentations, and change management conversations.

- Create reusable playbooks, templates, process models, and training materials to help Crowe teams adopt an agentic business analysis approach.

- Coach Crowe consultants on how to move beyond legacy requirements gathering into diagnostic, value-led, AI-enabled transformation work.

What success looks like :

- You can walk into a messy client process and make sense of it quickly.

- You can separate symptoms from root causes.

- You know when the right answer is process redesign, data cleanup, integration, training, governance, automation, or AI.

- You can help clients and internal teams understand what agents should do, what humans should do, and how to measure whether the new process is better.

- You make technical teams sharper by giving them better process context, and you make business teams more confident by helping them understand what technology can realistically do.

Basic Qualifications :

- 6+ years as a Business Analyst, Functional Consultant, or Process Consultant.

- Strong business process mapping and redesign experience.

- Experience with Microsoft Dynamics 365 and/or Power Platform implementations.

- Ability to facilitate client workshops and engage executive stakeholders.

- Exposure to AI, automation, or agentic transformation initiatives.

Preferred Qualifications:

- Exposure to responsible AI, governance, risk, compliance, controls, or regulated industry environments.

title: Senior Data Scientist - Python
description:
Are you looking to work in the cutting edge area of applying data-science to help global customers get a better insight into their health? If so, read on and apply.

Role Name : Senior Data Scientist

Science Team | Full-Time | In-Office | Bangalore

The Role :

The Ultrahuman Science Team builds the algorithms behind the Ring, M1 CGM, blood and urine biomarkers, and Performance Lab assessments. We are hiring a Senior Data Scientist to own those algorithms end to end : from the raw sensor signal to a model that is shipped, monitored, and trusted in users' hands.

This is a build role with real scope. In a typical month you will improve a production algorithm, root-cause a metric users are complaining about, and stand up the data pipeline the next model needs. The common thread is ownership : you take a vague question and return a working answer, without waiting to be handed scope.

What You'll Do :

- Own algorithms end to end : sleep staging, activity detection, sensor-derived metrics, and health scores. You frame the problem, build the features, train and evaluate the model, and see it live.

- Ship models, not notebooks : you prove a change on our own cohort before it reaches users, and a model is done only when it runs in production and you can tell how it is behaving.

- Validate against reference standards : design evaluations against gold standards, reference devices, and study ground truth, and know when a result is real and when it is an artifact.

- Own the data layer : cohort extraction, feature pipelines, study data, and raw sensor data, so the next model starts from clean inputs.

What This Looks Like in Practice :

1. Improving production algorithms :

- Take an existing production model like sleep staging, root-cause the failure modes against reference data, and ship a fix you can defend with numbers.

2. Building new models :

- Train an activity classifier on raw sensor data, design the labeled data collection that expands it, and pick the operating point so false positives never erode trust.

3. Proving it before it ships :

- Run a new steps algorithm against reference-device cohorts, decide with data when it is ready, and monitor how it behaves after rollout.

Who You Are :

The two things we can't coach :

- High ownership, end to end : you take a problem from a vague question to a shipped model without waiting to be handed scope, and you can point to something you owned from raw data all the way to production.

- Hungry for more scope : you have outgrown your current role and want problems bigger than your title, with the technical depth to be trusted with them.

Also important :

- You've worked with human health data : wearables, physiological signals, or clinical data.

If your experience is close but not exact, show us why you will ramp fast :

- You've built at a startup : or somewhere small enough that nobody handed you clean data, clear specs, or a mature ML platform.

- You work like it's 2026 : coding agents and AI tooling are part of how you build every day, and you can tell which new capabilities are worth adopting.

- You communicate : you can explain a model and its limits to a product manager, an engineer, or a founder, and hold your own with our scientists.

Core Technical Skills :

- Languages and data : Python and SQL daily, comfortable working in a real codebase.

- Machine learning : PyTorch or TensorFlow, scikit-learn, and gradient boosting, with the judgment to know which the problem needs.

- Advanced machine learning : time series and sequence models, deep learning on continuous physiological signals, and ensembles.

- Statistics and evaluation : hypothesis testing, experiment and A/B design, model evaluation, and error analysis against a reference standard.

- Scale and cloud : Spark or equivalent on large datasets, and AWS, GCP, or Azure.

- Production ML and MLOps : training pipelines, model versioning, deployment, monitoring, and drift detection.

- LLMs and agentic systems : fine-tuning and serving models, building agentic pipelines, and using coding agents to move faster.

Experience :

- 4 - 5 years building and shipping machine learning systems. We index on what you have shipped and on trajectory, not the exact number of years; if you are a little earlier but have clearly outgrown your current scope, we want to hear from you.

- Bachelor's or higher in engineering, computer science, statistics, or a related field.

How We Work and Who Thrives Here :

- The Science team is small and moves fast, and much of the work has no precedent to copy.

- People do their best work here when they are energized by ambiguity, low on ego, quick to adopt a better idea no matter where it comes from, and comfortable owning something before anyone has told them how. If you need a mature data org, clean labelled datasets, and clear guardrails to thrive, this particular role will not be the right fit, and that is worth knowing up front.

What You'll Gain :

- Ownership of algorithms that hundreds of thousands of people see every morning.

- A dataset most scientists never get to touch : 100M+ nights of sleep and continuous physiological signals at scale.

- Direct collaboration with the engineering, product, and design teams building Ultrahuman.

title: Senior AI/ML Engineer - Observability Services
description:
About the Role :

We are hiring a Senior AI/ML Engineer to own the end-to-end applied LLM, retrieval, and evaluation layer of our healthcare AI platform. You will build production systems that automate mid- and end-revenue cycle workflows for US healthcare spanning coding, claim edits, denial triage, appeal generation, and payer-rule reasoning. This is a production engineering role focused on building scalable, auditable, and cost-efficient LLM systems in a regulated healthcare environment.

Self-Hosted LLM Infrastructure :

- Deploy, fine-tune, and operate open-source models (Llama, Qwen, MedGemma, and successors) as our primary inference stack.

- Work with vLLM / SGLang / TensorRT-LLM for serving at scale, with disciplined attention to throughput, tail latency, batching, KV-cache, and GPU economics.

- Own fine-tuning workflows end-to-end (SFT, LoRA, QLoRA, DPO) on clinical notes, claims, and payer-rule data.

- Optimize GPU usage, latency, batching, and cost; make build-vs-buy and hosted-vs-self-hosted trade-offs explicit and measured.

Knowledge Graphs and Embedding-Based Retrieval :

- Design and maintain the knowledge graph encoding ICD-10-CM, CPT, HCPCS, modifiers, HCC, NCCI edits, LCD/NCD policies, and payer-specific rules.

- Build embedding-based retrieval over clinical notes, historical claims, denial reasons, and payer-policy corpora, including chunking, embedding model selection, hybrid search, and reranking.

- Combine graph traversal and dense retrieval so every coded line, scrubbed edit, and appeal response is grounded in auditable evidence.

- Own ingestion, versioning, and quality of underlying knowledge sources (CMS, AHA, AMA, NCCI, payer bulletins).

Evaluation and Monitoring :

- Build continuous evaluation pipelines that gate every model, prompt, retrieval, and graph change before production.

- Run offline eval suites grounded in coder- and biller-validated labels; use LLM-as-judge where appropriate, calibrated against human ground truth.

- Monitor drift, hallucinations, regressions, and output quality in production; operate shadow-mode rollouts and per-cohort accuracy tracking.

- Track business metrics: chart-level and opportunity-level coding accuracy, denial rate impact, clean-claim rate, cost per chart, and end-to-end latency.

LLM Systems and Prompt Engineering :

- Design prompts and context pipelines for coding, claim edits, denial classification, and appeal drafting.

- Implement structured outputs (JSON, function calling, constrained decoding) on top of the self-hosted stack.

- Apply RAG over medical coding standards (CMS, ICD-10 AHA, NCCI) and payer policies, grounded in the knowledge graph and embedding stores.

- Treat prompts as a thin, well-versioned, well-evaluated layer, never the load-bearing piece.

Agentic Workflows and Tooling MCP :

- Build MCP servers for internal tools: code lookup, NCCI / rule checks, payer logic, eligibility, and denial classification.

- Design multi-step agent workflows with audit trails and human-in-the-loop checkpoints for coder, biller, and AR-analyst review.

- Define deterministic vs. LLM-based tool boundaries for reliability.

Requirements :

- 5+ years in ML/AI engineering, including 6+ months in production LLM systems.

- Hands-on experience deploying and operating self-hosted LLMs (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, or equivalent).

- Strong experience designing embedding-based retrieval and/or knowledge graphs for grounded LLM applications.

- Demonstrated ownership of evaluation infrastructure, offline benchmarks, online monitoring, drift, and regression detection.

- Strong Python + PyTorch + Hugging Face experience.

- Production experience with monitoring, incidents, and system ownership.

Strongly Preferred :

- Fine-tuning experience (SFT, LoRA, QLoRA, DPO) on domain-specific corpora.

- Experience with graph databases (Neo4j, ArangoDB, or equivalent) and graph-aware retrieval.

- Experience with vector databases and hybrid search (BM25 + dense, rerankers).

- Familiarity with LLM observability tools (Langfuse, LangSmith, Arize, Braintrust, or in-house equivalents).

- Exposure to healthcare, RCM, claims, or other regulated domains.

- Experience with MCP or similar tool-orchestration frameworks.

- Strong prompt-engineering and LLM-evaluation instincts.

title: Data Scientist - AI/ML
description:
About The Company :

Experience : 5 - 8 years

Employment Type : Contractual (6 Months, extendable based on performance/business need)

Location : Hybrid from India or Vietnam

About the Role :

We're looking for an experienced Data Scientist to support an AI-powered classification platform built around a single LLM agent (using disambiguation, lookup, and determination functions) operating inside a large enterprise client's Azure-based AI infrastructure. The immediate priority is instrumenting real usage to replace planning assumptions with measured data, and rigorously evaluating whether the LLM agent meets the accuracy bar required for production use in a regulated, audit-sensitive domain.


mloA conditional later phase may introduce a classical ML hybrid engine if the LLM-only approach doesn't clear that bar - this candidate should be equipped for that work if it materializes, but it is not the day-one focus. This is a hands-on role for a practitioner comfortable working close to a live evaluation and instrumentation effort, not a greenfield model-building engagement.

Key Responsibilities :

- Design and implement instrumentation to convert planning assumptions - token consumption, cache/reuse hit rate, model tier selection, retrieval-context sizing - into measured figures from representative traffic

- Analyze usage data to validate or revise pre-launch cost and volume estimates

- Design and build the evaluation framework and ground-truth test set used to determine whether the LLM agent can classify reliably and independently against a defined rules framework

- Define and calibrate accuracy thresholds and confidence scoring that determine whether a secondary classical modeling phase is needed

- Analyze classification errors and failure modes to distinguish disambiguation gaps, retrieval gaps, and reasoning gaps

- Evaluate explainability/audit quality of agent-generated decision records against compliance requirements - outputs need to satisfy audit trail standards, not just accuracy metrics

Conditional - Hybrid Classical Modeling Phase :

- Design, train, and validate classical ML classifiers for structured, hierarchical classification tasks

- Establish retraining cadence, drift detection, and confidence-band calibration

- Produce model explainability outputs (e.g., SHAP/LIME) suitable for regulatory audit review

Ongoing Responsibilities :

- Build and maintain MLOps pipelines for evaluation, monitoring, and (if the classical modeling phase triggers) model deployment and retraining, within Azure environment or AWS

- Collaborate with engineering, platform, and compliance stakeholders to translate compliance and accuracy requirements into evaluation and modeling design

- Document methodology, evaluation results, and modeling decisions clearly for both technical and business/compliance audiences

Required Skills :

- 5 - 8 years of professional experience in Data Science / AI / ML roles

- LLM evaluation methodology - building test sets, defining accuracy/quality metrics, and rigorously assessing LLM-based system performance

- Practical experience with RAG systems and prompt engineering, including retrieval quality assessment

- Strong proficiency in Python and relevant ML/data libraries (scikit-learn, PyTorch, or similar)

- Solid understanding of statistics, probability, and ML algorithms

- Experience with SQL and working with structured/semi-structured datasets at moderate scale

- Hands-on MLOps pipeline experience (MLflow, Airflow, Kubeflow, or cloud-native equivalents)

- Working experience with Azure ML tooling (required); AWS ML tooling experience also valuable

- Familiarity with containerized deployment (Docker; Kubernetes a plus)

- Experience with data visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI, or Matplotlib/Seaborn)

- Strong analytical rigor and comfort working with ambiguous, evolving requirements

- Excellent communication skills - ability to present evaluation findings to both engineering and compliance/business stakeholders

- Bachelor's/Master's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Mathematics, or related field

Good to Have :

- Experience with NLP or classical text classification

- Experience with regulated/compliance-sensitive domains (audit trails, explainability requirements)

- Prior experience in contract/consulting roles with fast ramp-up

- Familiarity with Spark for batch data processing

Contract Details :

- Engagement Type : Contractual

- Start Date : Immediate / 30 days

title: Director of brand & creative
description:
Contentsquare is the all-in-one experience intelligence platform designed to be easily used by anyone who cares about digital journeys. With our flexible and scalable platform, organizations quickly get a deep understanding of their customers’ whole online journey.
We are a global leader in the experience analytics space, with a growing presence across 15 offices worldwide. We’re here to stay—and we’re looking for team members who are excited to drive impact and help us scale even further.
Our aim is to create an inclusive workplace where everyone learns and succeeds. Contentsquare has built a community of individuals who are daring, understanding, and deliberate. We invite you to join us in making the complex simpler—for our customers, their customers, and each other.
Important note: Be careful of scammers pretending to be from Contentsquare. We will never ask for money or contact you through random texts. Any communication from our in house Talent Acquisition team will only ever come from our or @contentsquare-ext.com domain. For more information, visit our careers blog.

We are looking for a senior creative leader to define the next chapter of Contentsquare’s brand and lead the evolution of our global Studio.

You will set the creative vision for how Contentsquare shows up in the world. Your mission is to elevate our brand, making it more distinctive, modern, and recognizable, and ensuring our creative expression positions us as a leader in our industry.

You will drive the creative evolution of our brand across every touchpoint, from campaigns and product launches to web, events, motion, and executive storytelling. You'll push creative boundaries, champion bold ideas, and set an exceptional standard for quality and differentiation.

A key part of the role is translating complex technology, data, and AI innovation into simple, compelling creative experiences. You'll partner closely with Product, Product Marketing, Brand, and GTM teams to understand what makes our platform unique and bring that story to life.

You'll also lead and transform our global Studio, developing a high-performing team of designers, creative leads, and agency partners. You'll evolve our brand system and embrace AI, automation, and self-service to scale production, freeing the team to focus on creativity, craft, and high-impact work.

Your mission: build a category-defining brand and a world-class, AI-enabled creative organization to bring it to life.

What you’ll own

Brand creative direction

  • Set the creative vision for Contentsquare and hold an exceptional standard across launches, campaigns, brand, web, events, and executive storytelling.

  • Champion bold ideas, challenge conventional thinking, and push the team beyond safe, predictable creative work.

  • Stay ahead of what the best brands are doing, in SaaS, AI, technology, and beyond, to create work that is unmistakably ours.

    • The team

    • Lead, develop, and retain exceptional designers and team leads, building a high-performing culture of craft, bold thinking, ownership, and accountability. Empower the team to take creative risks and make strong decisions independently.

    • Build and manage a network of world-class agencies and specialist partners, bringing fresh perspectives and expertise. Own agency selection, creative direction, budgets, and performance, ensuring exceptional quality and the flexibility to scale during peak demand.

      • The platform and product story

      • Build a deep understanding of our platform, AI capabilities, and technology, keeping the Studio closely connected to our product and customers.

      • Partner early with Product and Product Marketing to turn complex technology into simple, compelling, and memorable creative experiences.

      • Bring our product story to life through distinctive design, motion, video, and storytelling across every relevant touchpoint.

        • The Brand System

        • Evolve our visual identity into a distinctive, recognizable, and scalable brand system that reflects our ambition as an AI leader.

        • Build reusable frameworks, templates, and self-service tools that help teams create effectively without compromising quality.

        • Know when to scale through the system and when an idea deserves something entirely new.

          • AI in the studio

          • Lead how the Studio uses AI across design, copy, production, and creative operations.

          • Use AI to absorb repetitive work and production volume, expanding creative capabilities and giving the team more time for ideas, craft, and innovation.

          • Help the team adopt new tools and workflows confidently, without compromising creative quality or brand standards.

            • How the creative studio runs

            • Own the Studio operating model, including priorities, resourcing, project management, creative reviews, and delivery across internal teams and external partners.

            • Build a fast, effective, and scalable operation that anticipates demand, manages production peaks, and removes unnecessary complexity.

            • Partner closely with Product, Product Marketing, Brand, Content, Web, Comms, and GTM teams, engaging early enough to shape the work rather than simply receive briefs.

What We’re Looking For

  • 10+ years across design, brand, creative, or Studio leadership, including 5+ years leading teams in SaaS or technology.

  • Experience managing managers/team leads and operating in complex, global organizations.

  • Exceptional portfolio with a high creative bar across brand, digital, campaigns, and product storytelling.

  • Strong ability to turn complex technology and AI into simple, compelling creative narratives.

  • Deep understanding of SaaS/tech; AI or AI-native experience is a strong plus.

  • Proven experience evolving brand/design systems and scaling quality through templates and self-service.

  • Hands-on experience transforming creative teams with AI across workflows, automation, production, and enablement.

  • Strong command of Creative Operations, resourcing, agencies, and end-to-end Studio workflows.

  • Strong benchmarking instincts and a clear point of view on differentiation and creative excellence.
  • Excellent executive communication and cross-functional partnership skills.

You’ll Thrive in This Role If You

  • Have exceptional creative taste and a strong point of view on what our brand could become.

  • Understand the product deeply enough to find the creative idea within it, rather than waiting for a brief to define it.

  • Turn complex technology, data, and AI into simple, human, and memorable creative experiences.

  • Know what the best brands are doing, both in our category and far beyond it, and are more interested in what nobody has done yet.

  • Move confidently between setting creative vision, challenging the details, shaping product storytelling, and leading a high-performing team.

  • See AI as a way to take more creative risks, not fewer. Let it handle the volume so your team can focus on the work only people can do.

  • Build simple systems that keep creative teams fast, collaborative, and effective, while knowing which work deserves something entirely original.

  • Challenge work that's merely good enough, inspiring teams and agency partners to push for exceptional.

  • Balance bold creative ambition with a strong understanding of customer impact and business outcomes.

What Success Looks Like

Within your first year, we would expect to see:

  • A visibly higher and more consistent creative bar across the company.

  • A distinctive creative language for our platform, products, and AI capabilities that makes complex technology easier to understand and more exciting to experience.

  • A Studio that is deeply connected to Product and Product Marketing and engaged earlier in the storytelling process.

  • Strong differentiation from competitors across our visual identity, campaigns, product launches, and customer-facing experiences.

  • A strong, scalable brand and design system.

  • A clear Studio operating model with stronger prioritization, ownership, and delivery.

  • Meaningful adoption of AI across creative workflows, resulting in faster execution, better output, and expanded team capacity.

  • More teams able to self-serve effectively through high-quality templates, systems, and guidelines.

  • Strong leadership across the Studio, with team leads operating with greater autonomy and accountability.

  • Better balance between internal resources, agencies, automation, and self-service.

  • A Studio viewed by the business not as a production function, but as a strategic partner in how we bring our product and technology to the world.

Why you should join Contentsquare
We invest in our people through career development, mentorship, social events, philanthropic activities, and competitive benefits. We are always assessing the perks we offer to ensure we’re aligned with the employees' needs.
Here are a few we want to highlight:
- Virtual onboarding, Hackathon, and various opportunities to interact with your team and global colleagues both on and offsite each year
- Work flexibility: hybrid and remote work policies
- Generous paid time-off policy (every location is different)
- Lifestyle allowance
- A Culture Crew in every country we’re based in to coordinate regular activities for employees to get to know each other and bond outside of work
- Every full-time employee receives stock options, allowing them to share in the company’s success
- We have multiple Employee Resource Groups, that offer a safe space for individuals who share common identities, life experiences, or allyship to connect, support one another, and passionately advocate for the issues close to their hearts
- And more benefits tailored to each country
Contentsquare is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to sex, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law.
Your personal data is used by Contentsquare for recruitment purposes only. Read our Job Candidate Privacy Notice to find out more about data protection at Contentsquare and your rights. You can exercise your rights by using our dedicated Data Subject Rights Portal here.
Your personal data will be securely stored in our hosting provider’s data center in Oregon (US west). We have implemented appropriate transfer mechanisms under applicable data protection laws.
Contentsquare may use AI-assisted tools to help review and screen applications. All decisions involving hiring are made by human reviewers, and your personal data will be processed in accordance with our Candidate Privacy Policy.

Job Summary

Community Resource Worker - Outreach plays an important role in supporting individuals to live as independently as possible in their homes and community. This position involves assessment and goal planning, provides skill-building support, promotes safety and well-being, and works closely with clients, families, and other professionals to ensure high-quality, person-centered care.


Key Responsibilities

Program Planning & Support

  • Participate in assessment, goal setting, and development of Individual Service Plans.
  • Document, implement, and provide input into program evaluations.
  • Assist with case management by identifying potential problems and reporting difficulties.
  • Contribute to the evaluation of participants’ progress and prepare accurate reports.

Daily Living & Community Skill Support

  • Support participants to increase independence in their homes and communities.
  • Assist with daily living skills, social development, and behavior management strategies.
  • Provide life skills training such as meal preparation, housekeeping, personal care skills, and personal finance.
  • Assist with activities of daily living, including feeding, lifts, transfers, hygiene, grooming, and toileting.
  • Perform specialized care tasks as required (e.g., gastrostomy feeding, tracheostomy management, suction, and bowel management).
  • Teach and assist with activities such as grooming, basic cooking, money management, shopping, household safety, and pet care.
  • Facilitate physical, recreational, educational, social, and vocational activities.

Health & Safety

  • Respond promptly to emergencies, including situations involving potential aggression, ensuring safety for all.
  • Report concerns the supervisor as required.
  • Administer medications in accordance with organizational policies
  • Ensure proper infection control and sanitation practices in all environments.
  • Maintain high standards of health and safety in all environments.

Monitoring & Communication

  • Review and evaluate participants’ progress and adjust programs as needed.
  • Provide ongoing support and constructive feedback to participants and families.
  • Accompany or transport clients to appointments, shopping trips, and leisure activities.
  • Prepare accurate written and verbal reports detailing daily activities, progress, and required documentation.

Community Connections & Transportation

  • Identify community resources that meet participants’ social, recreational, physical, vocational, and educational needs.
  • Advocate for participants by liaising with community agencies and professionals to access necessary resources.
  • Maintain positive relationships with other agencies, professionals, government representatives, and community members.
  • Accompany or transport clients to appointments, shopping trips, and leisure activities; operate vehicles safely and responsibly.

Household Maintenance

  • Perform housekeeping and maintenance duties in supportive living environments, including laundry, sweeping, mopping, lawn care, inventory, shopping, and cleaning equipment.

Other

  • Perform other related duties as required.

Education & Experience

  • Certificate in a related human or social services field.
  • One (1) year of recent related experience, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience.


Requirements

  1. Class 5 Driver’s License (may be required to obtain Class 4).
  2. Current First Aid and CPR certification.
  3. Current (every 3 years) TB test results
  4. Clear and current Criminal Record Check (completed through OneSky).

title: Benefits Coach
description:
*Applicants who apply through third-party sites (Indeed, LinkedIn, etc.) will receive an email from isolved to complete their application.*

SUMMARY

The Benefits Coach works with clients by assisting them to identify and access all applicable public benefits, including but not limited to Temporary Assistance for Needy Families (TANF), Food Stamps, Medicaid, and Colorado Childcare Assistance Program (CCAP). This position works directly with clients, assisting them to maintain ongoing benefit eligibility and program compliance. Coach and provide support to clients so that they have the knowledge and resources to navigate public benefits systems on their own while empowering them to become self-sufficient.

ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES

• Understands and stays current on the eligibility criteria and outcome requirements for all public benefits programs, as well as within the Colorado Refugee Services Program (CRSP) and Employment & Benefits Division (EBD).
• Using a strengths-based and client-let coaching approach, helps clients to develop goals and action steps to be used in their Roadmaps, with the aim of achieving stability and independence.
• Works with other LFS staff members to complete client benefit applications, redeterminations, and interviews as required by county human services offices. Receives, reviews and submits required client documents to applicable county human services offices.
• Enters Roadmaps and work participation hours into Colorado Benefits Management System (CBMS).
• Review request for transportation, and other county approved supportive services and enter into CBMS to ensure a continual path towards self-sufficiency.
• Communicates with county and State Human Services staff to ensure clients receive timely public benefits. Advocates for clients when needed.
• Schedules and conducts benefit orientations for new participants to ensure state and federal compliance.
• Provides ongoing training to Lutheran Family Services Rocky Mountains (LFSRM) staff as needed pertaining to public benefit rules and regulations.
• Serves as an advocate and resource for clients and provide equal treatment to all client groups in accordance with the agency's commitment to the dignity of all persons.
• Coordinates services with other key staff to assure comprehensive services to clients.
• Attends and participates in staff meetings and other meetings as requested.
• Abides by high quality of standards of case management and adheres to service delivery expectations of LFSRM, State of Colorado, Department of Health and Human Services - Office of Refugee Resettlement and Department of State.
• Complies with all federal, state and LFSRM contracts.
• Participates in community outreach activities that advance the work and message of the Refugee & Asylee Programs.
• Provides leadership in conceptualizing new program possibilities and suggesting improvements in existing programs and practices.
• Ensures that program services are provided in accordance with quality assurance standards of the agency, state, accrediting organizations and HIPAA.
• Performs other duties as assigned.

QUALIFICATIONS

To perform this job successfully, an individual must be able to perform each essential duty satisfactorily. The requirements listed below are representative of the knowledge, skill, and/or ability required. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.
• Outstanding organizational ability.
• Written communication skills, ability to edit and make presentations.
• Cross cultural sensitivity and knowledge with the ability and desire to work with people of other cultures.
• Computer skills in Microsoft applications, including Word, Excel, and Outlook.
• Detail oriented, extensive documentation skills, organized and able to work in a multi-tasked environment.
• Maintains punctuality for work, appointments and report dates.
• Functional fluency in one or more foreign languages preferred.
• Skills in problem solving, negotiations, decision-making and mediating conflict.
• Ability to self-start and work well in a team setting. Proven team-builder.
• Must have and maintain a valid driver's license and provide proof of auto liability insurance at the level of 100,000/300,000/100,000.
• Demonstrates commitment to the mission, values, and vision of Lutheran Family Services Rocky Mountains.


EDUCATION and/or EXPERIENCE

Bachelor's degree from a four-year college or university, OR two + years related experience AND/OR training; OR equivalent combination of education and experience.


SUPERVISORY RESPONSIBILITIES

This position has no supervisory responsibilities.

All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, or status as a protected veteran.

title: AI/ML Engineer
description:
Why Join 7-Eleven Global Solution Center?

When you join us, you'll embrace ownership as teams within specific product areas take responsibility for end-to-end solution delivery, supporting local teams and integrating new digital assets. Challenge yourself by contributing to products deployed across our extensive network of convenience stores, processing over a billion transactions annually.


Build solutions for scale, addressing the diverse needs of our 84,000+ stores in 19 countries. Experience growth through cross-functional learning, encouraged and applauded at 7-Eleven GSC. With our size, stability, and resources, you can navigate a rewarding career. Embody leadership and service as 7-Eleven GSC remains dedicated to meeting the needs of customers and communities.

Why We Exist, Our Purpose and Our Transformation?

7-Eleven is dedicated to being a customer-centric, digitally empowered organization that seamlessly integrates our physical stores with digital offerings. Our goal is to redefine convenience by consistently providing top-notch customer experiences and solutions in a rapidly evolving consumer landscape. Anticipating customer preferences, we create and implement platforms that empower customers to shop, pay, and access products and services according to their preferences. To achieve success, we are driving a cultural shift anchored in leadership principles, supported by the realignment of organizational resources and processes.

At 7-Eleven we are guided by our Leadership Principles. Each principle has a defined set of behaviours which help guide the 7-Eleven GSC team to Serve Customers and Support Stores.

- Be Customer Obsessed

- Be Courageous with Your Point of View

- Challenge the Status Quo

- Act Like an Entrepreneur

- Have an "It Can Be Done" Attitude

- Do the Right Thing

- Be Accountable

About This Opportunity :

Responsibilities :

Join our Analytics, Data Strategy, and AI team and help engineer the next generation of our digital capabilities. We are looking for a hands-on, highly motivated problem solver to play a pivotal role in scaling our proprietary agentic AI initiatives.

This is a role for a true builder with a strong systems-thinking mindset. We need someone who is endlessly curious, excels at rapidly mastering new technologies, and understands how individual AI components interact within our broader technical architecture. Rather than simply tuning existing models, you will actively expand our AI's cognitive capabilities, integrate new frameworks on the fly, and deliver measurable business value. If you have a passion for taking an idea from the whiteboard to production and building robust, reusable solutions that elevate the entire ecosystem, this is where you belong.

Educational & Required Qualifications :

- 5 - 7 years of hands-on experience in AI/ML engineering, including Machine Learning, Deep Learning, statistical modeling, and data modeling on large-scale datasets.

- Strong experience in Generative AI, Large Language Models (LLMs), and Agentic AI, including building AI agents and production-grade AI applications.

- Proficiency in ML model development using Python, TensorFlow, PyTorch, and related ML libraries.

- Experience with Agentic AI platforms such as Glean and Agent Bricks, and orchestration frameworks such as LangChain.

- Experience with LLM evaluation, observability, and monitoring tools such as Langfuse and LangSmith.

- Strong programming and API development skills using Python, FastAPI, and SQL.

- Experience working with databases and large-scale data technologies such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, and Spark SQL.

- Strong understanding of data structures, design patterns, automation, and software engineering best practices.

- Experience with real-time/streaming technologies such as Kafka and Amazon Kinesis.

- Hands-on experience in developing, deploying, and productionizing AI/ML applications using Docker and Kubernetes.

- Familiarity with Git-based version control, preferably Azure Git/Azure DevOps.

- Proven experience in leading AI/ML projects end-to-end, from business requirements and solution design through development, deployment, and production support.

- Ability to translate business requirements into scalable technical and AI/ML solutions.

- Experience leading and mentoring team members, along with strong written and verbal communication skills.

- Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Data Science, or an equivalent discipline.

- Retail industry experience is a strong plus.

7-Eleven Global Solution Center is an Equal Opportunity Employer committed to diversity in the workplace. Our strategy focuses on three core pillars - workplace culture, diverse talent and how we show up in the communities we serve. title: Merchandise Manager, Bike
description:
Adventure is our Culture. Join a team that celebrates a lifestyle as bold as the terrain we love. At Backcountry, we are rooted in adventure, recognition, and wellbeing on and off the mountain. We spotlight employee stories, celebrate milestones, and offer exclusive outdoor perks. Whether you are at HQ, in a retail store, or remote, you will be part of a team that thrives on energy, exploration, and connection.

Reports to: Brett Sullivan, VP Merchandising Hardgoods

Location: Remote, USA (Mountain or Pacific Time Zone preferred)

About the Role:

Backcountry's Bike category spans complete bikes, frames, and a deep components assortment across five banners — Bike Tires Direct, Backcountry, Competitive Cyclist, Steep & Cheap, and Marketplace. This role exists to drive the merchandising strategy and financial performance of the entire category, ensuring differentiated assortments and technically sound product for each banner's customer.

As Merchandise Manager, Bike, you will own the open-to-buy budget, vendor relationships, and day-to-day buying decisions while mentoring a team of buyers and junior merchants. Success in the first 6–12 months means establishing strong vendor partnerships that deliver margin improvement, tightening assortment accuracy across banners, and building the cadence and KPI framework your team runs on.

This is a lean team. You will own a lot, move fast, and make decisions with full end-to-end responsibility.

What You'll Do:

Category Management

  • Execute the merchandising and sourcing plan across complete bikes, frames, and components (drivetrains, wheels, brakes, suspension, cockpit, pedals) for each banner
  • Drive sales, margin, and inventory turn goals across all channels and platforms
  • Manage the open-to-buy budget for Bike across Bike Tires Direct, Backcountry, Competitive Cyclist, Steep & Cheap, and Marketplace
  • Source and assess merchandise by evaluating market trends, cross-component and build-kit compatibility, and historical selling data

Vendor Management & Differentiation

  • Build and maintain relationships with bike brands and component manufacturers, negotiating pricing, terms, key buys, and promotional windows to maximize gross margin
  • Identify, evaluate, and onboard new vendors to strengthen the supply chain and assortment
  • Establish and enforce quality standards through supplier collaboration and regular product quality checks

Inventory & Analytics

  • Own SKU/PO worksheets and purchase orders — quantity, dollar, style allocation, size/color breakout — under tight deadlines
  • Manage inventory flow by setting receipt plans, sell-through targets, and re-order or reduction edits; partner with Planning on exit strategies for slow movers
  • Leverage sales data, customer insights, and analytics to forecast demand and refine procurement plans
  • Monitor category KPIs, evaluate vendor performance, and recommend actions to hit profitability targets

Customer Experience & Cross-Functional Partnerships

  • Apply deep technical knowledge of bike systems to ensure assortment compatibility, spec accuracy, and informed support for vendors, planning, and customer-facing teams
  • Uphold category content standards, visual merchandising, and taxonomy to improve conversion
  • Partner with Planning on budgets, forecasting, and KPI reporting; collaborate with Marketing and Creative on promotions, campaigns, and selling strategy

Team Leadership

  • Guide and mentor the Bike buying team, supporting buyer development and fostering a collaborative work environment

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree (Business, Supply Chain Management, or related field preferred)
  • 10+ years in retail buying or merchandising with a proven track record in strategic sourcing, vendor management, and e-commerce
  • Hands-on technical knowledge of bikes, frames, and components — drivetrains, groupsets, brake systems, wheel/tire standards, suspension, cockpit/contact points, frame geometry and materials — with the ability to evaluate cross-component and build-kit compatibility
  • Deep understanding of the cycling and outdoor retail market, customer preferences, and industry dynamics
  • Proven experience in inventory management, demand forecasting, and procurement optimization
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with demonstrated negotiation ability
  • Firm understanding of retail math and merchandising fundamentals
  • Excellent organizational skills with strong attention to detail and time management
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills; strong collaborator across functions
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office with advanced Excel skills; experience with purchasing software and systems
  • Working knowledge of AI tools and their practical application in merchandising workflows (e.g., demand forecasting, assortment planning, trend analysis)
  • Genuine passion for cycling and the products Backcountry offers
  • Willingness and ability to travel as needed

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Direct experience in the bike industry, including relationships with major bike and component brands
  • Experience managing or mentoring a buying team
  • Familiarity with marketplace merchandising alongside owned-inventory channels

Why Join:

The people who do best here are builders. They take ownership, move fast, and want to see the direct impact of their work.

  • Team Impact: Build and lead a buying team with direct ownership of their outcomes, shaping how Backcountry shows up in one of its most important categories.
  • Growth & Leadership Development: Sharpen your craft as a people leader while getting hands-on with AI-driven merchandising tools — from demand forecasting to assortment planning — building skills that set you apart.
  • Category Ownership: Own end-to-end financial and assortment performance across five banners, with the autonomy to make vendor, pricing, and strategy decisions that directly move the business.
  • Competitive Benefits: Paid time off policies, 401(k) match, medical/dental/vision and a variety of supplemental policies, and employee discounts across our portfolio of brands.

Interview Process:

  1. Recruiter Screen - A 45-minute conversation with our recruiting team to align on the role, your background, and what you are looking for.
  2. Hiring Manager Interview - Conversation with the VP, Merchandising Hardgoods focused on your merchandising experience, vendor management approach, and technical bike knowledge.
  3. Take-Home Assignment - A short challenge so we can understand how you approach problems and execution.
  4. Panel Interview - Deep-dive interviews with Backcountry leadership focused on your experience, product mindset, and operational thinking.
  5. In-Person Interview - We'd like to meet you at our Cottonwood Heights office. Details and logistics will be arranged with your recruiter.
  6. Reference Checks - Conducted in parallel with the final stages where possible.
  7. Offer - We move quickly for the right candidate.

Interview process is subject to change. Any updates will be communicated promptly and clearly.

Please Note:

  • Part of our interview process is a mandatory in-person interview with someone on our team prior to an offer. Candidates that are unwilling or unable to meet for an in-person interview will be removed from consideration immediately.

CSC Generation is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to any characteristic protected by law. If you need an accommodation during the application process, contact hrbenefits@cscshared.com.

Employment is contingent on a background check, including verification of prior employment dates.

title: Apprentice 1st Step - Journeyman Lineman
description:
Job Title: Apprentice 1st Step - Journeyman Lineman

PS Job Title: Apprentice 1st step - Journeyman Lineman

Work Place Flexibility: Onsite

Legal Entity: Entergy Texas, Inc.-GTX

APPRENTICE 1ST STEP

A. JOB QUALIFICATIONS:

Under Class 1 supervision, as an apprentice in training, must be able to perform the less difficult tasks and assist others in high and low voltage line work involved in the construction and maintenance of electric transmission and distribution conductors, structures, underground systems, and related equipment, and be qualified to do the following and related work as assigned:

  1. Use pole climbing equipment and have ability to handle self on pole in safe and efficient manner.
  2. Handle poles, install poles, and assist in the erection of steel, wood and other structures, including foundations.
  3. Make up and install guys and install secondaries.
  4. Connect services on energized conductors up to 600 volts.
  5. Install secondary racks and clevis, anchors, miscellaneous hardware, grounds, fittings for vertical type construction, buss supports, and conductors on dead circuits.
  6. Perform simple transmission and distribution switching (qualified lineman assistance).
  7. Tie knots and splice rope.
  8. Assist in trimming trees.
  9. Assist qualified lineman or servicemen in simple routine inspection and maintenance.
  10. Assist in the installation of all types of conduit systems.
  11. Assist in the handling, moving and installation of all transmission, distribution and plant equipment, machinery, etc.
  12. Prepare reports and records.
  13. Read and understand job drawings and maps and assist with Job Hazard Assessment.
  14. Operate Company’s equipment.
  15. Become familiar with new technology such as computers and tablets required to perform work.
  16. Follow the Safety Action Plan “SAP” expectations according to minimum required qualifications. (Rev 03 dated 7/15/2023) If the SAP is to be revised the Company will notify the Union of any proposed changes prior to the effective date of the change, and upon request by the Union, meet and negotiate any change.

B. EXPERIENCE AND SPECIAL QUALIFICATIONS:

An Apprentice Lineman during the first three months in classification shall not work on circuits or equipment energized at more than 600 volts. They shall not be permitted to climb through or above ungrounded conductors or equipment rated at more than 600 volts even though such conductors are properly covered or spaced out of casual reach. This includes all transmission conductors.

1. During the second three months apprenticeship, the apprentice may be allowed to perform structure

inspections provided the following conditions are met:

a) Energized primary circuits shall be properly covered, and shall not be within casual reach.

b) Energized transmission circuits must have a phase spacing no less than fifteen feet.

c) Inspection does not require apprentice to cross from one pole in structure to another.

d) Structure maintenance is not required

2. During the last six months of apprenticeship, the apprentice is allowed to assist a qualified lineman incovering and working all voltages. The qualified lineman shall be on the pole, structure, work board, or in an aerial basket participating in the work if the voltage is above 600 volts. The apprentice may also be allowed to climb through or above properly covered primary distribution circuits for the purpose of structure inspections to assist a qualified lineman in hot stick work. The apprentice may be allowed to climb by or above energized transmission circuits for the purpose of structure inspections. The apprentice may also be allowed to assist a qualified lineman in doing such tasks as pole wrapping, static replacement, etc.

Note: Regardless of what step the apprentice may be in their classification, any assignment must first be discussed, and both the apprentice and their Supervisor must be confident that it can be done safely. Line and equipment must be grounded to be considered de-energized.

3. Work towards the completion of 200, 300 and 400 level certification or accredited Lineman Trade certification.

4. Learn Company’s safety rules, and be able to administer all approved methods of resuscitation, and be able to render practical first aid.

5. Know the location of, and be able to operate, all the firefighting equipment. Know what kind of equipment to use on electrical, oil, and other fires.

6. Maintain a valid Class A Commercial Driver’s License

7. Have knowledge of line and substation material and use of line construction tools and equipment

C. PHYSICAL QUALIFICATIONS:

1. Must have full use of mental and physical faculties.

2. Have strength and endurance adequate for arduous labor in all kinds of outdoor weather conditions.

3. Be able to work at heights and close spaces

4. Good hand-eye coordination and physical dexterity.

D. PERSONAL QUALIFICATIONS:

1. Be particularly alert in observing hazards and avoiding accidents.

2. Be willing to work under unusual surroundings, as well as the normal working conditions pertaining to this job.

3. Be able to receive and transmit orders and instructions in such a manner as to inspire respect and confidence of both superiors and subordinates

APPRENTICE 2ND STEP

A. JOB QUALIFICATIONS:

Under Class 1 supervision, must be able to perform the less complicated tasks and assist in the installation and removal of electric meters, services and related equipment on customers' premises, connect and disconnect service at the pole, locate and repair all types of breaks in the electric transmission and distribution system, answer electric trouble calls to customers' premises, and be able to perform the less complicated tasks on high and low voltage line work involved in the construction and maintenance of electric transmission and distribution conductors, structures and equipment, and be qualified to do the following and related work as assigned:

  1. Have equivalent experience in related work, having all the qualifications of Apprentice 1st Step.
  2. Install crossarms, secondary racks and clevis, anchors and guys, and install hardware and fittings for vertical type construction, including conductors, single phase transformers, lightning arresters, grounds, cutouts, etc., on dead circuits.
  3. Trim trees.
  4. Refuse transformers and circuit breakers and check grounds.
  5. Inspect meters and meter loops for irregularities.
  6. Prepare records and reports.
  7. Check customer's wiring for accidental ground.
  8. Check installation for proper secondary ground.
  9. Operate Company's trucks and automobiles.
  10. Assist qualified serviceman, lineman, or others in working on energized conductors up to 34.5kV.
  11. Handle and work from ladders.
  12. Assist in the installation, maintenance and repair of street lighting equipment and fixtures.
  13. Read meters, install and remove secondary meters and services.
  14. Make secondary load and voltage checks, setting of recording meters and change charts.
  15. Under Class 1 supervision may be allowed to cover and work energized circuits when they and their supervisor are confident that this can be done safely.
  16. Direct work of helpers when authorized.
  17. Follow Safety Action Plan “SAP” expectations according to minimum required qualifications. (Rev 03 dated 7/15/2023) If the SAP is to be revised the Company will notify the Union of any proposed changes prior to the effective date of the change, and upon request by the Union, meet and negotiate any change.

EXPERIENCE AND SPECIAL QUALIFICATIONS:

  1. Must have worked and qualified, as an Apprentice 1st Step or have had equivalent experience in related work, having all the qualifications of the previous classifications.
  2. Completion of 400 level certification.
  3. Know Company’s safety rules, and be able to administer all approved methods of resuscitation, and be able to render practical first aid.
  4. Know the location of and be able to operate all of the firefighting equipment. Know what kind of equipment to use on electrical, oil and other fires.
  5. Obtain/maintain a valid Class A Commercial Driver’s License
  6. Know city streets, and roads in rural sections.
  7. Know Company’s electrical and mechanical tagging rules.
  8. Have working knowledge of Company’s practices and standards.
  9. Have a working knowledge of technology needed to perform job such as computers and current computer applications.
  10. Have general knowledge of electric circuits and equipment.
  11. Be familiar with Company's rules and regulations applying to service and meter installations, Underwriters' National Electrical Code and any state or local regulations governing electrical wiring as pertains to service and meter installations.
  12. Be able to read and understand simple wiring diagrams and blueprints.
  13. Know Company's electrical and mechanical tagging rules.
  14. Accurately identify and record all changes to Company equipment according to Company requirements.
  15. Have thorough knowledge of city and state traffic laws.
  16. Have a thorough knowledge of Company regulations and state laws governing disconnects for nonpayment, and diversion of current.

PHYSICAL QUALIFICATIONS:

  1. Must have full use of mental and physical faculties.
  2. Have strength and endurance adequate for arduous labor in all kinds of outdoor weather conditions.
  3. Be able to work at heights and close spaces.
  4. Good hand-eye coordination and physical dexterity.

PERSONAL QUALIFICATIONS:

  1. Possess all personal qualifications as an Apprentice 1st Step
  2. Be particularly alert in observing hazards and avoiding accidents.
  3. Be willing to work under unusual surroundings, as well as the normal working conditions pertaining to this job.
  4. Be able to receive and transmit orders and instructions in such a manner as to inspire respect and confidence of both superiors and subordinates

APPRENTICE 3RD STEP

A. JOB QUALIFICATIONS:

Under Class 1 and/or 2 supervision, with some latitude for planning or laying out of working details, must be able to perform tasks of average difficulty involved in the installation and removal of electric meters, services and related equipment on customer's premises, connect and disconnect service at the pole, locate and repair all types of breaks in the electric transmission and distribution system, answer electric trouble calls to customer's premises, and be qualified to do related work as assigned and following prescribed routine and instructions as to methods and working details of average difficulty and importance, must be able to perform the less complicated tasks on high and low voltage line work involved in the construction and maintenance of electric transmission and distribution conductors, structures and equipment, and be qualified to do the following and related work as assigned :

  1. Have equivalent experience in related work, having all the qualifications of Apprentice 2nd Step.
  2. Use hot line tools.
  3. May be allowed to cover and work energized circuits when they and their supervisor are confident that this can be done safely.
  4. Fuse transformers and sectionalizing fuses.
  5. Locate trouble and restore service on all classes of lines, substations, sectionalizing equipment, reclosers, etc.
  6. Check, handle and be responsible for all material removed from and returned to stock and prepare reports and records.
  7. String, sag and tie in conductors on dead lines of all classes.
  8. Install all types of transformer installations, make tap changes and install primary metering equipment.
  9. Install, maintain, and repair street lighting equipment and fixtures.
  10. Assist in making aerial and submarine cable installations, including the making of joints and installing potheads.
  11. Assist in the installation of pole type regulators and transformers to boost or buck line voltage.
  12. Assist in phasing and checking rotation in circuits direct and with potential transformers.
  13. Assist in erecting and maintaining steel towers and outdoor substations.
  14. Assist in receiving blocks.
  15. Work energized conductors on simple structures, up to and including 35.4kV.
  16. Run services, install and remove all types of secondary meters and related equipment.
  17. Replace fuse links in outdoor type cutouts, and transformers.

title: IT Security Specialist
description:
Job Summary:

Step2 is looking for a security leader who thinks big picture and is also an expert at the keyboard. You will set security strategy, stay ahead of fast-changing threats (especially new attack methods and vulnerabilities that come with AI), and do the hands-on work to protect our users, systems, data and sites. You will own our security program end to end: strategy, tools, vendors, training and incident response. We want someone excited by the challenge of protecting Step2 as AI makes attacks faster, cheaper and harder to spot: someone who questions whether yesterday's tools still fit, learns fast, and designs new defenses where needed. This is not a role for someone looking to re-implement a familiar legacy stack.

Job Duties:

  • Strategy and threat intelligence: Track emerging threats, including AI-enabled phishing, deepfake and social-engineering attacks, prompt injection, data leakage through AI tools, and vulnerabilities in AI agents and integrations. Turn that into a security and business continuity strategy, with a tactical roadmap that stays current, and brief leadership on risk. The goal: no malware or device loss can take Step2 down.
  • AI security: Set guardrails for how employees and systems use AI tools, agents and MCP connections. Review new AI tools and vendors for data exposure and access risk.
  • Incident response and risk: Own the incident response plan, playbooks and courses of action. Run tabletop exercises, lead response when incidents happen, and maintain a risk register with mitigation plans.
  • Business continuity: Build and test the continuity plan so malware, ransomware or device loss cannot stop the business. Includes fast device rebuilds, recovery of OneDrive and Microsoft 365 data (versioning, retention and backup), and regular recovery drills.
  • Hands-on security operations: Set and verify security controls: MFA, conditional access and privileged accounts in Entra ID; Microsoft 365 security settings; vulnerability management; firewall, VPN and segmentation rules, including plant networks; access reviews for employees and contractors. The Senior Manager, IT Infrastructure & Operations administers these platforms; this role defines and checks the controls.
  • Endpoint security and disposable devices: Own the security strategy for employee laptops and mobile devices. Treat every device as disposable: work lives in OneDrive and Microsoft 365, so any device can be wiped and replaced without losing data. Run remote scans, keep a live device and software inventory, find installed threats and unapproved software, remove malware, and isolate or wipe compromised devices remotely.
  • Secure development (DevSecOps): Work with the software development team to design and enable CI/CD pipelines that include static (SAST) and dynamic (DAST) code analysis, plus dependency and secrets scanning. Cover industry-standard vulnerability classes such as the OWASP Top 10 and CWE Top 25, and help developers fix findings.
  • Vendors and tools: Select, implement and manage security vendors and monitoring tools (EDR, SIEM/MDR, email security, vulnerability scanning). Manage contracts, performance and budget.
  • Security telemetry and reporting: Consolidate security telemetry and logs into Snowflake for analysis. Build dashboards and alerting (e.g. Grafana) that show risk, trends and program performance.
  • Third-party risk: Evaluate existing, proposed and new vendors against Step2's security compliance thresholds before and after onboarding. Apply the right access controls to each vendor (least privilege, time-limited access, MFA) and reassess them on a regular schedule.
  • Policy and compliance: Keep security policies and standards current. Support audits, cyber insurance requirements and customer or retailer security questionnaires.
  • Security awareness program: Take over and run our KnowBe4 employee training and phishing simulation program. Measure results, tailor content to our real threats and roles, and recommend how the program should evolve.
  • Physical site security: Own building access control (badges, door systems, visitor access), security monitoring and CCTV across Step2 sites. Manage the related systems and vendors, review access rights, and bring physical security events into incident response and telemetry.

Basic Qualification Requirements:

  • A forward-looking mindset: you can show how you have adapted defenses to new threats, and you evaluate modern and AI-driven security tools on their merits rather than defaulting to what you used before.
  • 7+ years in IT security, with both strategic and hands-on technical responsibility.
  • Proven record of taking initiative: building or substantially improving a security program, not just maintaining one.
  • Current knowledge of AI-related threats and controls, and a habit of keeping up with the threat landscape.
  • Deep hands-on skill with Microsoft 365 security, Entra ID, EDR, SIEM or log tools, vulnerability scanning, firewalls and VPN.
  • Comprehensive experience with modern endpoint security strategy and management (e.g. Microsoft Intune and Defender for Endpoint): remote scanning, device and software inventory, threat and malware detection and removal, remote isolation and wipe. This is security-focused endpoint work, not general infrastructure.
  • Experience running a security operations center (SOC), either internal or outsourced (MSSP/MDR), including setting escalation rules, SLAs and performance reviews. Experience selecting and managing security vendors.
  • Experience writing and running incident response plans and tabletop exercises.
  • Experience building and testing business continuity and ransomware recovery plans.
  • Experience running a security awareness program (KnowBe4 or similar).
  • Working knowledge of a security framework such as NIST CSF or CIS Controls.
  • Clear communicator who can explain risk to leadership and train non-technical staff.
  • Certifications preferred: CISSP, CISM, Security+, CySA+, or Microsoft SC-200/SC-300.

Additional Qualifications:

  • Experience securing manufacturing or OT/plant networks.
  • SQL and scripting (PowerShell, Python) to automate checks and analyze telemetry; Snowflake or Grafana experience.
  • Experience with Oracle E-Business Suite or Snowflake access controls.
  • AI security frameworks such as OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications or NIST AI RMF.

Work Environment/Physical Demand:

Hybrid; based in Streetsboro, OH. Office, plant and warehouse environments, with travel between Step2 sites for physical security and incidents. Standard business hours, with flexibility to be reasonably available and respond quickly to critical outages or incidents that stop business operations, especially during peak selling seasons.

Exempt

  • Premium FREE Medical Plan Option
  • Employee Discount
  • 10 Paid Holidays

We're proud of the culture we've built - one rooted in trust, collaboration, respect, and genuine relationships. Significance, Inc. is seeking a CMS Transportation Program Administrator to support a federal program (contingent upon award). This position requires the ability to obtain and maintain a Public Trust.
This position is open to local candidates only as it requires onsite work five days per week at the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services in Baltimore, MD.

The Transportation Program Administrator is the primary point of contact for CMS employees who use the transportation programs administered by the CMS Office of Security, Facilities, and Logistics Operations (OSFLO) at CMS Headquarters in Baltimore, and delivers high-quality, responsive, and professional customer service across all of them. The role supports four programs: the Transit Subsidy Benefits Program (administered through an Interagency Agreement with the Program Support Center), the CMS Headquarters Parking Program, the Fleet Management Program, and Cargo Traffic Services for freight and household goods. The Representative takes over the high-volume, day-to-day transactions currently handled as secondary duties by the CMS Parking and Transit Program Manager and the CMS Fleet Manager, so those managers can focus on policy, compliance, and strategy.

Responsibilities:

  • Answer employee inquiries by phone, email, and in person about transit subsidy benefits, parking program eligibility and availability, fleet reservations, freight and household-goods services, and other transportation and traffic-related services
  • Intake, evaluate, and process transit subsidy applications (mass transit, vanpool, and Bike2Work), renewals, adjustments, and terminations through the GOVGO! Portal in a timely and accurate manner and in strict compliance with program rules and guidelines
  • Administer CMS Headquarters parking: process new applications, make parking assignments, manage waitlists to ensure equitable distribution, and maintain accurate parking records
  • Coordinate fleet vehicle reservations, track vehicle availability, and maintain up-to-date fleet utilization records
  • Assist with scheduling fleet vehicle maintenance and help ensure vehicles are available and compliant with applicable federal regulations and CMS policies
  • Support Agency traffic management by arranging freight reservations for large shipments (such as IT equipment relocations and trade show materials) and processing household-goods services for Agency-supported employee relocations, using TMSS 2.0 or a similar system
  • Maintain accurate and complete records of all customer interactions and transactions in the applicable program systems
  • Escalate complex or unresolved issues to the Commuter Services and/or Transportation Program Manager(s); raise critical issues immediately so they can be reported to the COR within 24 hours
  • Compile data for the monthly Transit Subsidy, Parking, and Fleet Utilization reports and the Monthly Status Report, including inquiries received, resolved, and pending and transit applications returned for editing
  • Support the quarterly Quality Assurance/Customer Satisfaction Report, the Annual Performance Report, and ad hoc data requests (due within 5 business days)
  • Assist with developing and maintaining customer service standard operating procedures (SOPs) and reference materials
  • Participate in team meetings, training sessions, and quarterly and annual program reviews as directed

Required Skills:

  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in a customer service, administrative support, or transportation-related role
  • Prior experience managing a federal agency contract that provided transportation program support services, including independently processing incoming customer applications in full accordance with program regulations, policies, and procedures
  • Knowledge of federal regulations for transit subsidy programs
  • Experience with intake and evaluation of transit applications through the GOVGO! Portal, ensuring strict compliance with all program rules and guidelines
  • Knowledge of federal traffic management regulations, including acquiring services for the Agency through the Transportation Management Services Solution (TMSS 2.0) or a similar transportation management system
  • Familiarity with federal government transportation programs and policies
  • Experience with parking management systems and fleet management platforms
  • Prior experience supporting a federal agency or government contractor
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite (Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams)
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously in a fast-paced environment
  • Experience with transportation management or fleet management software preferred

Education

  • High school diploma or equivalent required; Associate's or Bachelor's degree preferred

Key Responsibilities:

Talent Acquisition Configuration and Support:
