- Partner with Talent Acquisition, HR, HRIS, IT, and delivery teams to gather requirements, evaluate options, and deliver scalable recruiting and onboarding solutions.

- Support enhancements, incidents, releases, testing, deployment, and production operations.

Employee Central Configuration and Cross-Module Support:

- Configure and support Employee Central foundation and employee data needed for recruiting, onboarding, hire, rehire, position, job, workflow, and downstream processes.

- Configure and troubleshoot Employee Central business rules, workflows, event reasons, hire and rehire logic, position/job data dependencies, propagation rules, and data validation logic supporting recruiting and onboarding processes.

- Analyze and resolve cross-module dependencies, data quality issues, security needs, business rules, and process design gaps.

- Support EC data loads, imports, mass changes, validation, and troubleshooting as needed.

Integrations, Data, Security, and Reporting:

- Support Integration Center interfaces, scheduled jobs, data loads, candidate and new-hire updates, EC data movement, and downstream integrations.

- Analyze XML, template, field mapping, business rule, API, and integration-related issues that impact requisitions, postings, offers, onboarding records, employee data, or downstream systems.

- Troubleshoot interface failures, mapping errors, data quality issues, reporting gaps, and downstream impacts with technical teams and vendors.

- Understand and troubleshoot downstream impacts to Employee Central Payroll, including employee master data, job and compensation data, organizational assignments, time-related data, and payroll-relevant integration dependencies.

- Ensure data integrity, role-based access, privacy, audit readiness, and accurate SuccessFactors reporting.

Business Partnership and Solution Delivery:

- Translate business requirements into functional designs, configuration decisions, test scenarios, deployment plans, and support procedures.

- Lead solution walkthroughs, readiness reviews, and design discussions with HR, Talent Acquisition, HRIS, IT, and business stakeholders.

- Communicate status, risks, dependencies, and decisions while recommending practical process and system improvements.

Testing, Release, and Operational Support:

- Develop test plans and scripts, coordinate SIT/UAT, assess SuccessFactors releases, and track defects through closure.

- Support deployment, cutover, hypercare, incident triage, root-cause analysis, and documented resolution.

- Maintain functional designs, configuration workbooks, test scripts, release notes, user guides, and support documentation.

Required Qualifications:

- 5+ years of hands-on SAP SuccessFactors experience across Recruiting, Onboarding, and Employee Central configuration/support.

- Deep hands-on experience configuring SuccessFactors Recruiting Management and Recruiting Marketing, including XML-based requisition and application templates, job posting templates, offer templates, field permissions, route maps, email templates, and career site configuration.

- Ability to design, configure, test, and troubleshoot business rules across Recruiting, Onboarding, Employee Central, workflows, alerts, notifications, data propagation, validations, and hire/rehire processes.

- Strong working knowledge of Career Site Builder, Recruiting Marketing site maintenance, job search configuration, landing pages, branding components, and candidate experience updates.

- Comfortable reviewing technical configuration details, identifying root cause, documenting changes, coordinating with SAP or implementation partners, and moving updates through development, test, and production environments.

- Strong knowledge of RCM, RMK, ONB 2.0, CSB, JPB, EC foundation objects, employee data, workflows, business rules, imports, and role-based permissions.

- Understanding of Recruiting-to-Onboarding-to-EC data flow, hire/rehire processes, cross-module dependencies, and downstream impacts.

- Experience with Integration Center, data imports, scheduled jobs, integration monitoring, troubleshooting, testing, releases, and production support.

- Working knowledge of Employee Central Payroll touchpoints and ability to assess how EC, recruiting, onboarding, business rule, template, or integration changes may affect payroll processing, replication, validation, and downstream controls.

- Strong communication, facilitation, analytical, troubleshooting, documentation, and stakeholder-management skills.

Preferred Qualifications:

- SAP SuccessFactors certification in Recruiting, Onboarding, and/or Employee Central.

- Knowledge of People Analytics, Story Reports, release management, change control, data privacy, audit support, and Agile delivery.

- Experience supporting global recruiting, onboarding, and Employee Central processes in a GCC, shared services, or global support model.

- Good-to-have experience with SmartRecruiters integration, data migration, recruiting process alignment, or future coexistence with SuccessFactors Recruiting.

Success Measures:

- Reliable delivery of Talent Acquisition and Employee Central enhancements, releases, integrations, and production support.

- Stable data flow from recruiting and onboarding into Employee Central and connected systems.

- Improved stakeholder communication, documentation, data integrity, security, user experience, and operational readiness.

title: SAP Oil & Gas Functional Business Analyst
description:
Role Overview :

8 - 12 years of overall SAP functional experience, with a minimum of 5 years focused on SAP Oil & Gas (IS-Oil and/or S/4HANA for Oil & Gas).

We are seeking an experienced SAP Oil & Gas Functional Business Analyst to act as the functional bridge between the business, SAP delivery teams and our UiPath Test Automation Engineers.

The successful candidate will bring deep knowledge of SAP Oil & Gas (IS-Oil / S/4HANA for Oil & Gas) processes and will translate complex industry workflows into clear, testable scenarios that automation engineers can build, execute and maintain with confidence.

This role is central to the success of our test automation programme.

You will ensure that automation engineers understand not just what to automate, but why each business process works the way it does, how SAP modules interact, and where integration points create risk.

Your guidance will directly shape the coverage, accuracy and resilience of the automated regression suite.

Key Responsibilities :


Functional Knowledge Transfer & Enablement :

- Act as the primary functional subject matter expert for SAP Oil & Gas processes, guiding UiPath Test Automation Engineers through module functionality, transactions, master data and business rules.

- Conduct structured walkthroughs, demos and knowledge-transfer sessions on end-to-end Oil & Gas business workflows, explaining process intent, dependencies and expected system behaviour.

- Prepare and maintain functional documentation (process flows, business process maps, data dependency matrices and transaction guides) tailored for an automation audience.

- Respond to day-to-day functional queries from the automation team and resolve ambiguity quickly to keep automation development on schedule.

Test Scenario Design & Automation Support :

- Analyse business requirements, functional specifications and process designs to identify critical test scenarios across business-as-usual, exception and edge cases.

- Define and document detailed test scenarios, test cases, preconditions, test data requirements and expected results in a format suitable for automation.

- Partner with automation engineers to prioritise processes for automation based on business criticality, transaction volume, change frequency and regression risk.

- Review automated test cases and UiPath workflows for functional accuracy, ensuring they validate the right business outcomes, postings and document flows.

- Identify and help prepare reusable, stable test data sets (materials, customers, vendors, contracts, plants, storage locations, pricing conditions) and advise on data refresh and dependency strategies.

- Support defect triage by distinguishing automation script failures from genuine functional defects, and liaise with SAP functional and development teams to resolve issues.

Integration & End-to-End Process Coverage :

- Map and explain integration points between SAP Oil & Gas and core SAP modules (SD, MM, FI/CO, PM, QM, PP, EWM) as well as external systems such as terminal automation, SCADA, hydrocarbon accounting, pricing and third-party logistics platforms.

- Design end-to-end test scenarios that span multiple modules and interfaces (IDocs, BAPIs, RFCs, APIs, middleware such as SAP PI/PO or SAP Integration Suite), validating data flow and reconciliation across systems.

- Ensure automated regression packs adequately cover high-risk integration touchpoints, financial postings and month-end processes.

Stakeholder Collaboration & Governance :

- Work with Business Process Owners and key users to validate test scenarios and obtain sign-off on functional coverage.

- Assess the impact of SAP releases, support packs, enhancements and change requests on existing automated test suites, and advise on required updates.

- Promote best practices in requirement traceability, linking business requirements to test cases and automation coverage within the test management tool.

Required Functional Expertise : SAP OIL & GAS :

Strong hands-on knowledge across several of the following SAP Oil & Gas areas is required:

Downstream :

- HPM : Hydrocarbon Product Management (HPM), covering dual units of measure, temperature and density conversions, quantity conversion logic.

- Transportation & Distribution (TD) : Bulk transport planning, shipment scheduling, load confirmation and delivery confirmation processes.

- Trader's & Scheduler's Workbench (TSW) : Stock projection, nominations, bulk scheduling and ticketing.

- Exchanges : Exchange agreements, borrow/loan, netting and exchange settlement.

- Pricing : Formula-based and quotation-based pricing, marketing pricing and price determination.

- Inventory & Excise : Tank and silo management, physical inventory, gain/loss handling and excise duty processes.

- Retail & Secondary Distribution : Service Station Retailing (SSR) and Secondary Distribution (SAP OGSD), where applicable.

Upstream (desirable) :

- Joint Venture Accounting (JVA), including cost allocation, cutback and partner billing.

- Production and Revenue Accounting (PRA) and/or Upstream Operations Management (UOM).

Core SAP Integration :

- Sound understanding of Order-to-Cash, Procure-to-Pay, Plan-to-Produce and Record-to-Report processes as they apply to Oil & Gas.

- Working knowledge of how Oil & Gas transactions drive financial postings and controlling objects in FI/CO.

Required Skills & Experience :


- Experience : 8 - 12 years of overall SAP functional experience, with a minimum of 5 years focused on SAP Oil & Gas (IS-Oil and/or S/4HANA for Oil & Gas).

- Delivery : At least 2 full-lifecycle SAP implementations, rollouts or large support engagements within the Oil & Gas industry.

- Testing : Proven experience supporting testing activities (SIT, UAT and regression testing), including test scenario design and test data preparation.

- Automation : Experience working with test automation teams; exposure to UiPath Test Suite (Studio, Test Manager, Orchestrator) or comparable tools (Tricentis Tosca, Worksoft, SAP CBTA) is strongly preferred.

- Communication : Ability to explain complex business processes clearly to technical audiences who may not have an SAP or Oil & Gas background.

- Analytical : Strong analytical, documentation and problem-solving skills with keen attention to detail.

- Tools : Familiarity with SAP Solution Manager, SAP Cloud ALM, Jira, Azure DevOps or similar tools for requirements and defect management.

- Methodology : Experience working within Agile/Scrum and hybrid delivery models.

Preferred Qualifications :

- Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Information Technology, Business Administration or a related field; an MBA is an advantage.

- SAP certification in a relevant functional area (SD, MM, FI/CO) or SAP Oil & Gas.

- Understanding of RPA concepts and automation design principles such as modular, reusable and data-driven test design.

Key Competencies :

- Business process thinking with an end-to-end view of Oil & Gas value chains.

- Collaborative, coaching-oriented approach to working with technical teams.

- Ownership, accountability and the ability to work independently with minimal supervision.

- Clear, structured written and verbal communication with stakeholders at all levels.

- Adaptability in fast-paced, multi-vendor and geographically distributed environments.

title: Lead AI Specialist - Machine Learning
description:
Job Description :

This position will lead the technical design, deployment, and operational management of QAD's Finance AI agents. The role bridges finance operations, data engineering, and AI systems to build secure, high-performing, and auditable agent-assisted workflows that optimize finance processes.

Core Responsibilities :

1. Data Foundation & Semantic Layer :

- Define and own the context tables (business glossary, entity definitions, metric hierarchies) that ground AI agents in QAD's financial reality.

- Build and maintain the semantic layer - the translation between raw Google Cloud BigQuery datasets and the financial concepts agents reason over.

- Partner with the data engineering team and other functions on dbt model governance and Fivetran pipeline integrity.

2. Agent Architecture & Process Design :

- Determine the build methodology for process agents - frameworks, orchestration patterns, tool use conventions, handoff protocols between agents.

- Sequence the agent build roadmap.

- Design the human-in-the-loop thresholds - when an agent escalates vs. executes autonomously.

- Own the technical architecture decisions: LLM selection, retrieval strategy, memory design, context window management.

3. Agent Operations & Lifecycle Management :

- Run the agent registry - versioning, deployment, deprecation, and change control for all live agents.

- Manage agent performance over time: drift detection, accuracy degradation, prompt updates as business rules change.

- Own the incident response protocol when an agent produces an incorrect output or takes an unintended action.

- Coordinate agent updates when underlying data schemas, business logic, or finance policies change.

4. Visibility & Monitoring Platform :

- Build or procure a Finance AI Control Center - a dashboard giving real-time visibility into which agents are running, what they've done, error rates, and escalation queues.

- Define and track agent KPIs: task completion rate, exception rate, cycle time vs. manual baseline, cost per transaction.

- Create an audit log for every agent action - who initiated it, what data was touched, what output was produced.

- Report agent health and ROI to management on a regular cadence.

5. AI Risk Management & Internal Controls :

- Design and own the internal control framework for AI in Finance.

- Define approval hierarchies: what an agent can do autonomously vs. what requires human sign-off (e.g., any journal entry over $X requires controller review).

- Partner with infosec on data access controls.

6. Finance Organization Training & Change Management :

- Design and deliver the Finance AI literacy curriculum - from foundational concepts to role-specific agent interaction training.

- Build the change management playbook for the transition: how teams move from manual processes to agent-assisted workflows.

- Create and maintain agent user guides - what each agent does, its limitations, how to override it, and how to report issues.

- Work with Finance leaders to embed AI fluency into their team cultures.

7. Process Reengineering :

- Lead the Finance process rewrite initiative.

- Identify which steps in each process are agent-executable vs. requiring judgment, and draw those boundaries explicitly.

- Ensure redesigned processes still satisfy internal control requirements and auditability standards.

- Feed process redesign outputs back into agent specifications and the semantic layer.

Qualifications :

- Minimum 8 years of experience. Hands-on experience building and managing LLM-based agents in production environments. Background spanning finance operations, data engineering, and AI/ML systems.

- Computer skills: BigQuery, dbt, Fivetran, SQL, Python, LLM orchestration frameworks, data pipeline management.

title: Head of Quality
description:
About Tutor

We believe robots are the biggest lever we have to making the physical world a better, more affordable place. But robots are a rounding error in our society: nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t even have a single robot, and robots have yet to make their way into our homes or places of business.

Tutor Intelligence is changing that.

Tutor is a robotics research and deployment company, building generally capable robot hardware and artificial intelligence to enable robots to go where no robots have gone before. Sonny is a semi-humanoid robot with frontier dexterity approaching the human form. Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for businesses from family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Tutor robots are manufactured at scale and operate as a network, combining the whole fleet’s learned experience to train ever more capable robot artificial intelligence.

Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, our team is full stack: we design and manufacture robot hardware, train our own models, work directly with the smallest and largest end-customers, and maintain our fleet across the United States. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.

Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.

The Role

Our Watertown factory is ramping Cassie from 30 to 80+ robots a month and launching Sonny V2 production in 2027. We're hiring our first Head of Quality to build the function from the ground up.

You'll report to our CTO as a peer to the Heads of Manufacturing and Supply Chain, with the authority to hold any shipment that isn't right.

This is a builder role. There's no incoming inspection or formal quality system yet. You'll lead root cause yourself at first, then grow a small team around you.

What You'll Own

  • Production quality: incoming, in-process and final quality gates, first-pass yield, and ship-hold authority
  • Field reliability: RMA, failure analysis, FRACAS and the weekly MRB, with MTBF targets set alongside Engineering
  • Supplier quality: audits, PPAP and SCARs across our US and Asia supply base, plus qualifying second sources
  • Quality system: document control, CAPA, product safety certifications (UL/CSA/CE) and ISO 9001 readiness
  • Data and tools: quality data on our MES (ION) and internal platform (Atlas) that every team trusts
  • Your team: hire a Quality & Reliability Engineer, US and Asia supplier quality engineers, and a quality systems specialist

Your First Year

  • Zero escapes through the Cassie ramp to 80+ robots a month
  • A launch quality plan ready for Sonny V2's ramp to 18 robots a day
  • Every field failure traced to a root cause and a verified fix
  • Second-source suppliers qualified for drives, PCBAs, robot arms and castings

What You Bring

  • BS or higher in engineering
  • 8+ years in hardware quality, including 3+ leading quality engineers
  • You've built a quality function or QMS where none existed
  • You've personally led 8D/RCA to closure on electromechanical hardware
  • Supplier quality at scale, including suppliers in Asia
  • A background in robotics, EV/battery/automotive, or capital equipment
  • The judgment to stop a shipment, and the relationships to keep teams moving
  • You manage by data. Bonus if you've built tools other people use.

Nice to Have

  • Lithium battery safety and transport (UN 38.3)
  • Product safety certification experience (UL/CSA/CE)
  • ASQ CQE/CRE or Six Sigma Black Belt
  • Mandarin, or direct work with Chinese suppliers
  • MES/PLM experience (ION, Arena or similar)

Why Tutor?

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

About our team

Technology | Enterprise Technology Services | Operational Capability | Enforcement Communications

The Operational Capability Branch (OCB) enables operational capability through the provision, support and sustainment of technology to operational areas responsible for Australian Border Force (ABF) frontline activities, in line with the ABF Service Delivery Framework and Capability Lifecycle Management Model.


The Enforcement Communication Section (EC) within the Operational Capability Branch, Enterprise Technology Services Division, contributes to the preservation of Australia's border integrity, delivering, maintaining and enhancing Australian Border Force (ABF) operational enforcement communications networks and equipment. Enforcement communications capabilities are critical to ABF operational effectiveness, security and officer/safety.


The EC team is responsible for the design, installation, support, maintenance and upgrades to operational Enforcement Communications equipment, including Ultra High Frequency (UHF) systems at airports and seaports, networks in regional centres including the Torres Strait where there is an operational ABF presence.


The team is also responsible for deployable tactical satellite communications systems and the delivery of projects funded under the Capital Investment Program.

Please visit our website for more information about the Department of Home Affairs or Australian Border Force.

Our ideal candidate

  • The Candidate will have the ability to, or be willing to quickly acquire, technical expertise in the enforcement communications capabilities that are managed by the Section. Specifically, UHF, Very High Frequency (VHF) radio and other communications equipment to be used in remote areas, such as satellite communication and 4G
  • The candidate will have an interest in and or experience with computer networking technologies and procedures desirable for UHF and Radio Over IP (ROIP) installation/troubleshooting
  • The Enforcement Communications Officer will work directly to the Enforcement Communications Technical Officer and with other members of the team and external service providers for Enforcement Communications support and maintenance
  • The role will also be required to contribute to contract management through logistical support and fault and asset management. The position holder will also assist with management of the Enforcement Communications Lab
  • The candidate will have the opportunity to align and work with subject matter experts for Enforcement Communications within the Section to assist with maintenance and logistical asset support across Australia.

  • Address issues with regards to EC systems, infrastructure and reporting of faults to third level service providers
  • Assist with management of a substantial number of EC assets recorded in the Asset Management database within the Connected Services Portal
  • Facilitate Deployment, set up, tune and calibrate radio frequency elements following maintenance schedules using appropriate tools and test equipment
  • Provide logistical support, including but not limited to:
    • Encryption key uploads
    • Upgrade of equipment
    • Equipment shipping/tracking
    • Management of storage and equipment, including disposal planning
  • Coordinate management of the Enforcement Communications Lab and warehouse and ensure compliance with work, health and safety regulations, including housekeeping.

title: Missions Coordinator
description:
MISSIONS COORDINATOR

Hillside Fellowship

Missions Department | Full-Time | Exempt


Anticipated Start Date: January 2027


Reports To: Director of Missions

Schedule: Sunday - Thursday, with occasional evening and weekend responsibilities

Benefits: As outlined in the Hillside Fellowship Personnel Handbook


ROLE SUMMARY

Hillside Fellowship believes that Jesus Changes Everything! Our mission is that we exist to worship God, by proclaiming Jesus, making disciples, rooted in the Word of God, empowered by the Spirit of God. Discipleship is a byproduct, as we know and make much of Jesus.


The Missions Coordinator serves under the direction of the Director of Missions to coordinate the planning and execution of mission trips, outreach initiatives, training opportunities, and ministry events. This role provides project coordination, operational organization, and consistent follow-through to ensure ministry priorities are carried out effectively and participants are well-supported throughout their involvement.


As a key member of the Missions team, this role strengthens ministry operations by developing repeatable systems, managing project timelines, coordinating communication, and equipping staff and volunteer leaders with the tools and information needed to serve effectively. Through initiative, attention to detail, and thoughtful problem-solving, the Missions Coordinator helps build sustainable ministry processes that support both Missions and Outreach while allowing ministry leadership to focus on strategic priorities and relationships.


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Mission Trip Coordination

  • Coordinate mission trip operations from initial planning through post-trip follow-up
  • Manage participant requirements, payments, passport information, fundraising milestones, training schedules, travel preparation, and other trip-related logistics
  • Coordinate operational details with ministry partners, trip leaders, Finance, Communications, and other Hillside teams
  • Develop and maintain trip checklists, planning templates, participant resources, and leader tools that support consistent preparation and execution


Mission Initiatives + Events

  • Coordinate operational planning for equipping classes, community service projects, local disciple-making initiatives, and other missions and outreach events
  • Manage registrations, materials, supplies, facility needs, purchasing, and event preparation
  • Coordinate responsibilities and communication among staff, volunteers, ministry partners, and supporting Hillside teams to ensure events are prepared and executed effectively
  • Develop reusable event plans and operational resources, with Director input and approval, that support consistent execution and future ministry growth


Project + Timeline Management

  • Maintain an annual calendar of missions initiatives, planning windows, promotional deadlines, and key milestones
  • Develop and manage project plans that establish clear responsibilities, deadlines, dependencies, and next steps
  • Monitor project progress, identify competing priorities or potential delays, and proactively coordinate solutions within established ministry direction
  • Provide timely updates to the Director of Missions regarding project status, upcoming deadlines, challenges, and decisions requiring leadership input


Participant Communication + Engagement

  • Manage participant communication for mission trips, trainings, classes, outreach initiatives, and events, including registration confirmations, preparation instructions, reminders, and follow-up
  • Partner with the Communications Team on promotional timelines, ministry information, and participant-facing materials
  • Maintain clear participant pathways from initial interest through preparation, participation, and appropriate follow-up


Ministry Systems + Process Development

  • Develop and maintain documented workflows, checklists, templates, and shared planning resources that support consistent ministry operations across Missions and Outreach
  • Partner with the Director of Missions and ministry leaders to identify operational improvements and implement approved process changes
  • Identify barriers or gaps that affect church-wide participation and recommend practical improvements to the participant experience
  • Maintain accurate participation records, registration information, and other data needed for planning and decision-making
  • Train and support staff and volunteer leaders in using shared processes, timelines, and tools that support effective ministry execution


Collaboration + Churchwide Alignment

  • Collaborate with Hillside ministries and teams to align and support coordinated ministry planning, clear communication, and timely follow-through
  • Coordinate operational requests and handoffs with Finance, Communicatios, Facilities, and other departments as appropriate
  • Support churchwide initiatives and priorities as requested by the Director of Missions

Additional Responsibilities

  • This role may include additional responsibilities as needed to support the mission and leadership of Hillside Fellowship, with the scope of ministry growing and adapting as organizational needs change


QUALIFICATIONS AND REQUIREMENTS

Faith + Character

  • Demonstrates a maturing relationship with Jesus Christ and embodies the culture and values of Hillside Fellowship (Galatians 5:22–23)

title: Taxi Crane Operator
description:
Taxi Crane Operator

At Beyel Brothers, we're dedicated to excellence in crane operations, rigging, heavy haulage, and marine transport. Our mission is to lead with humility, drive, and social smarts, attracting talented individuals to join our team. With a focus on safety, efficiency, and client satisfaction, we strive to set industry standards and build lasting relationships. As we continue to expand our operations, we are searching for a skilled and experienced Large AT Crane Operator who also excels in equipment logistics management.

Position Overview:

We are currently looking for a talented Taxi Crane Operator to operate our fleet of taxi cranes. The successful candidate will be responsible for safely and efficiently operating the crane to lift, move, and position materials and equipment at job sites. This position offers the opportunity to work with state-of-the-art equipment and be a part of a dynamic team.

Responsibilities:

  • - Operate taxi cranes to lift and move materials and equipment on construction sites, industrial facilities, and other locations as needed.
  • - Interpret load charts and work orders to determine the appropriate crane configuration and lifting procedures for each job.
  • - Conduct pre-operational inspections of the crane to ensure it is in safe working condition and report any defects or maintenance issues to the appropriate personnel.
  • - Safely rig loads and attach them to the crane using appropriate rigging techniques and equipment.
  • - Communicate effectively with ground personnel using hand signals, radio communication, or other means to coordinate crane movements.
  • - Adhere to all safety regulations and procedures to prevent accidents, injuries, and damage to property.
  • - Complete required paperwork and documentation accurately and in a timely manner.
  • - Perform routine maintenance tasks on the crane, such as lubrication and minor repairs, to keep it in optimal working condition.

Requirements:

  • - Must have valid NCCCO certification.
  • - Minimum of 1-3 years of experience operating taxi cranes or similar equipment.
  • - Must have valid CDL for at least 3 years.
  • - Strong understanding of crane operation principles, load capacities, and rigging techniques.
  • - Proficient in industry rigging standards and practices (ASME, OSHA), adept at calculating sling angles and tensions, and skilled in determining center of gravity both mathematically and in the field through comprehensive training and hands-on experience with various materials and weights.
  • - Must demonstrate expertise in selecting appropriate rigging capacities and pick points to safely support the load.
  • - Proficiency in creating and executing critical lift plans in the field.
  • - Capable of accurately adhering to critical lift plans and procedures crafted by the Engineering team.
  • - Excellent hand-eye coordination and spatial awareness.
  • - Ability to work effectively as part of a team and communicate clearly with others.
  • - Willingness to work outdoors in various weather conditions and at heights.
  • - Ability to lift and move heavy objects and work in confined spaces as needed.
  • - Good communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work well in a team environment.
  • - Attention to detail and a commitment to safety at all times.
  • - Flexibility to work evenings, weekends, and overtime as required by project demands.
  • - Must be willing to travel out of state for extended periods as required by project demands.
  • - Must pass fit for duty assessment, drug test, and background check.

Benefits:

  • - Competitive pay commensurate with experience.
  • - Comprehensive benefits package, including medical, dental, and vision coverage.
  • - 401(k) retirement savings plan with employer match.
  • - Opportunities for professional development and future advancement within the company.


At Beyel Brothers, we believe in offering equal employment opportunities to all individuals, irrespective of race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, age, disability, genetic information, veteran status, or any other protected status. We are dedicated to fostering a workplace culture that values diversity and inclusivity, where every employee is treated with respect and dignity. title: AI Delivery Lead - Atlas Platform
description:
About Anthrobyte :

Anthrobyte wins by putting AI agents into the real operations of enterprise clients and making them work, in production, where it matters. We need a leader who does this exceptionally themselves and builds a team that does it the same way. You'll own how we deliver AI, from the client's messy reality to a system they trust and turn every engagement into repeatable capability inside our ATLAS platform. This is a build-from-the-front role. You lead from inside the problem, not from a whiteboard.

What you'll own :

- Embedded delivery : You go where the work is inside the client's environment, alongside their operators to understand their workflows, data, and constraints firsthand. You don't design in the abstract; you build against reality.

- End-to-end ownership : From business problem to architecture to a deployed, secured, monitored agent running in production and driving outcomes. You own the whole arc, not a slice of it.

- The product loop : You turn what you learn in the field into reusable patterns, accelerators, and standards inside ATLAS so the next engagement is faster and we compound into a product, not a services treadmill.

- Building the team : This is the multiplier. You hire, mentor, and level up engineers to work the way you do codifying your instinct into a playbook others can run. Success is a team who deliver like you, not you delivering everything.

- Client trust : You sit across from client security, data, and business leaders and earn their confidence in architecture reviews, security reviews, and the room where decisions get made.

What we're looking for :

- Production track record : You've personally taken AI, ML, or agent systems into enterprise production not demos, not pilots that died. You've worked with real client data and lived with what you shipped.

- Proof you build people: You've mentored engineers, set technical standards, and shaped how a team works. Evidence you can reproduce your skill in others, not just exercise it yourself.

- Range: You're equally comfortable writing code, whiteboarding architecture, and holding your own with a client's CISO.

- Systems mindset: You think in reliability and trust, not cleverness enterprise AI is won on auditability and things that keep working.

- Ownership drive: You're energised by building something from early and shaping how it's done.

Bonus points :

- Domain experience in supply chain, procurement, pricing, or other regulated / operational enterprise environments.

- Exposure to enterprise security, governance, and responsible-AI practices.

- A track record of growing engineers into strong, independent operators.

What this role is not :

- A back-office ML research lead.

- A pure people-manager who's left the tools behind.

- An architect who designs from a distance and never touches the client's reality. If you want to lead from a whiteboard rather than from inside the problem, this isn't it.

title: Community Nature Educator
description:
Job Title: Community Nature Educator

About the Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy:

Our vision: A vibrant park system that is welcoming, accessible, and enjoyed by all.
Our mission: We improve quality of life by enhancing and stewarding Pittsburgh’s parks in partnership with the community.



Position Summary

The Community Nature Educator develops and delivers nature-based education programs that strengthen understanding of and connection to Pittsburgh’s parks and their natural and cultural resources. As a member of the Education Department, this position builds and sustains partnerships with community-based organizations to engage children, families, and learners of all ages. Current programming and outreach focus on Homewood, Hazelwood, the Northside, and South Hilltop, with opportunities to serve other communities.



This position represents the Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy (PPC) in the community and advances its mission through programming that responds to community needs and partner priorities. The ideal candidate brings strong interpersonal skills, an understanding of natural systems and the intersection of economic and environmental justice, and the ability to communicate the importance of parks and green spaces to individual and community well-being. This position requires adaptability and the ability to work both independently and collaboratively.



Position Duties

Under the general supervision of the Director of Education, responsibilities include:

  • Design engaging, age-appropriate, nature-based learning experiences that promote comfort in, curiosity about, and care for nature. Activities may include nature exploration, arts, crafts, games, gross motor play, mindfulness, and inquiry-based observation.
  • Deliver nature-based learning experiences in afterschool programs, summer camps, community parks, and other community learning spaces, incorporating positive youth development principles, inclusive practices, and environmental justice.
  • Develop and sustain partnerships with youth- and family-serving organizations, Citiparks, schools, universities, and other community partners through outreach, ongoing communication, collaborative programming, reflection, and assessment.
  • Create safe, supportive learning environments through positive reinforcement, role modeling, and respect for learners’ diverse backgrounds and experiences.
  • Serve as PPC’s lead representative for the PNC Grow Up Great Buzzword Initiative, which provides early learning and literacy resources to young children and their families, and coordinate programming, partner communication, and required deliverables.
  • Collaborate with the education team to deliver K–12 school-based outdoor education programs and identify opportunities to connect school partnerships with community programs.
  • Lead and contribute to the planning and delivery of family-based public programs and special events, including Earth Month and Community Campfire.
  • Consistently document program participation, outcomes, and outreach activities to support program assessment, grant proposals, and grant reporting.
  • Contribute to the training and professional development of part-time educators, camp counselors, volunteers, and interns.
  • Collaborate with community engagement and visitor experience staff to coordinate work with community partners and stakeholders.
  • Perform other related duties as assigned.



Knowledge, Skills and Abilities

  • Ability to develop and adapt curriculum and lesson plans for school, afterschool, and camp settings.
  • Understanding of natural systems and the role of parks and green spaces in individual and community well-being.
  • Commitment to respecting human diversity and fostering appreciation for biodiversity.
  • Ability to build collaborative relationships and respond to community needs and partner priorities.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office Suite and digital tools for research, data management, scheduling, and communication.
  • Ability to manage multiple projects, establish priorities, solve problems creatively, and meet deadlines.
  • Strong listening, interpersonal, and oral and written communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively and adapt programming to different audiences and settings.



Requirements

  • Three or more years of experience engaging youth in environmental education, outdoor learning, and/or the arts; or a degree in environmental education or a related field.
  • Obtain and maintain required clearances: Pennsylvania Department of Human Services Child Abuse History Clearance, Pennsylvania State Police Criminal History Record Check, and FBI Criminal History Background Check.
  • Maintain a valid driver’s license.
  • Maintain current First Aid and CPR certifications.
  • Availability to work evenings as part of the regular schedule and occasional weekends.



Physical Requirements

The physical demands described here are representative of those required to perform the essential duties of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform these duties.

  • Ability to lead and participate in indoor and outdoor educational activities, including remaining seated or standing for extended periods.
  • Ability to travel over rough or uneven terrain and wet or slippery surfaces in parks and other outdoor learning spaces.
  • Ability to bend, kneel, crouch, reach, and handle program materials and equipment during program preparation, delivery, and cleanup.
  • Ability to communicate with participants and colleagues and monitor participants and surroundings during educational activities.



Compensation & Benefits:

The Pittsburgh Parks Conservancy offers a competitive compensation and benefits package for eligible full-time employees, including:

  • Medical coverage through an Individual Coverage Health Reimbursement Arrangement (ICHRA)
  • Employer-paid dental and vision insurance
  • Retirement plan with an employer match of up to 8%
  • Employer-paid life insurance
  • Short-term and long-term disability coverage
  • Generous paid time off and paid holidays
  • Paid parental, bereavement, and other applicable leave
  • Professional development opportunities
  • A flexible work environment with opportunities for hybrid work, based on position responsibilities and organizational needs

The PPC is committed to creating a diverse environment and is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, religion, gender, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, national origin, genetics, disability, age, veteran status, or other protected characteristics.

title: Generative AI Engineer
description:
Role Overview:

As a Generative AI Engineer, you will sit at the intersection of cutting-edge research and scalable product engineering, architecting sophisticated systems that leverage Large Language Models to solve complex business challenges. Your day-to-day involves designing and deploying Agentic AI workflows, fine-tuning LLMs for domain-specific tasks, and optimizing inference pipelines to ensure high performance and reliability. You will collaborate closely with cross-functional product teams, data scientists, and senior stakeholders to translate ambiguous business requirements into robust, production-grade AI solutions.

Key Responsibilities:

- Architect and deploy end-to-end Agentic AI frameworks that automate multi-step reasoning tasks to improve operational throughput for our business units.

- Fine-tune and optimize pre-trained LLMs using techniques like LoRA or QLoRA to ensure high accuracy and relevance for specialized industry datasets.

- Design scalable RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) pipelines to provide models with real-time, context-aware data, significantly reducing hallucination rates.

- Collaborate with engineering teams to integrate AI models into existing production environments, ensuring seamless API performance and low-latency response times.

- Evaluate and benchmark model performance against business KPIs, iterating on prompt engineering and architectural design to maximize ROI for stakeholders.

- Mentor junior engineers on best practices for machine learning operations (MLOps) and the ethical deployment of generative technologies.

Required Skillset:

- Demonstrated expertise in building and scaling Generative AI applications using frameworks such as LangChain, LlamaIndex, or AutoGPT, with a deep understanding of LLM orchestration.

- Proven ability to design and implement complex machine learning pipelines, including data preprocessing, model training, and deployment in cloud environments like AWS, GCP, or Azure.

- Strong proficiency in Python and deep learning libraries such as PyTorch or TensorFlow, combined with the ability to write clean, maintainable, and production-ready code.

- Exceptional communication skills, with the ability to articulate technical AI concepts to non-technical stakeholders and influence product roadmaps.

- A collaborative mindset that thrives in a hybrid work environment, balancing independent research with active participation in cross-functional team sprints.

- A Masters or Bachelors degree in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, or a related quantitative field, backed by 6 - 10 years of professional experience in software engineering or data science.

- High adaptability to the rapidly evolving AI landscape, demonstrated by a history of quickly adopting new research papers, tools, and architectural patterns.

title: International Relations Internship
description:
DevTech Systems, Inc. is seeking an International Relations Intern interested in gaining hands-on experience in the international development and professional services field.

This internship is designed as a structured educational and professional development experience. Through supervised assignments, observation, mentorship, and feedback, the Intern will have opportunities to apply academic concepts and develop practical skills in international affairs research, project and program management, business development, professional communications, stakeholder engagement, and organizational operations.

Learning activities will vary based on the Intern’s academic and professional interests and available educational opportunities at DevTech.


What You Will Learn and Experience

During the internship, the Intern may have opportunities to:

  • Conduct supervised research on countries, regions, international development issues, policies, institutions, donors, and stakeholders.
  • Prepare draft research summaries, briefing notes, country or stakeholder profiles, and other analytical materials for feedback.
  • Learn how international development projects are planned, managed, monitored, and documented.
  • Observe selected project meetings, workshops, business development discussions, and stakeholder engagements.
  • Learn how organizations identify and evaluate government contracting, grant, partnership, and other business development opportunities.
  • Review solicitations and practice conducting opportunity, client, market, and partner research.
  • Develop professional written and verbal communication skills through supervised exercises and presentations.
  • Practice using project-management, research, data-organization, and knowledge-management tools.
  • Gain exposure to professional stakeholder engagement and cross-cultural communication.
  • Complete a culminating research and writing project related to international development or international affairs.

Throughout the internship, the Intern will receive instruction, mentorship, and feedback from DevTech staff and will have opportunities to revise work and demonstrate continued skill development.


What You Will Bring

  • Currently enrolled in an undergraduate or graduate program; International Relations, International Development, Political Science, Global Studies, Economics, or a related field preferred.
  • Strong interest in international development, international affairs, consulting, government contracting, or professional services.
  • Strong research, organizational, and attention-to-detail skills.
  • Clear written and verbal communication skills.
  • Basic proficiency with Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint; familiarity with Canva or other professional tools is a plus.
  • Curiosity, initiative, professionalism, and an interest in learning from multiple areas of an international organization.
  • Authorization to work in the United States.


Internship Structure

This is an unpaid educational internship intended primarily to provide the Intern with structured learning, mentorship, practical experience, and professional development. Activities are performed under supervision and are selected for their educational value.

The internship is not intended to replace or displace paid employees, and the Intern will not independently manage projects, clients, proposals, or other organizational functions ordinarily assigned to DevTech employees.

There is no expectation or guarantee of paid employment with DevTech following completion of the internship.


Selection Process

Applicants will be evaluated based on relevant coursework, demonstrated interest in international affairs or international development, applicable skills and experience, academic and professional goals, and interview performance.

title: Billing Coordinator
description:
MG+M The Law Firm (MG+M) has an immediate opening for a Billing Coordinator in our New Orleans, LA, Edwardsville, IL, Basking Ridge, NJ, and Wilmington, DE.

MG+M is a nationally renowned litigation firm focused on complex civil matters. Our work is diverse but concentrated in toxic tort, complex product liability, local government, general liability, and commercial litigation. We approach every case as a unified team, working closely with our clients to advance their interests wherever they do business. Our goal is always to deliver optimal results at the best possible value.


The Billing Coordinator plays a critical role in the firm’s revenue cycle by managing complex billing for firm partners and clients. They are responsible for printing and distributing pre-bills and preparing all electronic billing by verifying that all billing requirements are met and submitted bills are accepted. The Coordinator also assists with investigating and resolving billing issues, tracking billing requirements for complex litigation clients and third-party payees, and will work closely with all finance departments to ensure accurate billing and reporting.

The ideal candidate will have at least 3 years of experience in a legal or professional services environment, familiarity with Aderant or similar law firm accounting software, advanced Excel skills, and the ability to work independently and collaboratively with others both within and outside the Finance Team. Discretion, attention to detail, and diplomacy are essential.


Key Responsibilities:

  • Collaborate with attorneys and staff to create, distribute, post and submit pre-bills and bills through various delivery methods
  • Uphold firm requirements including client and insurer and billing guidelines, rates, preferences and expenses to ensure compliance
  • Identify, research and resolve billing inaccuracies and issues
  • Participate in firm-wide and departmental projects
  • Analyze client accounting, including work in progress, and provide ad-hoc reporting as needed
  • Maintain documentation of procedures for assigned attorneys and accounts
  • Escalate billing issues to management as needed

Candidate Qualifications:

  • At least 3 years’ experience in legal billing or similar financial role (legal billing or paralegal with billing experience preferred)
  • Minimum of an Associate’s degree required (Bachelor’s is preferred, but not required)
  • Familiarity with insurance defense billing preferred
  • Experience with complex legal billing

Essential Skills:

  • Proficient in Microsoft Excel, including formulas, pivot tables and V-Lookups
  • Experience with Aderant, BillBlast, and electronic billing platforms preferred
  • Excellent communication skills, strong problem-solving ability, and team-oriented mindset


Why Should You Apply?

Our associates work closely with our senior lawyers and clients on challenging work in an entrepreneurial and collegial environment. We offer a hybrid work environment, competitive compensation and a comprehensive benefits package including medical, dental, vision, life, disability, and 401(k).


MG+M will not discriminate in its employment practices due to an applicant’s age, race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, and veteran or disability status. We are committed to cultivating an environment that embraces and promotes diversity as a fundamental value.

title: Data Scientist - Python
description:
Data Scientist

Role : Data Scientist - Python

Location : Hyderabad, India

Experience : 7 - 12 years

Employment Type : Full-time, Work from Office role

About TrueID :

TrueID is a Biometric-Enabled Identity Management company providing solutions for digital identity, biometric authentication, identity verification, KYC, and secure customer onboarding for the fintech and banking sectors. We use AI, machine learning, biometrics, and advanced data analytics to solve complex identity and fraud-related problems.

Role Overview :

We are looking for a Data Scientist with hands-on Python coding skills to develop and deploy AI/ML solutions for identity management. The role involves working with real-world identity data, developing NLP and name-matching algorithms, building ML models, and integrating them into production applications. The candidate will also be required to understand, analyze, enhance, and extend an existing Python codebase. Since access to external LLM-based coding assistants such as ChatGPT or Claude may be limited due to the confidentiality of data, the candidate must have strong independent coding and problem-solving abilities.

Key Responsibilities :

- Develop algorithms for name matching, entity resolution, record linkage, duplicate detection, and identity matching.

- Apply NLP and text similarity techniques including Jaro-Winkler, Levenshtein, TF-IDF, n-grams, token-based similarity, phonetic matching, embeddings, and transformer-based approaches.

- Perform data preparation, feature engineering, statistical analysis, model training, validation, and performance optimization.

- Develop hybrid solutions combining deterministic rules, fuzzy matching, statistical methods, and machine learning.

- Write clean, efficient, maintainable Python code and develop reusable data science and ML components.

- Understand and work extensively with an existing Python codebase, identify issues, optimize algorithms, and implement new functionality.

- Develop and deploy ML models as production services/APIs and work with engineering teams to integrate them into enterprise applications.

- Analyze model performance and address issues such as false positives, false negatives, scalability, latency, and model explainability.

- Research and evaluate new AI/NLP techniques relevant to identity verification, fraud detection, and identity intelligence.

Required Skills :

- Strong hands-on Python programming and software development skills.

- Natural Language Processing and advanced text matching.

- Strong foundation in Data Science, Machine Learning, statistics, and predictive modelling.

- Strong knowledge of NLP, text processing, similarity algorithms, and entity matching.

- Experience with Pandas, NumPy, Scikit-learn, SciPy, and related Python ML/NLP libraries.

- Identity management, digital identity, KYC/e-KYC, or biometric applications.

- Ability to independently understand and modify an existing codebase and develop solutions with limited reliance on LLM coding assistants.

- Experience in Fraud detection and anomaly detection models with respect to identity fraud is an added advantage.

- Worked on Customer/entity resolution and duplicate identity detection.

- Worked on Multilingual NLP, transliteration, and matching of names across different languages/scripts.

- Experience in ML model deployment, REST APIs, Docker, AWS, or MLOps.

Education :

Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Data Science, Artificial Intelligence, Statistics, Mathematics, Engineering, or a related discipline.

title: Techno-Functional Manager - Temenos Payments Hub
description:
Job Description :

The ideal candidate will have strong functional expertise in Temenos Payments Hub (TPH), hands-on technical capabilities, and a thorough understanding of payment processing workflows and core banking integrations.

The candidate will collaborate with business stakeholders, architects, development teams, and implementation partners to deliver scalable, secure, and efficient payment solutions.

Key Responsibilities :

- Lead the functional design, configuration, implementation, and enhancement of Temenos Payments Hub (TPH).

- Understand and translate business requirements related to domestic and international payments into functional and technical specifications.

- Design and optimize end-to-end payment processing workflows, including payment initiation, validation, routing, processing, settlement, and exception handling.

- Configure payment products, payment schemes, transaction rules, and processing parameters based on business requirements.

- Ensure effective handling of payment investigations, returns, reversals, rejections, and reconciliation processes.

- Work with business teams to identify process gaps and recommend platform enhancements.

- Design and implement integration solutions between Temenos TPH and Temenos T24 (Transact), ensuring seamless data exchange and transaction processing.

title: Common Ground Country Fair Manager
description:
Overview of Responsibilities: This position is responsible for managing administrative and retail operations for MOFGA’s Common Ground Country Fair. Reporting to the CGCF Director, this role manages exhibitor application workflows, the Fair’s CRM system, and drives retail operations by leading the Country Store budget, inventory forecasting, and vendor coordination. Additionally, the Manager assists with overall Fair budgeting, revenue forecasting, and stipend processing.

The Manager supervises the CGCF and Store Assistant, conducts volunteer training, and manages the Fair Office as the central hub for vendor support and inquiries. Responsibilities also include updating digital and print materials, as well as assisting with Fair set-up and clean-up.


Supervisor: Common Ground Country Fair Director


Work Week: Full time, generally Monday through Friday, 9:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Occasional weekend hours required. Extended hours required around and including the Common Ground Country Fair.


Position: Salaried. Federal Fair Labor Standards Act Exempt. This employee is not eligible for overtime payment. This position is not eligible for MOFGA’s collective bargaining unit.


Location: This position is based at MOFGA’s office in Unity, Maine. Work is primarily on-site, requiring a minimum of three days per week in the office starting in the summer, and full-time on-site presence during September. A flexible hybrid work schedule may be arranged for the remainder of the year and can be discussed during the hiring process.


Salary and Benefits: The salary range for this position is $58,000-63,000 annually depending upon experience. MOFGA has an excellent benefits package, including paid medical, dental and vision insurance, and parental leave. Employees receive a generous paid time off package, including vacation and sick time, three personal days, two week-long office closures, 14 paid holidays annually, and a sabbatical after seven years of employment


Minimum Qualifications:

  • Passion for organic farming, gardening, and community-based work in Maine.
  • Experience planning and executing events while managing multiple projects concurrently.
  • Exceptional organizational skills with the ability to manage a high volume of administrative data.
  • Outstanding written, proofreading, and interpersonal communication skills across diverse stakeholders (staff, volunteers, vendors, and the public).
  • Demonstrated success leading, supervising, and training small teams and volunteers.
  • Strong computer literacy: including CRM databases, Microsoft Office, Google Workspace, website content management, and an aptitude for learning new systems.
  • Creative problem-solving skills and the ability to take initiative where appropriate.


Responsibilities:

Overall:

  • Coordinate CGCF Planning Team members to ensure that exhibitor correspondence, applications, contracts, and guidelines are updated and accurate each year.
  • Manage all elements of exhibitor applications, contracts and Fair Office correspondence to ensure we have all required paperwork and information.
  • Provide support and oversight, as necessary, to Planning Team members to ensure that planning and implementation of all areas are completed on time and follow MOFGA policies and Fair and Area guidelines.
  • Manage and facilitate the Fair CRM; and ensure all CGCF information is entered accurately.
  • Manage relations and communicate effectively with Country Store third-party vendors regarding Fair merchandise, including forecasting future inventory, ordering and order management.
  • Coordinate and place the ribbon order by discount deadline to ensure all ribbons will be available for the upcoming Fair.
  • Assist in increasing diversity at the Fair and helping MOFGA advance their diversity, equity, inclusion, and justice work.
  • Coordinate the review process of Food Area applications, providing ongoing support to Food Vendors in collaboration with the Food Liaison.
  • Write and manage distribution of communications with the Fair Steering Committee, Planning Team and CGCF participants.
  • Update CGCF website content in collaboration with the Communications Team.
  • Supervise and train the CGCF Fair and Store Assistant to ensure a positive work environment that meets the goals of the Fair and facilitates volunteers working with the Fair office team.
  • Attend all Fair Steering Committee (FSC) meetings and represent the Fair at MOFGA committee meetings and meetings outside of regular business hours, as needed and directed by the CGCF Director.
  • Assist CGCF Director with compilation of the Fairbook and other internal and external communications as needed.


Annual CGCF Planning:

  • Participate in on-site Fair set-up and clean-up as needed.
  • Coordinate the operation of the Fair office during the Fair, including, being the primary resource for vendors during set-up and Fair weekend regarding fees, tickets, coordinating office volunteers, answering phone & email inquiries, selling ice, being a communication hub for Fair participants, and more.
  • Record and report Fair participant stipends and payments.
  • Assist CGCF Director with preparation of annual stipend report to the Maine Department of Agriculture, Conservation and Forestry (MDACF).
  • Assist CGCF Director with projecting the annual budget for all Fair generated revenue streams including tickets, merchandise, booth fees, and other Fair related fees.
  • Procure goods and services for the CGCF as needed.
  • Participate and lead aspects of an annual Post-Fair review, reporting, surveys, and lesson learned sessions around the review of CGCF systems and procedures.
  • Other duties as needed.
  • Carry out all of the responsibilities listed above in accordance with the mission statement, goals, and philosophy of the Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Association.


The Maine Organic Farmers and Gardeners Association (MOFGA) is a broad-based community that supports farmers, empowers people to feed their communities, and advocates for an organic future. Our vision is a future where local organic farming nourishes all people, and sustains thriving ecosystems, healthy communities, and fair economies. MOFGA is committed to creating an inclusive and sustainable workplace that reflects this mission. MOFGA is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of race, ethnicity, age, religion, gender, marital status, sexual orientation, disability, veteran status, political orientation, or any other characteristic protected by federal, state, or local law. We strongly encourage BIPOC (Black, Indigenous, and People of Color) and LGBTQ+ individuals, as well as veterans to apply.

title: 1st shift Mold Technician-D
description:
NOW HIRING: Setup / Mold Technicians – 1st Shift

Hoffer Plastics Corporation

Starting Pay: $22.00–$24.00/hr (based on experience)

1st Shift Hours: 8:00am–4:00pm

Want to be part of something special? We're filling important jobs!

Join an industry leader and innovator looking for people who want to make a difference. If you're mechanically minded and want to build a real skilled trade in plastic injection molding, we want to meet you.

Why You'll Love Working Here

  • Day shift: Regular daytime hours, 8:00am to 4:00pm
  • Clear career path: Advance through leveled training from Level C to Level A, with pay that grows with your skills
  • Get trained: Full training on molding, setup, processing and new technology
  • Great benefits: Medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match and more
  • Stability: An established, growing third-generation U.S. company

The Role

As a Setup / Mold Technician, you'll mold parts to meet internal and external customer requirements, including machine setup, auxiliary equipment setup and process parameter input. You'll also keep a neat and orderly work area to 5S standards and follow safety policies. The position is divided into four classifications based on skill set and responsibility, and pay is determined accordingly.

Responsibilities vary based on skill level and experience:

Level C:

  • Complete the B level training curriculum while at Level C.
  • Perform mold setups and color changes to meet production demands.
  • Set molding process parameters with the help of a foreman, supervisor, or A or B level molding technician.
  • Monitor production for accuracy and efficiency and work with quality inspectors to identify defects.
  • Perform material handler duties as assigned.

Level B:

  • Complete the A level training curriculum while at Level B.
  • Set molding process parameters to ensure part quality.
  • Troubleshoot process, machine and auxiliary equipment problems and make necessary changes to ensure quality and reduce downtime.
  • Learn new technology as it's brought into manufacturing.
  • Work with the supervisor and/or Lead Molding Technician to find ways to improve productivity and reduce scrap, defects, etc.

Level A:

  • Work with quality inspectors to identify defects and make good decisions on process changes.
  • Sample new and existing molds.
  • Stay current with new technology in molding, auxiliary equipment, robots, etc.
  • Promote safety by following all related policies and procedures and setting a good example for others.
  • Help maintain 5S and plant cleanliness by completing assigned cleaning tasks and setting a good example for others.
  • Take on the responsibilities of the supervisor or foreman in their absence.

All team members shall:

  • Maintain a positive work atmosphere by communicating in a way that helps you get along with customers, clients, co-workers and management.
  • Continue to grow job-specific knowledge and use tools to identify and assist with continuous improvement.
  • Comply with safety regulations and maintain clean and orderly work areas.

This job description does not contain every function or responsibility that may be required in the performance of this job. All team members are required to perform other related duties and functions as assigned.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Ability and interest in successfully progressing through the leveled Molding Technician training curriculum.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and math proficiency.
  • Proficiency in reading and writing English.
  • Computer proficiency.

Benefits

  • Medical, Dental & Vision: Blue Cross Blue Shield medical and dental, VSP vision
  • 401(k): Hoffer Plastics matches $0.50 per $1.00 contributed each payroll period, up to 6%, plus a Safe Harbor contribution equal to 3% of annual eligible earnings
  • Paid Life Insurance: 1.5 times basic annual salary
  • Short-Term and Long-Term Disability
  • Time Off: 2 weeks paid vacation, up to 5 days of Illinois Paid Leave, and 9 paid holidays
  • Reimbursements: tuition, prescription safety glasses, steel toe shoes, and fitness

Physical Requirements

The incumbent will:

  • Usually stand / walk most of the shift.
  • Frequently bend at waist, twist, kneel / crouch, climb ladders and climb up on machinery with proper fall protection.
  • Occasionally push, pull and lift up to 75 lbs. or more.
  • Occasionally lift above waist and/or shoulder up to 75 lbs. and over.
  • Sometimes perform hand / wrist / finger movements and foot movements for pedal controls on forklift.
  • Occasionally perform keyboarding and squeezing movements.
  • Be frequently exposed to odors, dust and oil / grease.

title: Interior Design Manager
description:
Kinetic Design + Development is looking for an Interior Design Manager to join the Krew.


If you’re a design leader who thrives in both the creative and technical sides of the process, this role is for you.


You bring spaces to life by turning client goals, budgets, and big ideas into thoughtful, functional interior environments. From early programming and design concepts to construction administration and final closeout, you’ll lead projects from start to finish, keeping design quality, project delivery, and the client experience moving in the right direction.


You’ll also help shape the people and processes behind great design. Working alongside architects, consultants, clients, and vendors, you’ll guide project teams, mentor emerging designers, and make sure every detail works together. At Kinetic, your leadership helps move projects forward while building the kind of collaborative, people-first experience our clients and Krew deserve.


Who You Are

You’re a design-minded leader who can zoom out to see the big picture and zoom in to catch the details that make a space work. You balance creative vision with technical know-how, sound project management, and a clear understanding of how design decisions affect budgets, schedules, and construction.


You build trust through honest communication, thoughtful decisions, and follow-through. You know how to bring people together across disciplines, delegate with purpose, and give designers the feedback and support they need to do their best work. When challenges pop up, you adapt, solve problems, and keep things moving without losing sight of the client’s goals.


You take ownership of your projects, care about the quality of your work, and believe the best results come from a team that feels supported, accountable, and connected. You’re ready to lead with confidence while staying approachable, curious, and open to better ways of working.


What You’ll Do

  • Lead interior design projects from programming and concept design through documentation, construction administration, and closeout, serving as the primary day-to-day contact for clients and project teams.
  • Define project expectations by establishing scope, deliverables, milestones, team responsibilities, and priorities at kickoff, keeping them aligned as projects evolve.
  • Drive design direction across space planning, materials, finishes, furniture, fixtures and equipment (FF&E), lighting, millwork, and detailing, balancing client goals with budget, code, and constructability.
  • Coordinate across disciplines by aligning interior deliverables with architectural, structural, MEP, lighting, acoustical, and other consultant teams, clarifying responsibilities, and resolving gaps.
  • Manage project performance by tracking schedules, budgeted hours, fees, billings, and financial forecasts with Project Delivery and the Director of Interior Design. Identify risks early and communicate potential scope changes or additional service needs.
  • Present with purpose by leading client meetings and design presentations, setting clear agendas, documenting decisions, managing expectations, and following through on next steps.
  • Mentor and develop designers by directing, delegating, coaching, and reviewing work from interns and Interior Designers I–III. Balance project needs with individual growth goals, workload, NCIDQ preparation, and professional development.
  • Own quality control by reviewing interior drawings, plans, elevations, details, schedules, and specifications for accuracy, completeness, coordination, and compliance with Kinetic standards before QC Committee handoff.
  • Support construction through closeout by conducting site visits, verifying existing conditions, observing construction, reviewing submittals and RFIs, and leading interior punch lists and closeout activities.
  • Support project pursuits by assisting the Director with proposals, scopes, fee estimates, budgeted hours, and schedules, with clear assumptions and deliverables.
  • Build strong partnerships with clients, contractors, furniture dealers, vendors, and internal teams to support successful projects, repeat business, referrals, marketing, recruiting, and interviews.
  • Improve how we work by using and refining interior design standards, templates, and workflows, sharing lessons learned, and staying current through continuing education and industry events.
  • Lead with clear ownership by exercising day-to-day authority over assigned project design, quality, task direction, and client communication while partnering with firm leadership on proposals, design direction, and interiors standards.
  • Strengthen the Krew by following Kinetics' delivery systems, design standards, and HR Handbook while contributing to a culture of collaboration, clear ownership, and shared accountability.


Tools You’ll Use

  • Design and documentation: Revit, interior plans, elevations, details, schedules, and specifications.
  • Visualization and presentations: Design visualization tools and presentation software.
  • Project delivery and coordination: Kinetics' established project delivery systems, project schedules, budget tracking, consultant coordination, and quality control workflows.
  • Construction administration: Submittal and RFI review processes, site observations, punch lists, and closeout documentation.


What You’ll Bring

  • A bachelor’s degree in Interior Design or a related field.
  • 7+ years of professional interior design experience in an architecture or multidisciplinary practice, including experience leading project teams.
  • Required NCIDQ certification.
  • Experience managing interior projects through programming, concept design, documentation, and construction administration.
  • Strong knowledge of space planning, interior materials, finishes, FF&E, lighting, millwork, detailing, schedules, and specifications.
  • The ability to apply accessibility, life safety, and building code requirements while evaluating constructability, construction methods, and client budgets.
  • Proficiency in Revit and visualization tools, with the ability to review drawings and communicate design concepts through clear presentations.
  • Experience managing project scope, deliverables, schedules, budgeted hours, consultant coordination, financial forecasts, and additional service needs.
  • A sharp eye for detail and the ability to review coordinated documentation for accuracy, completeness, and compliance with established quality standards.
  • Construction administration experience, including submittal and RFI reviews, site observations, punch lists, and closeout.
  • An understanding of procurement coordination, including the boundaries between construction, millwork, and furniture packages, along with lead times and their impact on project delivery.
  • Strong client communication, presentation, organization, and time management skills, with the ability to balance multiple projects and priorities.
  • A collaborative leadership style, sound judgment, adaptability, and a practical approach to problem-solving.
  • A commitment to mentoring teammates, delivering thoughtful design solutions, and following through on commitments with professionalism and care.


Why Join the Krew:

Our Vision:
Kinetic Design + Development is pushing the limits of traditional architectural practice. With a focus on forward motion in technology and design principles, Kinetic is dedicated to bringing energy and innovation to each and every project and client. Kinetic is dedicated to helping clients navigate the adventure of development with ease and energy that moves them forward.


Who We Are:
People are our purpose. Kinetic was created with the idea that people – both our staff and clients – should be above everything else. The firm puts this principle in motion in work-life balance for employees and emphasis on truly getting to know our clients so we can better understand their dreams, goals, and ideas.


Benefits & Perks:
FLEX FRIDAYS: Our standard workweek is Monday through Thursday. Need to shift a day for life stuff? No problem! Swap a weekday with Friday if/when needed.
Comprehensive health benefits
Flexible working arrangements
Opportunities for internal advancement and career development
Relaxed office environment with “smart casual” dress code
Monthly company sponsored events (Check out our socials for pics!)
Monday Morning Breakfasts
Frequent Lunches
PTO & paid company holidays (Including the entire week between Christmas and New Year!)

Traditional & Roth 401k with a 3.5% company match
Daily Snack Cart

2025 ULI Impact Award
