This is a hands-on individual contributor role with influence over our technical direction. You’ll build infrastructure, improve delivery workflows, investigate production behavior, and help other engineers operate more independently. You’ll also help shape how Engineers and AI agents work effectively within our engineering environment.
We’re looking for someone we can trust with an outcome: someone who asks good questions, develops a point of view, brings others along, and follows through.
Our environment includes AWS, Kubernetes, Docker, Terraform, GitLab CI/CD, Datadog, Linux, and PHP/Laravel, alongside data and workflow systems. You don’t need prior experience with every tool.

What You’ll Do:

Our immediate priorities are developer self-service, safer releases, and less operational toil. You’ll help identify where complexity and manual intervention slow us down, and build the practical improvements engineers will and want to use.
You’ll spend most of your time doing technical work, with coaching, collaboration, and technical leadership woven into how you deliver it.
You will:
  • Build a platform that helps engineers help themselves.
  • Build self-serve workflows that let engineers provision infrastructure, ship services, and recover from failures without waiting on anyone.
  • Improve our CI/CD pipelines, deploy checks, progressive delivery, and automated rollback so safe releases take less coordination and manual work.
  • Simplify our infrastructure.
  • Make production changes safer and easier to recover from.
  • Change our AWS and Kubernetes environment by turning the complexity you find into a prioritized plan that balances reliability, security, cost, and upkeep.
  • Improve reliability through evidence
  • Strengthen our observability, alerting, SLOs, and capacity planning, and use incidents and support trends to decide what to fix next.
  • Help build the foundation for agent-assisted engineering.
  • Improve the tooling, environments, reusable context, and access boundaries that let engineers direct agents effectively.
  • Partner with security colleagues to keep permissions, secrets, and consequential actions appropriately controlled.
  • Work across infrastructure and application boundaries.
  • Partner with product and data engineers to track down performance and reliability issues across application code, containers, databases, networking, and cloud services.
  • Make the team more capable.
  • Share your thinking, document decisions, and coach teammates so the systems you touch are understandable to others.
  • Join platform on-call and incident response, and work to make those interruptions rarer and lighter.

Your Experience:

  • 5+ years of experience in platform engineering, DevOps, SRE, or related infrastructure work, or equivalent demonstrated depth.
  • Deep, hands-on Kubernetes experience, including configuration, secrets, deployment, scaling, and production troubleshooting.
  • Experience building and operating AWS infrastructure for production systems with meaningful traffic and availability requirements.
  • Strong infrastructure-as-code and CI/CD experience, including Terraform and GitLab CI or comparable tools.
  • An observability mindset, with experience using metrics, logs, traces, and alerting to understand system behavior.
  • The ability to write, read, debug, and maintain automation and tooling, and investigate problems across application and infrastructure boundaries.
  • Examples of making delivery safer, reducing operational toil, or enabling engineers to work independently.
  • Clear written communication and experience leading technical work across teams without relying on formal authority.
  • Experience with cloud security, least-privilege access, secrets management, SOC 2, or GDPR is especially useful.
  • Application performance tuning, PHP/Laravel, database operations, and infrastructure for AI agents are additional strengths.

What success looks like:

In your first few months, you’ll develop a clear understanding of our environment, earn trust across engineering, and deliver an evidence-backed plan alongside useful early improvements.
As your work takes hold:
  • More routine infrastructure and delivery tasks happen through self-service.
  • Releases become easier to verify and recover from.
  • Engineers spend less time waiting on access, coordination, and manual intervention.
  • Operational noise and recurring incidents decrease.
  • Platform knowledge and ownership become more widely shared.
  • Agent-assisted workflows produce better results with appropriate checks and human accountability.
We care about the depth of your experience and how you approach problems. If this work resonates with you, we’d like to hear what you’ve built, what you’ve simplified, and what you learned along the way.
#LI-ST1

Loop Story

Commerce should feel effortless. Every product adored, every order perfect, every customer loyal for life. But reality is messier: operations get tangled, margins grow thin, and trust is fragile. That’s where Loop steps in. We create confidence where commerce fails.

We started by fixing returns and exchanges. Today, we’re building a connected commerce operations suite — powering everything from order tracking to fraud prevention, with hundreds of innovations in between. Grounded in data and insight, our platform helps merchants make smarter decisions with every transaction. Over 5,000 of the world’s most loved brands trust Loop to turn cost centers into growth engines. Our mission is simple: protect margins, delight customers, and help merchants build businesses that last.

Life at Loop is rooted in our core values. We balance high empathy with high standards, knowing that work is better when we can show up authentically and resilience is built by facing challenges head-on. We expect you’ll grow quickly, learning skills that last far beyond your time here. Loop is a formative chapter in your career — a chance to shape the future of commerce and to leave better than when you arrived.

Learn more about us here: .

You can review our privacy notice here.

title: Project Manager - Service Electrical
description:
PURPOSE

The Service Electrical Project Manager is responsible for leading electrical service, maintenance, repair, renovation, and small-project work from the initial customer request through successful completion. This position serves as a primary point of contact for customers and coordinates estimating, proposal development, project planning, material procurement, manpower, scheduling, field execution, safety, quality control, documentation, and project closeout.

The Service Electrical Project Manager works closely with service operations, electricians, apprentices, subcontractors, vendors, internal departments, and customers to ensure work is performed safely, accurately, profitably, on schedule, and in accordance with applicable codes, specifications, Baker Group standards, and customer expectations. This role is also responsible for identifying additional customer needs, developing service opportunities, supporting long-term customer relationships, and advancing the Baker Group “Client for Life” concept.

ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

The following duties are typical for this job. These are not to be construed as exclusive or all inclusive. Other duties may be required and assigned.

  • Develop and maintain professional relationships with customers, team members, contractors, consultants, vendors, and internal departments.
  • Serve as the primary point of contact for service projects and maintenance accounts.
  • Conduct site walks and meetings to identify deficiencies, risks, repair needs, and future opportunities.
  • Develop scopes, proposals, budgets, material lists, manpower requirements, schedules, execution plans, and pricing for electrical service, maintenance, repair, renovation, preventive maintenance, thermography, NFPA 70B services, equipment replacement, and other electrical work.
  • Communicate schedule, budget, disruptions, safety requirements, changes, and project status.
  • Review drawings, one-lines, schematics, specifications, submittals, existing conditions, and manufacturer documentation.
  • Develop MOPs, shutdown plans, LOTO requirements, outage plans, JHAs, and contingency plans when applicable.
  • Manage projects from authorization through closeout.
  • Coordinate emergency, scheduled, shutdown, outage, and after-hours work while minimizing customer disruption.
  • Provide field direction and technical support to electricians, apprentices, subcontractors, vendors, and other project personnel.
  • Coordinate materials, permits, inspections, utilities, shutdowns, startup, testing, commissioning, and turnover.
  • Sequence work safely and efficiently and verify installation, operation, testing, documentation, code compliance, acceptance, and warranty requirements.
  • Develop and administer budgets, fiscal controls, contracts, purchase orders, and quality-control requirements.
  • Track labor, materials, subcontractors, billing, purchase orders, and projected profit.
  • Compare labor and productivity to estimates and address budget or schedule concerns promptly.
  • Prepare and negotiate change orders, T&M work, NTE work, and additional-scope proposals.
  • Review labor hours, service tickets, invoices, material charges, billing, collections, and closeout documentation.
  • Coordinate manpower, crew assignments, backlog planning, and resource allocation with service operations leadership.
  • Ensure work complies with the NEC, applicable codes, OSHA requirements, Baker Group policies, manufacturer requirements, and project specifications while coordinating JHAs, pre-task planning, confined-space requirements, energized work procedures, and other project-specific safety measures.
  • Maintain working knowledge of distribution systems, controls, generators, transformers, switchgear, motors, HVAC, emergency power, and building electrical systems.
  • Evaluate existing systems and recommend practical, code-compliant repair or replacement solutions.
  • Coordinate testing such as infrared scans, insulation resistance, phase rotation, grounding, startup, and functional testing when applicable.
  • Represent Baker Group professionally with customers, consultants, contractors, inspectors, utilities, and public agencies.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Construction Science, Construction Management, or Electrical Engineering OR a minimum of five (5) years of progressively responsible experience directly related to the essential functions specified.
  • Solid knowledge of Construction practices and principles

CERTIFICATES, LICENSES, REGISTRATIONS

MENTAL AND PHYSICAL COMPETENCIES REQUIRED TO PERFORM ESSENTAL FUNCTIONS

  • Ability to lead and coordinate service electricians, apprentices, subcontractors, vendors and other project team members.
  • Strong organization, communication, customer-service, and professional relationship skills.

  • Ability to remain calm in stressful situations
  • Proficient accounting knowledge
  • Proven problem solving and leadership skills
  • Ability to handle multiple tasks simultaneously
  • Receptive to change, ability to adapt to changing situations

ENVIRONMENTAL ADAPTABILITY

Performs highly complex computer systems analysis work for the CTO team with a primary focus on enterprise application modernization, legacy system transformation, domain-driven design, and responsible use of AI-assisted engineering practices. Work involves assessing aging technology platforms, analyzing complex legacy codebases and system dependencies, identifying business domains and bounded contexts, reducing technical debt, and developing practical strategies to modernize applications for improved scalability, security, interoperability, and long-term maintainability. The position supports modernization planning, source code analysis, migration of business logic, refactoring of monolithic applications, design of modular and cloud-ready service patterns, application of domain-driven design principles, responsible use of AI tools to assist code analysis and modernization planning, implementation of secure development practices, and transition of legacy functionality into modern application frameworks. Work includes preparing technical documentation, mapping current-state and target-state architectures, troubleshooting application issues, supporting modernization roadmaps, and collaborating with engineering, architecture, cloud, security, data, AI, and program teams to align technical solutions with agency business needs. Essential Job Functions (EJFs):

Analyzes legacy applications, source code, data flows, business rules, system dependencies, domain boundaries, bounded contexts, and technical debt; develops modernization assessments, target-state recommendations, and practical roadmaps to transition aging systems to secure, scalable, AI-ready, and maintainable platforms.35%

Refactors, rewrites, configures, and implements modernized application components, business logic, interfaces, domain services, and APIs using domain-driven design principles, secure design practices, approved development standards, AI-assisted engineering tools where appropriate, and modern application frameworks to support upgraded agency business capabilities. 30%

Troubleshoots, tests, and stabilizes modernized applications, code libraries, integrations, and runtime environments; identifies defects, resolves performance or service issues, and validates that modernized components meet functional, security, and operational requirements. 15%

Prepares modernization documentation, domain models, current-state and target-state architecture mappings, technical flowcharts, AI-assisted analysis findings, and implementation guidance; provides consultation to architects, engineers, security, cloud, data, AI, and program teams to align modernization work with enterprise standards and business needs. 10%

Supports modernization governance by promoting domain-driven design, secure coding, DevSecOps practices, responsible use of AI-assisted development tools, cloud readiness, quality standards, reusable patterns, and compliance with agency technology and architecture standards. 5%

Performs other duties as assigned. 5%

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities (KSAs):

  • Knowledge:
    • Thorough knowledge of enterprise application modernization practices, domain-driven design, legacy system assessment, technical debt reduction, modernization roadmaps, and AI-assisted modernization analysis.
    • Thorough knowledge of legacy enterprise computing frameworks, modern application frameworks, modular architecture, bounded contexts, domain services, API and service integration patterns, and cloud-ready design approaches.
    • Thorough knowledge of secure application development, OWASP Top 10 vulnerabilities, DevSecOps practices, CI/CD concepts, testing practices, responsible AI-assisted development practices, and approved technology standards.
    • Knowledge of translating legacy business rules, workflows, data dependencies, and domain concepts into modern technical requirements, domain models, and implementation designs.

    • Strong skill in applying domain-driven design concepts to refactor and rewrite legacy business logic into modular, maintainable, secure, AI-ready, and cloud-ready application components and services.
    • Strong skill in troubleshooting application defects, integration issues, performance constraints, runtime environments, and service-to-service communication errors.
    • Skill in using AI-assisted engineering tools responsibly to accelerate code understanding, pattern identification, documentation, modernization planning, and developer productivity while validating outputs for accuracy, security, and compliance.
  • Abilities:
    • Ability to develop modernization blueprints, domain models, technical documentation, architecture mappings, and implementation guidance that describe how legacy systems will transition to modern platforms.
    • Ability to translate legacy business processes, system behavior, and domain concepts into clear technical requirements, design options, integration patterns, modernization work items, and services aligned to business capabilities.
    • Ability to collaborate with architects, engineers, security, cloud, data, AI, vendor, and program teams; provide technical guidance; and support modernization decisions during planning and implementation.

None

  • Minimum of 4 years of experience in enterprise systems refactoring, legacy migration, or application modernization.

title: Director of Facilities
description:
The Indianapolis Zoo is seeking a Director of Facilities to join our team! Bring your expertise in facilities management, project leadership and team development to the Indianapolis Zoo, where the work behind the scenes helps create unforgettable experiences and advances our mission to protect nature and inspire people to care for our world.


About the Role

The Indianapolis Zoo is seeking a Director of Facilities to lead our Facilities, Life Support (Aquatic Engineering), and Energy Management teams. This role oversees the maintenance, reliability, and long-term performance of the Zoo's buildings, equipment, utilities, and infrastructure, with an emphasis on preventative maintenance, asset management, and continuous improvement.

Working collaboratively with leaders across the organization, the Director of Facilities guides complex projects, manages departmental budgets, supports regulatory compliance, and develops strategies to maintain safe, efficient, and reliable operations across our campus. This is an opportunity for an experienced leader to make a lasting impact on the infrastructure that supports our animals, guests, and team members. This is a full-time, 40 hours per week position. Due to the nature of facilities operations, the Director must be available on call 24 hours a day and may work evenings, weekends, holidays, and overtime as needed to support emergencies and peak-season operations.


Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the Facilities, Life Support (Aquatic Engineering), and Energy Management departments, supporting managers, prioritizing work, and strengthening preventative maintenance programs.
  • Oversee annual maintenance and infrastructure projects, coordinating procurement, contractor bidding, and contract development with internal partners.
  • Manage facilities asset records, building plans, equipment inventories, warranties, and the Zoo's Energy Management System.
  • Develop and monitor annual operating budgets and business plans while contributing to capital budget planning and long-range infrastructure strategies.
  • Promote a culture of safety, ensuring facilities operations, procedures, and protocols align with applicable regulatory requirements and safety standards.
  • Lead and develop departmental managers and team members, fostering collaboration, accountability, and continuous improvement.
  • Maintain emergency readiness and coordinate facilities support during severe weather, snow and ice events, and other operational emergencies.
  • Partner with departments across the Zoo to support campus operations, special events, and projects that contribute to the overall guest and team member experience.

What We're Looking For

  • At least seven (7) years of professional experience in facilities management, construction management, or a related field.
  • At least five (5) years of experience supervising direct reports, with a demonstrated ability to lead and manage teams successfully.
  • A bachelor's degree from an accredited college or university in Project Management, Construction Management, or a related field preferred.
  • Working knowledge of HVAC, plumbing, electrical systems, and carpentry, along with strong mechanical aptitude and the ability to read blueprints.
  • Broad knowledge of project management, general trades, preventative maintenance programs, and asset management.
  • Strong problem-solving, organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to collaborate effectively with department leaders and other internal partners.
  • Familiarity with motor and small engine repair is helpful; an engineering background is highly desirable.
  • A valid Indiana driver's license and a driving record that meets the Zoo's insurability requirements, or the ability to obtain an Indiana driver's license within 30 days of employment.

Why Join Us?

At the Indianapolis Zoo, your leadership helps support a place where people connect with wildlife and are inspired to protect the natural world. Join a collaborative team where your expertise will help maintain essential infrastructure, support animal care and guest experiences, and contribute to a mission that reaches far beyond our campus.

Employment at the Indianapolis Zoo is contingent upon the successful completion of pre-employment testing including a background check, motor vehicle check (if applicable) and a drug test.

title: 3rd Shift Mold Technician-D
description:
NOW HIRING: Setup / Mold Technicians – 3rd Shift

Hoffer Plastics Corporation

Starting Pay: $22.00–$24.00/hr (based on experience)

Shift Premium: +8% for 3rd shift

3rd Shift Hours: 12:00am–8:00am

Want to be part of something special? We're filling important jobs!

Join an industry leader and innovator looking for people who want to make a difference. If you're mechanically minded and want to build a real skilled trade in plastic injection molding, we want to meet you.

Why You'll Love Working Here

  • 8% shift premium: Earn extra on top of your base pay for working 3rd shift
  • Clear career path: Advance through leveled training from Level C to Level A, with pay that grows with your skills
  • Get trained: Full training on molding, setup, processing and new technology
  • Great benefits: Medical, dental, vision, 401(k) match and more
  • Stability: An established, growing third-generation U.S. company

The Role

As a Setup / Mold Technician, you'll mold parts to meet internal and external customer requirements, including machine setup, auxiliary equipment setup and process parameter input. You'll also keep a neat and orderly work area to 5S standards and follow safety policies. The position is divided into four classifications based on skill set and responsibility, and pay is determined accordingly.

Responsibilities vary based on skill level and experience:

Level C:

  • Complete the B level training curriculum while at Level C.
  • Perform mold setups and color changes to meet production demands.
  • Set molding process parameters with the help of a foreman, supervisor, or A or B level molding technician.
  • Monitor production for accuracy and efficiency and work with quality inspectors to identify defects.
  • Perform material handler duties as assigned.

Level B:

  • Complete the A level training curriculum while at Level B.
  • Set molding process parameters to ensure part quality.
  • Troubleshoot process, machine and auxiliary equipment problems and make necessary changes to ensure quality and reduce downtime.
  • Learn new technology as it's brought into manufacturing.
  • Work with the supervisor and/or Lead Molding Technician to find ways to improve productivity and reduce scrap, defects, etc.

Level A:

  • Work with quality inspectors to identify defects and make good decisions on process changes.
  • Sample new and existing molds.
  • Stay current with new technology in molding, auxiliary equipment, robots, etc.
  • Promote safety by following all related policies and procedures and setting a good example for others.
  • Help maintain 5S and plant cleanliness by completing assigned cleaning tasks and setting a good example for others.
  • Take on the responsibilities of the supervisor or foreman in their absence.

All team members shall:

  • Maintain a positive work atmosphere by communicating in a way that helps you get along with customers, clients, co-workers and management.
  • Continue to grow job-specific knowledge and use tools to identify and assist with continuous improvement.
  • Comply with safety regulations and maintain clean and orderly work areas.

This job description does not contain every function or responsibility that may be required in the performance of this job. All team members are required to perform other related duties and functions as assigned.

What You Bring

  • High school diploma or GED required.
  • Ability and interest in successfully progressing through the leveled Molding Technician training curriculum.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and math proficiency.
  • Proficiency in reading and writing English.
  • Computer proficiency.

Benefits

  • Medical, Dental & Vision: Blue Cross Blue Shield medical and dental, VSP vision
  • 401(k): Hoffer Plastics matches $0.50 per $1.00 contributed each payroll period, up to 6%, plus a Safe Harbor contribution equal to 3% of annual eligible earnings
  • Paid Life Insurance: 1.5 times basic annual salary
  • Short-Term and Long-Term Disability
  • Time Off: 2 weeks paid vacation, up to 5 days of Illinois Paid Leave, and 9 paid holidays
  • Reimbursements: tuition, prescription safety glasses, steel toe shoes, and fitness

Physical Requirements

The incumbent will:

  • Usually stand / walk most of the shift.
  • Frequently bend at waist, twist, kneel / crouch, climb ladders and climb up on machinery with proper fall protection.
  • Occasionally push, pull and lift up to 75 lbs. or more.
  • Occasionally lift above waist and/or shoulder up to 75 lbs. and over.
  • Sometimes perform hand / wrist / finger movements and foot movements for pedal controls on forklift.
  • Occasionally perform keyboarding and squeezing movements.
  • Be frequently exposed to odors, dust and oil / grease.

Hoffer Plastics Corporation: There's a part of us in Every Piece.

title: Marine Fire Systems Technician
description:
Marine Fire Systems Technician

Atlantic Canada | D&L Engineering – An Everguard Company



Put your skills to work where safety matters most.


If you’re an experienced fire protection, fire alarm, mechanical, or electrical technician with a strong safety mindset and hands-on approach, this is an opportunity to build your career in a specialized marine environment.


D&L Engineering is a national leader in fire and life safety services across commercial, industrial, and marine environments. We’re looking for a Marine Fire Systems Technician to inspect, test, service, troubleshoot, and maintain critical fire protection and life safety systems aboard vessels, in shipyards, and across marine facilities.



Why Work with D&L?

  • Competitive Pay & Overtime – Real earnings with premiums for on-call, overtime, travel, and special projects paid on top of your base wage.
  • Benefits that support you – Health, dental, vision, life & disability, employer-matched RRSP, paid holidays (Birthday, Vacation and Statutory), flex-time, and Employee & Family Assistance Program.
  • Marine experience that builds your career – Develop specialized skills working with marine fire suppression, detection, and alarm systems across vessels and marine environments.
  • Supportive, Safety-First Culture – Modern tools, equipment, and procedures; a team environment where safety, quality, and compliance come first.
  • Stable work with variety – Work across vessels, ports, shipyards, and marine facilities, with opportunities to take on increasingly complex technical assignments.
  • Training & professional growth – We invest helping you develop your skills across multiple fire protection disciplines through hands-on experience, ongoing training, and long-term career opportunities.



What You’ll Do

You’ll be responsible for maintaining critical fire protection and life safety systems in marine environments, including:

  • Inspect, test, service, troubleshoot, repair, and maintain marine fire fire protection and life safety systems aboard vessels at marine facilities.
  • Service and test fixed suppression systems, portable fire extinguishers, and related equipment.
  • Perform functional testing and diagnose mechanical and electrical faults in system components.
  • Complete preventative maintenance, repairs, component replacements, upgrades, and commissioning.
  • Develop and apply skills across both suppression and detection and alarm systems through hands-on experience and cross-training.
  • Verify system operation and identify deficiencies that could affect vessel safety, system performance, or regulatory compliance.
  • Ensure work complies with Transport Canada, Canadian Coast Guard, NFPA, manufacturer, and marine safety requirements.
  • Complete inspection reports, service records, certifications, work orders, and compliance documentation.
  • Communicate deficiencies, findings, repairs, and recommendations to customers and vessel personnel.
  • Assist with estimating, quoting, and identifying service and repair opportunities.
  • Follow marine site safety procedures and maintain a clean, organized work environment.
  • Travel to vessels, ports, shipyards, and customer sites and participate in on-call rotations as required.


This role combines hands-on technical work, troubleshooting, marine safety, customer interaction, and independent problem-solving in an environment where your work directly supports the safety of people and vessels. You’ll have the opportunity to broaden your technical capabilities across multiple fire protection systems while contributing directly to the safety of people, vessels, and marine operations.



What You Bring

  • 2+ years of field experience in fire protection, fire suppression, fire alarm, mechanical, electrical, HVAC, or a related trade.
  • Experience servicing or inspecting fire protection systems; marine or shipyard experience is an asset.
  • Strong mechanical aptitude and comfort with basic electrical troubleshooting.

title: Senior Political Intelligence Consultant (Business, Culture, and Technology), and Team Leader
location: London, London, City of, United Kingdom
description:
About the role


If you’re passionate about policy and politics, you’ll fit right in to our enthusiastic and vibrant team.


This position is for the portfolio of Business, Culture, and Technology which covers the department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade, and the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport and overlapping areas across government policy. Applications should refer to the role and detail any relevant policy expertise in these areas.


This is an exciting opportunity to become part of a highly-respected political intelligence team, providing market-leading intelligence services to ensure our clients stay ahead of political developments. We provide fast, focused, and comprehensive information and insight on the activities of legislatures, government, and a variety of stakeholders to clients across a wide range of sectors. In a time of political turmoil, keeping our clients constantly informed is a dynamic challenge.


You’ll be part of a team of fellow consultants, each of whom are experts in their respective policy areas, and will be providing finger-on-the-pulse analysis to your clients on a daily basis.


You will also have responsibility for managing a small team, providing day-to-day guidance and support, coordinating workloads and ensuring the delivery of high-quality, timely political intelligence to clients. We are looking for evidence of previous management experience in your application.


You will work towards becoming a respected authority within the industry on all issues relating to your specialist policy area and key stakeholders, with the potential opportunity to write articles for media publications and participate in broadcasting and panel discussions.


This role is based at our London office in Borough. Colleagues spend some of their working week in the office and some days working from home (usually 2-3 days in the office per week).


What are we looking for?


Our ideal candidate will have:


  • A strong grasp of the key issues within the portfolio and the ability to develop a thorough, in-depth understanding of its priorities,
  • An excellent understanding of parliamentary procedure, government policy and the UK political landscape.
  • A keen interest in politics and policy, and excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Some relevant client-facing experience.
  • Demonstrable experience of managing or supporting a small team, with the ability to provide guidance, coordinate workloads and support colleagues to deliver high-quality work to tight deadlines.
  • Experience of giving feedback, setting objectives or supporting the development of colleagues.
  • Excellent attention to detail and commitment to accuracy, while working quickly and to tight deadlines.
  • The ability to analyse large amounts of information at pace in a rapidly changing political environment.
  • The ability to prioritise multiple tasks and manage workloads.
  • A proactive approach, with the confidence to hit the ground running.
  • A professional attitude, enjoyment of working with both clients and colleagues, and the ability to show initiative and commercial awareness.
  • The ability to work well within a team but also take initiative when required.
  • IT literacy and confidence in using online applications to support your work.
  • A relevant degree-level qualification or relevant professional experience.


Key responsibilities


You will:


  • Provide a first-rate political intelligence service to your own portfolio of clients, including timely, high-quality political insight and research.
  • Contribute to the development of our business through the delivery of successful trial periods with prospective clients.
  • Manage a small team of consultants, providing day-to-day guidance and support, overseeing workloads and ensuring the consistent delivery of timely, accurate and high-quality political intelligence to clients.
  • Hold regular one-to-ones with your team, set clear objectives and review performance against them, recognising good work and raising problems early.
  • Coach and develop team members, supporting their policy expertise, client skills and career progression.
  • Set and maintain standards for the accuracy, timeliness and quality of your team’s work, and check that they are met.
  • Make sure work across the team has clear ownership and deadlines, including cover when colleagues are out of the office.
  • Pass client feedback, renewal risks and new opportunities on to the Account Management and commercial teams.
  • Lead by example in the quality of your own client work.


What’s it like to work with us?


At Dods we focus on our 3C’s: Collaboration, Continuous improvement, and Customers. We live these values by offering employees opportunities to further their skills through learning and development and training, plenty of opportunities to connect across teams to network, socialise and volunteer, and by always keeping the customer at the forefront. Our inclusive culture means there are always room for new ideas, opportunities to be creative and continuous improvement.


Situated in the heart of London, the office working environment is collaborative, bright and airy with everyone together in one space. There’s always a bit of a buzz and conversation going on, and people like to chat and help each other. The office is small enough that everyone knows everyone’s name, so colleagues work across teams on shared projects.


We prize initiative and creativity in how you best provide intelligence to your hugely diverse range of clients. We invest in our consultant’s expertise and will support you in gaining new skills with dedicated funding for your learning and development.


We’ve provided political intelligence for 190 years, and while we’re looking into how to leverage artificial intelligence, we know that it’s still our people and how we support our customers personally that makes us different. Work can be fast-paced – there’s an expectation that a customer can get straight through to their Consultant or Account Manager to ask a question and get a quick answer. This means that if a colleague is out-of-office, we cover for each other. It’s a very engaging environment to work in, and while it can be busy, you know that there are always great colleagues around to support you.


About Dods Group Ltd


Dods is a leading political intelligence business covering Westminster and the UK’s devolved parliaments. Organisations have been turning to us for pertinent information on what’s going on in Government since we first published the Dods Parliamentary Companion way back in 1832. We provide clients across the corporate, government and charity sectors with insight, intelligence and impact through our comprehensive suite of policy tools.


  • Intelligence - Dods Monitoring – our platform offers real-time alerts, diaries and legislative trackers, inhouse parliamentary coverage, and a powerful historical search function of policy information.
  • Insight - Dods Consultancy – our sector-specialist consultants provide analysis, bespoke research, and impartial guidance on the latest policy developments and trends.
  • Impact - Dods People – our constantly updated database of biographical and contact information for UK parliamentarians, the digital version of the original who’s who in politics established in 1832, enables you to identify and address the right policymaking audience.


For further information, please visit:


Why choose Dods?


We are proud of the inclusive culture we have built at Dods. Our team are passionate about what they do, and we are passionate about supporting them to be their best. We understand the importance of work-life balance and offer a flexible, hybrid working environment so you can choose how and where to work. Celebrating diversity and inclusion is also an important aspect of our culture and we often have social events to bring everyone together. Here’s some more information on our benefits and ways of working:


Employee Benefits


  • 25 days annual leave plus your birthday off, with the option to buy an additional 5 days holiday per year.
  • Our approach to work is agile and the team currently spend some of their working week at home and in our office in Borough. We also offer the option to work from anywhere for up to 4 weeks a year.
  • Flexible working, including 4pm finish on Fridays and early finish throughout the summer holiday period so you can spend more time with your family and friends.
  • Opportunities to connect across teams and locations to network, socialise and volunteer.
  • Our inclusive culture means there are always room for new ideas, opportunities to be creative and continuous improvement.
  • Continuous learning and development opportunities throughout your journey with us.
  • Life assurance: we hope you will never need this, but our cover is for 4 times your salary to your beneficiaries.
  • Enhanced maternity and paternity leave options.
  • Company Pension Scheme.
  • Discounted Gym Membership.
  • Cycle to work and season ticket travel loan scheme.
  • In-year employee bonus scheme.
  • Employee assistance programme.


How to apply


If you are interested in the role, please submit a copy of your CV and Cover Letter setting out why you are a good fit for the role through our Company Careers Page Careers | Dods Group Ltd. The closing date for applications is 9am on Friday 6th November 2026 with interviews to be held week commencing 16th and 23rd November. Please note that if we receive a high number of applications, we may interview on a rolling basis or close the vacancy early, so please do apply as soon as possible.


Ideal start date: December 2026, but we will allow a later start date for the right candidate.


We recognise that many candidates now use AI tools to support their applications, and we are comfortable with this where used appropriately. However, we kindly ask that you do not rely heavily on AI-generated responses. We are genuinely keen to hear your authentic voice, experience and skills, and to understand what you would bring to the role.


As part of your application, you will need to demonstrate that you have the Right to Work in the UK. We are unable to provide visa sponsorship.

Aertrip is redefining the future of travel through AI-driven innovation. We leverage cutting-edge AI/ML, Large Language Models (LLMs), and Agentic AI systems to build intelligent, multimodal, and deeply intuitive travel experiences.

Our AI ecosystem integrates voice, text, visual interfaces, and automation, combining both commercial and open-source technologies to deliver exceptional user experiences at scale. At Aertrip, we are building the next generation of AI-powered travel platforms that impact millions of users.

Role Overview :

We are looking for a hands-on AI Prompt Architect who will design, optimize, and deploy advanced prompt strategies and AI agent workflows. This role focuses on selecting the right LLMs for the right tasks, building collaborative AI agents, and ensuring fast, accurate, and user-friendly outcomes across Aertrip's AI products.

You will work closely with engineering, product, and design teams to ship production-ready AI solutions and MVPs rapidly.

- Prompt Engineering & LLM Optimization

- Design, craft, and refine high-quality prompts for LLMs such as ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, DeepSeek, LLaMA, and others

- Optimize prompts for accuracy, performance, and cost-efficiency

- Evaluate and select LLMs based on task suitability, latency, scalability, and output quality

- Agentic AI Architecture

- Build a Master AI Agent capable of breaking down user queries and routing them to specialized agents (Flights, Hotels, Booking, Support, etc.)

- Design and implement a Quality Analyzer Agent to validate outputs against user intent, ensure correctness, and reroute tasks when required

- Continuously improve agent workflows for speed, accuracy, and reliability

- Multimodal & User Experience Integration

- Enable multilingual capabilities using third-party plugins and language tools

- Integrate visual AI assistants (e.g., Tavus.io) to enhance user interaction

- Enable GUI + AI fusion, allowing AI agents to visually interact with on-screen elements and workflows

- System & Data Integration

- Connect LLMs with internal databases, APIs, and tools to provide context-aware and personalized responses

- Work with vector databases and retrieval systems to improve AI grounding and relevance

Required Skills & Qualifications :

- 2+ years of experience working with AI, LLMs, or automation systems

- Strong programming skills in Python with experience in APIs and backend integrations

- Hands-on experience with prompt engineering, LLM orchestration, and evaluation

- Familiarity with LangChain, vector databases, embeddings, and retrieval-based systems

- Strong problem-solving mindset and ability to ship MVPs quickly

- Passion for AI, automation, and real-world applications

title: Project Executive
description:

  • High level of character and integrity, essential for guiding the team toward successful business plans.
  • Experience in monitoring, evaluating, and projecting projects based on job cost reports and site observations.
  • Demonstrates strong commercial judgement and executive maturity in executing the Project Executive role and interacting with other executives at the firm.

Licenses/Certifications:

Professional certification in field of expertise preferred (State Electrical License, Project Management Institute, RCDD, etc.)

-401k Program w/ Direct Benefit

title: APPLIED AI ENGINEER
location: Johannesburg or Cape Town, Gauteng or Western Cape, South Africa
description:
WHY THIS ROLE EXISTS


Helm builds intelligent multilingual conversational assistants for major African enterprise brands. The Applied AI team is the intelligence layer behind these assistants, building and maintaining services that leverage natural language understanding, intelligent document processing, retrieval-augmented generation, and all things generative AI.


We need someone who can build production AI services and keep them running well. That means writing solid code, designing systems that hold up under real-world conditions, implementing safety and guardrails, and being rigorous about understanding when and why things go wrong. You will own services end-to-end and make architectural decisions that directly affect how enterprise clients experience our AI. You will have real ownership from early on. This is not a role where you just execute tickets, you make decisions about how services are designed, built, and operated.


WHAT YOU WILL DO

Build and operate production GenAI services. Implement LLM-powered services from architecture through to production, prompt management, provider abstraction, structured output, cost controls. The Head of Applied AI works with you to set architectural direction. You own implementation, deployment, and evolution of these services over time. As models and techniques advance, you stay close to what's changing and make grounded calls on what to adopt.

Improve retrieval systems. Work on retrieval-augmented generation, improving retrieval pipelines, response quality, diagnostics, and integration with the broader platform. Make these systems observable and systematically improvable.

Implement responsible AI practices. Content filtering, prompt injection protection, PII handling, output validation, guardrails. These are engineering problems, not checkboxes. You build them as first-class concerns in every service.

Extend observability for GenAI. Traditional monitoring doesn't cut it for LLM-based systems. You will build telemetry that tracks token costs, latency, output quality, and agent behaviour, so the team knows how systems are performing, not just whether they're up.

Drive error analysis. When something goes wrong, we need to understand why, not just patch it. You will build and contribute to systematic error analysis workflows that turn failures into actionable improvements. This is how we get better, and it's non-negotiable.

Strengthen shared infrastructure. Logging, configuration management, deployment automation, error handling. You improve the tooling and patterns that the whole team relies on.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

First 3 Months

You understand the platform, the integration patterns, and the constraints. You've shipped real improvements to existing services, not just read the code. You've formed a view on where the biggest engineering leverage is and started acting on it.

3–9 Months

You've built and shipped at least one GenAI service into production with multi-tenancy, safety layer, and cost controls. Retrieval systems have better diagnostics and clearer integration patterns. Responsible AI checks are in place. You've improved shared infrastructure in ways that benefit the whole team, not just your own work.

9–12 Months

You own one or more production services end-to-end. GenAI observability is operational, the team can see what's happening, what it costs, and where it breaks. You're contributing to architectural decisions and influencing technical direction. You can evaluate new GenAI capabilities critically and recommend what's worth pursuing.

Beyond 12 Months

You're contributing to the evolution toward agentic workflows - bounded AI systems operating under clear constraints. You're helping shape how AI-assisted orchestration fits into the platform. You're mentoring new team members and your influence on system design extends across the function. The trajectory is toward senior engineering ownership, though that's about growing scope and impact, not a guaranteed title change on a schedule.

REQUIREMENTS

Required

  • Strong Python skills, with experience building production APIs and services (not primarily notebooks).
  • Experience deploying containerised services on cloud infrastructure.
  • Ability to reason about system architecture, API design, and production trade-offs.
  • Practical experience with GenAI and LLM integration, prompt engineering, RAG, or model serving. You don't need to be a data scientist, but you need to understand how these systems work and how they fail.
  • Comfortable working autonomously with high ownership in a small team.
  • Genuine interest in evaluation, error analysis, and responsible AI, not just feature shipping.

Valuable

  • Experience with LLM provider APIs and patterns for abstraction, cost management, and reliability.
  • Experience building observability and monitoring for production services.
  • Familiarity with FastAPI, async Python, or similar frameworks.
  • Experience in multi-tenant environments serving diverse clients.

TEAM AND ENGINEERING CULTURE

We value measurable impact over activity, ownership over participation, and honest assessment over optimistic reporting. We build for production, not for demos. Engineers own real systems and are expected to think critically about trade-offs. We come from diverse technical backgrounds and respect what each person brings, but we hold each other to a high standard on engineering quality.

Learning is part of how we work. We protect time for disciplined research, short cycles with clear questions and defined exit criteria. Curiosity matters, but so does accountability.

title: Senior Technical Program Manager (18 Month Contract)
description:
The Senior Technical Program Manager (STPM) reports to the Director, Technical Program Management. The STPM owns end-to-end plan management and delivery execution for highly complex technical programs across EQ Bank's Digital Banking ecosystem, with a strong emphasis on measurable business value, customer outcomes, reliability, and usability.

The STPM leads execution across multiple interdependent teams and domains, proactively surfaces technical and non-technical risks, establishes mitigation plans, manages complex dependencies, drives decisions, and enables alignment across Engineering, Product, Business, Enterprise partners, and third parties. The STPM applies company policies and Enterprise Change Management requirements while balancing governance with modern product and technology delivery practices.

The STPM operates effectively where scope, ownership, or the delivery path is ambiguous. The role is expected to build strong cross-functional relationships, influence senior stakeholders without authority, resolve escalated delivery constraints, and provide clear executive-level visibility of program health, trade-offs, and decisions.

Main Activities:

  • Establish integrated, outcome-focused execution plans for highly complex programs spanning multiple teams, systems, or business domains.
  • Own delivery from initiation through implementation, maintaining a single source of truth for outcomes, scope, milestones, decisions, risks, dependencies, and program health.
  • Proactively identify and manage complex technical and non-technical dependencies, including negotiation with Director-level and senior stakeholders to secure decisions, capacity, or priority alignment.
  • Anticipate and mitigate material risks and issues that could affect customer outcomes, regulatory commitments, operational readiness, or delivery objectives.
  • Lead program governance and Steering Committee forums, presenting clear options, trade-offs, recommendations, and decisions required.
  • Influence quarterly and roadmap planning by identifying cross-program dependencies, sequencing constraints, and delivery risks.
  • Mentor and support other Technical Program Managers through practical guidance, peer review, and knowledge sharing.
  • Contribute to the evolution of Technical Program Management standards, tools, and ways of working based on delivery experience.

Knowledge and Skill Requirements:

  • Demonstrated success delivering highly complex technology programs that support business objectives and customer outcomes.
  • Advanced business and technical acumen, with the ability to navigate complexity across systems, processes, organizations, and stakeholders.
  • Advanced collaboration, relationship-building, executive communication, influencing, and facilitation skills across all levels and functions.
  • Advanced analytical thinking and problem-solving skills, including the ability to structure ambiguous problems and drive timely decisions.
  • Strong knowledge of delivery governance, risk management, change management, controls, and implementation readiness for complex technology programs.
  • Ability to coach peers, raise delivery quality, and contribute to consistent Technical Program Management practices without direct authority.
  • Experience in the regulated Financial Services or Insurance industry is preferred.
  • Seven or more years of experience leading complex technology programs through the full product or software delivery lifecycle (PDLC or SDLC).

Accountability:

  • Own end-to-end plan management and delivery coordination for highly complex technical programs, including initiation, planning, execution, risk and dependency management, readiness, implementation, go-live, and transition activities.
  • Maintain an accurate, executive-ready source of truth for program health, outcomes, milestones, risks, issues, dependencies, decisions, and required actions.
  • Ensure stakeholders understand program goals, priorities, trade-offs, and decisions required to maintain progress.
  • Drive alignment and delivery discipline across multiple teams and organizational boundaries, resolving or escalating material constraints.
  • Lead governance forums and Steering Committees for assigned programs, ensuring decisions and accountabilities are clear and followed through.
  • Apply established standards and controls while recommending improvements that strengthen consistency, quality, and supportability of delivery practices.
  • Ensure effective change intake, risk, compliance, security, audit readiness, implementation readiness, and operational transition for assigned programs.
  • Provide practical mentoring and delivery leadership beyond assigned programs when needed.

title: SAP Security & GRC Consultant
description:
Yoda Tech is seeking an experienced SAP Security & GRC Consultant to provide Level 2 (L2) support for SAP security operations, access governance, and identity management in an enterprise environment.

The ideal candidate will have hands-on experience in SAP S/4HANA Security, SAP GRC Access Control, and SAP authorization management.

Knowledge of SAP Cloud Identity Services (CIS), Identity Authentication Service (IAS), and Identity Provisioning Service (IPS) will be an advantage.

The role involves user administration, role management, access risk analysis, compliance monitoring, identity provisioning, and troubleshooting security-related incidents while ensuring adherence to enterprise security policies and service-level agreements.

Key Responsibilities :

1. SAP Security Administration :

- Perform user administration activities, including user creation, modification, locking, unlocking, and deletion.

- Manage SAP authorization concepts across SAP landscapes.

- Design, develop, modify, and maintain single, composite, and derived roles.

- Troubleshoot authorization issues and resolve access-related incidents.

- Execute role assignments and transport security objects across development, testing, and production environments.

- Conduct security audits and compliance reviews to ensure adherence to access control policies.

2. SAP GRC Access Control :

- Support SAP GRC Access Control modules, including : Access Risk Analysis (ARA), Access Request Management (ARM), Emergency Access Management (EAM), and Business Role Management (BRM).

- Analyse Segregation of Duties (SoD) conflicts and recommend appropriate mitigation controls.

- Manage firefighter IDs and monitor emergency access activities.

- Review and maintain mitigating control documentation.

- Support access governance processes and compliance requirements.

3. SAP S/4HANA Security :

- Support SAP S/4HANA security implementation and operational activities.

- Manage SAP Fiori security, including catalogs, groups/spaces, pages, and business roles.

- Troubleshoot Fiori authorization issues using standard SAP tools.

- Support security requirements across SAP Fiori, SAP GUI, and embedded applications.

- Collaborate with business and functional teams to design secure access solutions.

4. SAP Cloud Identity Services - CIS / IAS / IPS :

- Support SAP Cloud Identity Services (CIS), including Identity Authentication Service (IAS) and Identity Provisioning Service (IPS).

- Troubleshoot Single Sign-On (SSO) and authentication issues involving SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect (OIDC).

- Support identity federation with Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD).

- Manage user provisioning and de-provisioning processes.

- Support identity integration with SAP SuccessFactors and SAP Ariba.

- Assist with identity lifecycle management and authentication-related access governance.

- Troubleshoot IAS/IPS synchronisation and provisioning issues.

5. Incident & Service Management :

- Handle L2 SAP security support tickets within defined service-level agreements (SLAs).

- Perform root cause analysis for recurring security issues and implement corrective actions.

- Coordinate with Level 3 support teams to resolve complex security incidents.

- Participate in system upgrades, patching, and project-related security activities.

- Maintain operational documentation and prepare security reports and dashboards.

title: Instructional Designer
description:
Position Summary

The Instructional Designer transforms organizational concepts, business processes, and operational workflows into engaging, learner-centered training experiences. This role is responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining e-learning modules, instructor-led training materials, and blended learning programs. All learning solutions must align with adult learning principles, enterprise standards, and the company's culture and branding.



Duties and Responsibilities


Curriculum Design and Development

  • Design and develop instructional materials, including interactive e-learning modules, job aids, lesson plans, and facilitator guides for instructor-led, virtual, and self-paced training.
  • Create clear, structured learning experiences that support employee development and operational effectiveness.

Instructional Strategy and Multimedia Integration

  • Apply established instructional design methodologies, including ADDIE and SAM, to develop effective learning solutions.
  • Use modern authoring tools and multimedia elements to create engaging, interactive content that improves learner participation and knowledge retention.

Subject Matter Expert (SME) Collaboration

  • Partner with internal subject matter experts, project leads, and stakeholders to translate technical information, operational procedures, and leadership standards into clear, accessible training materials.
  • Define learning objectives and ensure course content aligns with business needs and performance expectations.

Learning Technology and Content Development

  • Develop, publish, and maintain interactive learning modules using industry-standard tools, including Articulate 360, Microsoft Office, and Adobe Creative Cloud.
  • Ensure training materials are compatible with learning management systems (LMS) and cloud-based platforms.

Needs Analysis and Assessment

  • Conduct training needs assessments to identify learning gaps and development opportunities.
  • Create knowledge checks, quizzes, and practical assessments to evaluate learner comprehension, training effectiveness, and knowledge application.

Branding and Content Standards

  • Ensure all training materials, visual assets, and instructional documentation follow FDOT and Florida’s Turnpike Enterprise branding and style guidelines.
  • Maintain a consistent, professional look and feel across all learning materials.

Cloud and Asset Management

  • Organize, maintain, and version-control course files, source materials, media assets, and published training packages within secure cloud storage environments.
  • Maintain accurate documentation and ensure learning assets are accessible and organized for future updates.

Quality Assurance and Prototyping

  • Develop course storyboards, prototypes, and pilot materials to validate instructional approaches before full deployment.
  • Gather stakeholder and learner feedback, test course functionality, and make revisions to improve usability and effectiveness.

Project Management and Stakeholder Communication

  • Manage instructional design projects from initial planning through development, testing, and deployment.
  • Track project milestones, manage competing priorities, meet established deadlines, and provide regular status updates to leadership and stakeholders.

Continuous Improvement

  • Research and incorporate emerging trends in instructional design, learning technology, and adult learning principles.
  • Identify opportunities to improve training content, delivery methods, and the overall learning experience.



Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Strong knowledge of instructional design theories, adult learning principles, and curriculum development methodologies.
  • Demonstrated experience with e-learning authoring tools, including Articulate 360, Microsoft Office, and Adobe Creative Cloud.
  • Understanding of user experience (UX) principles as they apply to digital learning interfaces and virtual training platforms.
  • Ability to collaborate with subject matter experts and translate complex technical or operational information into clear, engaging learning content.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications for documentation, presentations, and instructional material development.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects, prioritize tasks, and meet deadlines.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including instructional writing and the ability to tailor content to diverse audiences.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a collaborative learning and development team.
  • Strong attention to detail, problem-solving skills, and a commitment to producing high-quality training materials.


Position Requirements


Education

Bachelor’s degree in Instructional Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Education, or a related field, or equivalent relevant work experience.


Experience

A minimum of three years of experience in training, including instructional content development and training delivery.

title: Operations Advisor
description:
Date: October 29, 2026

Location: Mississauga, ON – On-site

Requisition ID: 21354

Status: Regular

Business Unit: Markets and Reliability

Grade/Band: MP4

Shift Work:

Annual Pay Range: For standard 35-hour work week

Step 1: $111,072 to Step 10: $158,704

The successful candidate will be placed at the appropriate step within the salary grade/band, based on relevant years of experience and other applicable considerations.

Why join us?

The IESO is committed to ensuring Ontario’s electricity system meets the province’s needs today and into the future. We are charged with purpose, delivering reliable, affordable, and sustainable electricity for homes, businesses, and communities across the province. We are energized to grow, embracing opportunities to shape the future of a dynamic and evolving energy sector while advancing our careers. We are powered by teamwork, supported by diverse and passionate colleagues who foster respect, celebrate successes, and thrive on shared achievements. At the IESO, it’s not just what we do—it’s who we are!

Who we are

Our central role includes managing the provincial power grid in real-time, overseeing and evolving Ontario’s electricity market, engaging with government, municipalities and Indigenous communities, and planning for Ontario’s future electricity needs. Our employees play a key role in driving grid innovation, protecting the system from threats, advancing the province’s energy conservation programs, and forecasting and procuring the electricity resources we’ll need in the decades to come.

This is a unionized position that falls within the Major Projects team with the Markets and Relaibility Business Unit.

What makes this role exciting

The energy sector is rapidly evolving, offering exciting new opportunities for those who want to make a difference.

As Ontario’s energy landscape evolves, the IESO is taking bold steps to modernize how major projects, from data centres to battery storage facilities and electric arc furnaces, connect to the grid. The IESO is launching a new Project Management Framework bring greater rigour, accountability, and customer focus to the connection process. This shift is about more than executing a process, it’s about supporting customers, enabling innovation and ensuring continued reliability, while delivering important economic growth within the province. If you thrive on leading complex projects, tackling meaningful challenges, and want to help shape the future of Ontario’s energy infrastructure, this is your opportunity to make a real impact.

  • Shape the future of Ontario’s grid by driving complex, high-impact projects from concept to implementation, turning strategic priorities into tangible operational outcomes that advance the energy transition.
  • Collaborate with some of the brightest minds across engineering, operations, IT, and market development to align decisions, remove barriers, and keep major initiatives moving forward.
  • Influence real change in real time by applying disciplined project leadership, seeing your work directly shape how new technologies, market rules, and grid connections come online.
  • Own the momentum; lead critical conversations, navigate complexity, and make decisions that enable Ontario’s evolving energy system to stay reliable, resilient, and ready for what’s next.


What you’ll do

In this role, you’ll make a meaningful impact by contributing to the IESO team and supporting the electricity needs of the province through:

  • Coordinate the overall authorization process for participation in IESO-administered markets and/or programs with internal IESO business units and organizations seeking such participation.
  • Coordinate the overall “facility registration lifecycle” with internal IESO business units and external participants. This responsibility includes:
    • Facilitate the registration, maintenance and de-registration of physical facilities for IESO-administered markets or programs.
    • Review connection assessment documentation, market rules, market manuals and converse with subject matter experts to develop registration requirements for facilities.
    • Following up customer issues to expedite their resolution within the IESO. Engage with subject matter experts and customers to achieve an acceptable resolution.
  • Support system operations by managing and maintaining the registration system, resolving issues related to registered data, and coordinating master data as a centralized resource for the IESO. Provide specifications for tool enhancements to ensure data accuracy and operational readiness.
  • Maintain knowledge of market rules for the purposes of identifying the obligations. Provide customers and others in the IESO with updates, interpretations and impacts as needed.
  • Issue approval documentation to the participant and within the IESO on recommended decisions pertaining to participation or physical facilities.
  • Provide coordination, technical leadership and business systems expertise to internal and external customer projects and system changes.
    • Represent Operations for items arising from IT change and release management.
    • Identify the objectives of business processes, assess the risk of not meeting those objectives and identify process controls to mitigate risk as appropriate.
    • Document process objectives, tasks, risks and controls in summary documentation (e.g. risk-control matrices).
    • Make recommendations and implement changes on streamlining tasks and procedures. Contribute to the enhancement/development of existing/new business processes, training packages or guides for participants.
  • Support process improvements and document management within Operations by preparing, maintaining, and delivering guides and IESO-controlled documents in alignment with business needs and regulatory requirements. Facilitate the baseline process and maintain an inventory of Operations documentation.
  • Exercise informal resource management over assigned staff and provide limited training to staff as needed.
  • Provide support to reliability organizations (NERC and NPCC).
  • Perform other duties as required

In a typical day, you will:

  • Coordinate the planning and delivery of complex, cross-functional initiatives impacting Operations, ensuring alignment with organizational priorities and system reliability objectives.
  • Drive structured project execution through clear governance, defined scope, risk management, and disciplined delivery practices that support operational readiness.
  • Guide cross-functional teams and advisors by providing direction, integrating technical and operational requirements, and ensuring accountability across all project stages.
  • Champion effective stakeholder engagement and change management strategies to enable seamless implementation and adoption of operational changes.
  • Enhance project management practices, tools, and frameworks within Operations Integration to continuously strengthen delivery and integration capabilities.

Role Requirements

Our team consists of experts from diverse backgrounds, each bringing their unique perspectives and skills.
To succeed in this role, you’ll need:

  • Requires lengthy exposure to the overall power system operation through progressive training in an appropriate technical field.
  • Requires specific experience as applicable to the particular specialty of the group.
  • Experience will be related to the fields of:
    • Registration of energy resources for Market Operations
    • Secure operation of bulk power system
    • Technical and non-technical requirements of IESO operational needs, and an understanding of participant capability


Background experience will include:

    • Electrical equipment design concepts as they relate to the functions and characteristics of power system components
    • Familiarity with power system and market operation, practices, and policies
    • Familiarity with IESO’s markets, practices, policies, and market rules
    • Project Management
  • Requires experience in dealing with customers (internal & external to the IESO) in a professional and service focused environment. Requires experience to effectively deal with complex inquiries as well as sensitive situations. Experience with diffusing irate callers by utilizing various soft skill techniques is essential.
  • Requires some experience in methods of discovery and or investigation, which involves having good analytical, reasoning and customer relations skills to resolve related problems or sensitive questions.
  • Requires experience in a customer service environment. Should be familiar with various customer-service related responsibilities, functions and their interrelationships, and with the contacts and sources of information involved.
  • Requires project manager skills to successfully manage registration requirements.
  • A period of over 6 years and up to and including 8 years is considered necessary to gain this experience.

How We Support You

From a comprehensive total rewards program to dynamic learning and development opportunities—including job rotations to broaden your expertise—we empower you to define and shape your own success. When you join the IESO, here’s what you can expect:

  • Best-in-class benefits and long-term support in the form of a defined benefit pension plan.
  • Work in a dynamic and evolving sector that offers exciting opportunities and the chance to explore new career paths.
  • Leadership that values meaningful discussions, welcomes feedback, and prioritizes career development.
  • A strong, inclusive culture and a collaborative team environment with a shared passion for impactful work.
  • Compensation packages that are regularly reviewed to remain competitive and to best accommodate the diverse needs of our employees.


Deadline

November 19, 2026. For future reference, please save a copy of the job posting as it will no longer be available once the posting closes.

Thank you for your interest in a career at the IESO. Only candidates selected for an interview will be contacted. Please note that the successful candidate must be legally eligible to work in Canada and will be subject to applicable background checks.

IESO will not conduct interviews or offer positions via online, text, chat or social media platforms. We will not gather personal information directly from candidates or potential candidates. Selected candidates will work with our Talent Acquisition team to ensure their application is processed.

The IESO currently has a 3-day in-office work week for applicable roles. Over the course of 2026, the IESO will advance plans to acquire additional office space to accommodate more in-office time. While the timeline for moving to a full 5-day in-office model has not yet been established, we are committed to keeping employees and candidates informed as plans progress and give them as much advance notice as possible to prepare for any changes.

We believe in opportunities for everyone.

At the IESO, we know that achieving great results depends on embracing diversity by attracting, developing, and retaining people from a wide variety of backgrounds. We do this by ensuring our recruitment and advancement policies are fair and equitable, and by creating an accessible and inclusive environment—one that values every team member’s unique skills and experiences and ensures they have the support they need to achieve their potential. If you require accommodation during the recruitment process, please let us know. We’re proud to say we’ve been recognized as a supportive, inclusive employer.

Be sure to follow us on LinkedIn.

Consultant is the level at which colleagues work autonomously to take forward substantial work packages, with guidance and support from their engagement leads. They have a strong core consulting skillset and can confidently prepare high quality deliverables.

At least three days a week in our Farringdon HQ.

title: Strategic Alliances Manager
description:
Role Overview

Pexip is looking for a Strategic Alliances Manager to own the day-to-day execution of our alliance partnerships.
