This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who is equally comfortable in a partner's field sales call, a deal-desk discussion and a quarterly business review.


Key Responsibilities

  • Alliance execution. Own day-to-day management of Pexip's alliance community, including pipeline, forecast, renewals and deal progression.
  • Pipeline and deals. Drive joint pipeline generation and deal closure, working with and between Pexip and partner sellers; engage directly on opportunities, renewals and escalations.
  • Deal support and pricing. Lead commercial and discount discussions with key partners, including deal structuring, pricing alignment and deal-desk coordination, within the parameters agreed with the VP and escalating exceptions as needed
  • Operating rhythm. Run the alliance cadence: partner team calls, pipeline reviews and business reviews. Prepare QBR materials and follow up on actions.
  • Partner Enablement. Manage partner enablement for sales and technical teams, including training, sales plays, content and co-developed marketing assets, in partnership with Marketing and Sales Engineering.
  • Internal sales enablement. Coordinate and deliver enablement for Pexip's own sellers on new partner and marketplace initiatives, preparing training content and guides and presenting them on regular forums such as the monthly Connected Spaces team calls and the Global Business Development team cadence calls.
  • Field and events. Plan and execute partner webinars, events and partner-specific shows, such as annual partner conferences, with Marketing and other internal resources as required.
  • Digital marketplace execution. Own the execution of Pexip's Digital Marketplace strategy, including hands-on support for the initial enablement of our products on each Digital Marketplace, and day-to-day management of listings, private offers and marketplace transactions.
  • Marketplace incentives and co-sell. Become Pexip's subject matter expert on ISV incentive programs, maximizing their bottom-line contribution. Coach sellers on co-sell requirements, manage the reporting and admin needed to secure payments, and guide customers on what they must do to enable them.
  • Broader partner portfolio. Manage relationships and programs for new and emerging partners as they join, flexing the level of support to each partner's tier as agreed with the VP.
  • Partner operations. Oversee partner business operations, including deal registration, orders, invoicing and reconciliation, in partnership with Finance and BizOps.
  • Partner support. Coordinate partner-facing communication channels and be the first responder to partner questions from sellers, SEs and partner program teams.
  • Cross-functional partner. Bring partner and market feedback to Product, Marketing and Sales leadership, and support execution of the strategic initiatives the VP sets, including pricing and licensing programs, global GTM plays and BDR programs.


Qualifications

  • 5+ years in alliances, channel, partner sales or business development in enterprise software, SaaS or collaboration/UC technology.
  • Proven record of sourcing and closing partner-influenced revenue, with strong forecasting and pipeline discipline.
  • Experience managing relationships with large technology partners, resellers and cloud marketplaces.
  • Strong commercial acumen: comfortable with deal structuring, pricing and discount negotiation.
  • Excellent communication and stakeholder management; able to influence partner and internal leaders without direct authority.
  • Organized and operationally minded, with a bias for action and follow-through.
  • Experience leading or developing a team preferred. Familiarity with video collaboration or the Microsoft, Zoom and Google ecosystems is a plus.


Success Measures (First 12 Months)

  • Partner-sourced and partner-influenced pipeline and bookings at or above target.
  • Digital marketplace incentive revenue and contribution to the bottom line at or above target, with co-sell registrations and incentive claims submitted accurately and on time.
  • Alliance operating cadence run consistently, with QBRs delivered on schedule.
  • Improved deal velocity and renewal rates across alliance accounts.
  • Measurable gains in partner and internal seller enablement, shown through engagement, co-sell adoption and pipeline impact.
  • Clean partner operations, with timely deal registration, invoicing and reconciliation.
  • Strong working relationships with partner field leaders and the Pexip Enterprise, Marketing and Finance teams.
  • New and emerging partners onboarded and supported to the level agreed with the VP

Supported by institutional investors and guided by a double bottom line philosophy, the company consistently delivers impact at scale and profitability with purpose.

As we enter its next phase of growth, it is shaping the future of AI-led public education infrastructure - where technology, partnerships, and governance intelligence converge to redefine how nations learn and thrive.

Role Overview :

As the AI Safety & Evaluation Lead with us, you will own the process ensuring every AI system deployed is accurate, safe, unbiased, secure, and compliant. Given that we serve children and underserved communities across India, this role carries direct responsibility for learner trust, content safety, and regulatory standing. A core dimension of this role is understanding student psychology, since our entire user base is school and college-going students, and AI outputs must be designed to handle sensitive or negative queries (e.g. distressing searches by students) in a safe, age-appropriate manner that does not surface harmful information. This role is part of a 0-to-1 vertical build. The person joining should be comfortable with ambiguity, high ownership, rapid iteration, hands-on execution, team building, and periods of high-intensity work during the early setup phase.

Key Responsibilities :

- Design and own the AI evaluation framework : benchmark construction, automated and human-in-the-loop eval pipelines.

- Lead red-teaming and adversarial testing across deployed models : prompt injection, jailbreaking, edge case identification.

- Define AI safety standards, responsible AI policies, and child-safe content guardrails for deployment at scale.

- Build and maintain evaluation tooling : RAGAS, LangSmith, PromptBench, EleutherAI lm-evaluation-harness.

- Conduct systematic bias detection and fairness measurement across outputs, especially for regional and linguistic variation.

- Manage AI risk assessments and translate safety findings into actionable model or prompt changes.

- Establish AI governance documentation : model cards, audit trails, safety reports for internal and regulatory stakeholders.

- Embed evaluation and safety checkpoints into the model release pipeline in collaboration with engineering.

- Track and apply evolving regulatory requirements : EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF, India AI policy frameworks.

- Measure and report model accuracy, grounding fidelity, and response quality across deployed AI systems through systematic evaluation.

- Build and maintain knowledge of AI governance and compliance standards - operationalising responsible AI practices into daily engineering workflows.

Must-Have Skills :

- Strong experience in AI/LLM safety, evaluation, and risk assessment.

- Expertise in designing and executing model evaluation frameworks and test methodologies.

- Experience in red-teaming, adversarial testing, and identifying model vulnerabilities.

- Strong understanding of bias, fairness, hallucination, and content safety in AI systems.

- Experience measuring model accuracy, grounding, and response quality.

- Knowledge of AI governance, compliance, and responsible AI practices.

- Familiarity with frameworks such as NIST AI RMF and AI regulatory standards; understanding of student psychology and age-appropriate AI output design.

- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with experience working on production AI systems.

What We Offer and Why You Should Join us :

We create an environment where purpose meets growth. You will be part of a mission driven organization that is transforming how learning reaches children across India, especially at scale and where it matters most.

- Work with a diverse and passionate team spread across India, bringing together people from different backgrounds, perspectives, and expertise.

- Be part of an organization with a strong on ground presence across more than two thirds of India, giving you exposure to large scale, real world impact.

- Play a meaningful role in strengthening the education ecosystem and contributing directly to learning outcomes for millions of children.

- Gain experience working at the intersection of education, technology, and public systems, building skills that are highly relevant and future focused.

- Work in a culture that values ownership, learning, and collaboration, with space to take initiative and grow professionally.

- Enjoy stability and peace of mind with employee friendly benefits, including health insurance coverage and other supportive policies.

- If you are driven by purpose, enjoy solving complex problems, and want your work to create visible impact, we offer a place to grow while making a difference.

IRCA Group USA LLC is the Group’s US subsidiary and the hub of our Americas business, including Dobla USA, with offices in Duluth, GA and Chicago, IL. The Americas are a priority growth market for the Group, combining organic expansion with an active M&A agenda.

Role

Reporting to the Director, FP&A, the Senior FP&A Analyst will play a critical role in driving the performance of the Americas business. The role owns the budgeting, forecasting and performance-analysis cycle and provides leadership with clear visibility on profitability by plant, product and customer, supporting pricing, sourcing and investment decisions. This is a highly visible position, working closely with Commercial, Operations, Procurement and Accounting in the US, and with Group Finance in Italy.

We are requiring someone to work onsite at our plant located in Duluth, GA.

Responsibilities

  • Budgeting and forecasting: Lead the bottom-up annual budget, interim forecasts and monthly outlooks for the Americas, including Gross Margin estimate and SG&A costs, and turn the methodology into the backbone of monthly performance reviews.

  • Variance analysis: Perform critical analysis of Monthly results and collect and synthesize business insights on variances

  • Insight for leadership and the Board: Analyze monthly results, explain variances in plain business terms and deliver the financial content for leadership and Board decks. Support business cases and the integration of acquired businesses as part of our M&A agenda.

  • Automation and scale: Automate data flows and turn one-off analyses into reliable, recurring reporting processes.

  • Product and customer profitability. Build and own SKU (product) and customer-level profitability models that link revenue, raw materials, conversion costs and operating expenses. Partner with Pricing, Sales, Procurement and Operations to pinpoint the true margin drivers and close the gap between contracted and actual margins

  • Sourcing and raw material economics. Compare contractual pricing assumptions with actual supplier costs, surface margin leakage and unprofitable contracts, quantify the impact and give management a recurring view that sharpens pricing and procurement decisions. Track and validate Procurement savings initiatives.

  • Reporting integrity: Review GL accounts, cost centers and P&L mapping, fix misclassifications at the root with Accounting, HR and headquarters, and embed standardized allocation frameworks that make monthly results accurate and comparable.

Qualifications

  • Education. Bachelor’s degree in Business, Finance, Economics or Engineering.

  • Experience. 3+ years in FP&A, commercial finance or cost accounting, ideally in manufacturing, food or ingredients.

  • Cost accounting and variance analysis. Hands-on experience building and analyzing detailed, multi-site P&Ls. A track record of investigating manufacturing variances, reviewing GL and cost-center allocations and quantifying the financial impact of what you find.

  • Profitability and pricing analysis. Experience building product- and customer-level profitability models that support pricing and customer portfolio decisions.

  • Forecasting and budgeting. Bottom-up forecasting and budgeting experience, including designing methodologies and coordinating inputs across functions.

  • Tools. Advanced Excel and financial modeling skills; experience with ERP systems and BI tools (e.g., Power BI) is a strong plus.

  • Communication. The ability to go from granular detail to a crisp executive narrative, and to influence stakeholders at every level.

  • Mindset. Hands-on, curious and driven by ownership: you dive into the details without losing sight of the big picture.

  • Languages. Italian or Spanish is a plus.

Medical, Dental, & Vision, 401(k) matching, Paid Vacation, and Holidays, Employee Education Tuition Reimbursement Program

title: Curator of Primates
description:
The Indianapolis Zoo is looking for a Curator of Primates to lead the care, management, and long-term planning of our primate collection. This position provides leadership and direction to animal care staff while maintaining direct accountability for animal welfare, husbandry, behavioral management, and collection health.

Working closely with veterinary services, conservation, research, facilities, and other Zoo teams, the Curator of Primates helps advance species-appropriate care, support responsible population management, and contribute to the Zoo's mission to protect nature and inspire people to care for our world.


Key Responsibilities

  • Provide leadership, supervision, and professional development for Assistant Curators and animal care staff, establishing clear expectations and promoting a culture of accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement.
  • Maintain direct accountability for the health, welfare, behavioral management, and husbandry standards of the primate collection.
  • Oversee animal introductions, social group management, breeding recommendations, animal transfers, and collection planning in collaboration with appropriate partners.
  • Develop, evaluate, and improve animal care practices, behavioral enrichment, training programs, and welfare assessment procedures.
  • Collaborate with veterinary services on animal health, preventive care, treatment plans, cooperative medical training, and ongoing welfare assessments.
  • Establish departmental goals, manage operating plans and budgets, and identify priorities for staffing, equipment, animal care, and facility improvements.
  • Ensure compliance with applicable regulations, institutional policies, animal care standards, safety procedures, and documentation requirements.

What We're Looking For

  • A bachelor's degree in Biology or a related field from an accredited college or university. A graduate degree in a related field preferred.
  • A minimum of 10 years of direct or related experience in a zoo or similar professional setting, including at least four years of demonstrated personnel management.
  • Experience working with primates, such as chimpanzees, orangutans, gibbons, baboons, or tamarins, preferred.
  • Demonstrated leadership, supervisory, communication, and interpersonal skills.
  • The ability to make sound decisions, manage competing priorities, and lead teams in a dynamic animal care environment.
  • Strong organizational skills and the ability to collaborate effectively across departments and with external professional partners.
  • The ability to work a flexible schedule, including evenings, weekends, and overtime as needed, and work outdoors in varying weather conditions.

Why Join Us?

At the Indianapolis Zoo, your work contributes to something bigger. Join a team dedicated to exceptional animal care, wildlife conservation and inspiring people to care for our world. As Curator of Primates, you'll have the opportunity to lead a talented animal care team, help shape the future of the primate collection, and make a meaningful impact on animal welfare and conservation.

About Tutor
We believe robots should be the next chapter in making physical labor safer and more affordable. But, nearly nine out of ten American factories and warehouses don’t have a single robot. Tutor Intelligence is changing that.
We build robots that go straight into real factories and warehouses, to do real work, with real impact. Our robot Cassie does back-breaking work, moving boxes, pallets, and bulk goods for family-owned manufacturers to some of the largest brands in the world. Our robot Sonny does handwork, using two arms to achieve human-like dexterity in picking and packing. Every robot learns on the job, and each one we deploy makes the next one more capable, more affordable, and faster to put to work.
Founded at MIT and headquartered in Watertown, MA, we do it all in-house: the robotics hardware, the machine learning, and the field deployment and service. We’re a team of researchers, engineers, technicians, operators, and sellers who love building things and solving hard problems.
Our mission is grand: robots everywhere, for the common good, raising the standard of living across North America, and then the world.
Why Tutor?
Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.
Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.
The Role
Tutor Intelligence robots run production on customer floors across North America. The fleet is growing faster than the tools behind it.
This role exists to fix that by building. The job is to find the parts of the operation that are held together with tape and replace them with something that works. Each project starts with a problem and very little else: no spec, no existing tool, no one to hand the work to. The person in this seat figures out what should exist, builds the first version, puts it in front of the people who need it, and keeps improving it until it runs on its own. Then it's on to the next one.
The role reports to the Head of Robot Operations and Reliability.
What the work looks like
Most of what it takes to run a much larger fleet hasn't been built yet. This role builds it. That means looking at how the operation runs today, finding where it breaks or slows down, and building what should be there instead. The work is tools, data, and the way the work itself gets done.
The work will keep changing as the fleet grows. What stays the same is the job itself: see the problem, build the fix, put it to use, and keep improving it until it runs on its own.
The hard failures
Some robot failures don't make sense at first. A sensor tests fine on the bench and fails on the floor. A robot runs clean for three weeks and then stops every afternoon at 2:00. This role leads those investigations. That means pulling logs, reading field reports and parts history, talking to the technician who was there, building a theory, testing it, and staying with it until the cause is found and the fix holds.
Who this is for
Someone who asks why a problem happened, not just how to make it stop, and who looks for the structure behind it: the process, the data, or the handoff that let it happen. Someone who, after watching a team struggle with the same problem twice, has already sketched a fix that keeps it from happening a third time, and built the first version. Someone who would rather own a result than report on one.
This can be an early-career role for someone with clear momentum, or a step up for someone five or more years in who is done reporting on problems they could have fixed. Either way, someone who learns fast, gets noticeably better every quarter, and wants the job to grow with the fleet.

Projects on the list

  • A training system that gives a field technician real-time instructions on the robot in front of them, built from what the fleet has already learned about that failure.
  • Issue tracking that joins robot telemetry to what the technician saw on the floor, so an investigation goes from symptom to root cause and the fix can be checked across the fleet.
  • Predictive tooling that flags a robot likely to fail before it does, from telemetry and parts history.
  • Capacity planning for a regional network of technicians: where they should be based, how many, and how fast they need to reach a robot.
  • The reliability data itself: what gets captured, how it connects, and which numbers are worth tracking.

How the work gets done

  • Code is a daily tool here, and so are AI agents. Build systems where agents pull the data, run the checks, and draft the write-ups, so the work runs without a person in the loop.
  • Ship a rough first version early, put it in front of real users, and improve it from what they say.
  • Work side by side with engineering, customer success and field technicians. Much of the best input comes from the people closest to the robots.
  • When something finally works, write it down so the next person can run it without asking.

Required

  • 2–7 years as a technical program manager, industrial engineer, or engineer, or in operations or a similar technical role.
  • A track record of building. At least one system, tool or program designed from scratch and put into real use, with a result that can be stated in numbers.
  • Comfortable building software with AI coding tools and agents, or ready to pick it up fast. The language matters less than having shipped something that works.
  • Clear thinking, and the ability to turn data into a clean picture that others can act on.
  • Clear writing for engineers, customers and leadership.
  • A degree in engineering or a technical field, or equivalent experience.

Stands out

  • Has started something at a past job that didn't exist before, and it's still running.
  • Experience in robotics, automation, manufacturing, logistics or fulfillment.
  • Builds outside of work too: side projects, a home lab, something made just to see if it could be done.

Probably not the right fit for someone who

  • Prefers a clear task list and regular check-ins.
  • Would rather maintain an existing system than build a new one.
  • Wants the same week, every week.

Why join

  • Few places hand one person this much ownership of how a fleet runs.
  • What gets built here becomes how a robotics company runs its fleet.
  • The role grows as the fleet grows.

Benefits

  • Fully employer-covered health insurance, so you’re protected without the premium.
  • A managed 401(k) to help you plan for the future.
  • Generous time off: unlimited PTO and all federal holidays off for full-time salaried employees, and 16+ days of accrued paid time off plus 1.5x pay on federal holidays for hourly employees.
  • Regular in-office meals and team social events throughout the year.
Compensation
The base salary range for this role is $100,000 to $140,000, depending on experience.
Location and travel
In office in Watertown, MA. Travel to customer sites and regional teams as needed, roughly 10–25%.
To apply
Along with a résumé, send a short note about something you built: what the problem was, what you made, and what happened after. Links, photos and code are all welcome.
As Tutor grows, so will our benefits. We’re continuing to invest in ways to support our team at work and beyond.
Tutor Intelligence is an equal opportunity employer and welcomes applicants from all backgrounds.

  • You've built test fixtures, bench rigs or HIL systems that others used
  • Python for test automation and data analysis
  • Strong electrical skills: schematics, scopes, meters, CAN
  • Comfortable on the production floor, working alongside technicians

Nice to Have

  • Experience bringing a new robot or hardware product into production
  • Humanoid, mobile robot or robot arm experience
  • Embedded firmware or Linux experience
  • MES/PLM experience (ION or similar)
  • Daily use of AI tools like Claude to build tools and analyze data

Why Tutor?

Whether you’re designing robots, closing deals, running deployments, or creating the processes that help us scale, your work doesn’t sit on a shelf. It shows up on real production floors, making physical work safer and more affordable.

Our team of 160+ is driven by curiosity and a genuine love of building. Everyone here takes real ownership, learns fast, and holds a high bar while having each other’s backs. If you love hard problems and creating things that didn’t exist before, you’ll fit right in.

title: Designated Coordinator
description:
About Safeway Home Healthcare

Safeway Home Healthcare is a Minnesota 245D-licensed provider supporting children and adults with disabilities across the Twin Cities. We are a growing organization with a lean administrative team and a startup mindset. We value professionalism, teamwork, and creative problem-solving, and we're passionate about the clients we serve and the quality of our programs.

About the Position

We are looking for a proactive, organized, and people-focused Designated Coordinator (DC) to lead daily service delivery and support our clients and Direct Support Professionals (DSPs).

This is a hands-on leadership role for someone who enjoys working with people, solving problems, mentoring staff, and keeping operations running smoothly.

The DC ensures clients receive the right services, DSPs have the support they need, schedules are maintained, and services are delivered efficiently and with quality.

Key Responsibilities

  1. Staff Leadership & Support
  • Serve as the primary contact for DSP questions, call-ins, and concerns.
  • Coach, mentor, and support staff while addressing performance and accountability.
  • Complete incident reports and regular staff check-ins.

2Client Support & Service Delivery

  • Serve as the primary contact for clients and families, addressing concerns promptly and professionally.
  • Assess new clients' needs, home environments, and staffing compatibility.
  • Ensure clients understand their services and DSPs deliver the correct authorized programs.
  • Monitor client satisfaction, resolve service concerns, and identify improvements.

3 New Client Starts & Staff Onboarding

  • Coordinate timely service initiation, meet-and-greets, and intake coordination.
  • Participate in DSP interviews, hiring recommendations, and onboarding.
  • Provide client-specific training and introductions before independent shifts.

4 Staffing & Scheduling

  • Partner with the Staffing Coordinator to manage staffing gaps, call-ins, coverage, and schedule approvals.
  • Monitor service utilization and develop solutions to improve the use of available hours based on client needs and preferences.

5 Quality & Service Oversight

  • Conduct regular quality check-ins and required visits.
  • Identify service concerns and escalate program or compliance issues to the Designated Manager.

6 Operations & Communication

  • Participate in weekly staffing meetings and support client intakes and renewals.
  • Provide team with brief weekly updates on staffing, service utilization, concerns, and priorities.
  • Collaborate with leadership to resolve problems and improve daily operations.

Who We're Looking For

We're looking for a natural leader who is a problem solver, mentor, and exceptional communicator. Someone who genuinely enjoys working with people but is also highly organized, dependable, and able to follow through.

The right person will:

  • Be a problem solver: Take initiative, think critically, and bring solutions rather than just identifying problems.
  • Be a mentor: Coach, encourage, and support DSPs while holding them accountable.
  • Be a people person: Build strong, trusting relationships with clients, families, and staff.
  • Be highly organized: Manage multiple priorities, stay on top of details, and follow through on commitments.
  • Be an exceptional communicator: Communicate clearly, consistently, and promptly—even when the news is difficult or a conversation is uncomfortable.

Qualifications

Good to have: Bilingual or multilingual skills especially Amharic, Tigrinya, Oromo.

Required

  • Meet Minnesota DHS qualification requirements for a Designated Coordinator under applicable 245D regulations.
  • Strong communication, organization, leadership, and problem-solving skills.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities and respond to urgent staffing or client needs.

title: MARINE DIVISION MANAGER
description:
MARINE DIVISION MANAGER



Landmark Solutions Ltd. (Landmark) is growing and we’re seeking an experienced Marine Division Manager to lead our Marine Division and manage the delivery of marine and waterfront projects. This role combines divisional leadership, financial management, client relationships and hands-on project management. The successful candidate will bring practical construction experience and the ability to coordinate people, design, fabrication and installation from early project discussions through completion.

WHO WE ARE

Landmark is a growing, multifaceted company with a dedicated team of professional and support staff, working together to provide our clients with high quality, innovative solutions in the safest, most efficient way. Our professional expertise includes project management, construction, forestry services, environmental services, ecosystem restoration, and marine construction. From concept to completion, we listen carefully to our clients and develop innovative, cost-effective solutions and provide high-quality service with a focus on safety and the protection of environmental and cultural values.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

Reporting to the Chief Operating Officer (COO), the Marine Division Manager is responsible for the division’s people, operations and financial performance by leading the Welding and Fabrication team, Design/Engineering, and Marine Business Development. This permanent, full-time position is based in Salmon Arm, BC, with fieldwork and travel throughout British Columbia, including overnight travel, as project demands require. Duties and responsibilities include, but are not limited to:



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Lead the Marine Division, set priorities and hold employees accountable for safety, quality, performance and follow-through.
  • Manage, mentor and support direct reports; coordinate staffing and performance matters with HR and the COO.
  • Plan divisional workload and resources across business development, design, fabrication and project delivery.
  • Manage divisional budgets, monitor revenue, costs, margins and forecasts, and report performance, risks and corrective actions to the COO.
  • Oversee fabrication through the Welding and Fabrication Manager, aligning shop priorities, capacity and quality with project requirements. Coordinate fabrication work and welding resources required by the Construction Division.
  • Coordinate internal design work and external engineering services with fabrication and installation schedules; provide constructability input and involve qualified professionals for engineering responsibilities.
  • Guide business development priorities and participate in site visits, project scoping, proposals, estimating and key client discussions.
  • Act as Project Manager for marine projects, managing scope, budgets, schedules, resources, contracts, quality, risks and client commitments from planning through closeout.
  • Coordinate procurement, suppliers, subcontractors, crews, equipment and mobilization, working closely with the Construction Division to resolve resource and scheduling needs.
  • Review drawings, specifications, layouts and proposed construction methods to identify practical issues, delivery risks and the need for specialist input.
  • Work on site as projects require, supporting crews with installation planning, sequencing, equipment decisions and practical problem-solving.
  • Ensure Landmark’s health, safety, environmental and quality requirements are implemented; coordinate environmental and permitting matters with qualified professionals and specialists.
  • Monitor project progress and costs, manage scope changes, and maintain accurate records to support reporting, invoicing, inspections and closeout.
  • Review and approve purchases within agreed authority and coordinate larger spending commitments and key personnel decisions with the COO.
  • Ensure project and employee timesheets are accurate, properly allocated and approved on time; work with Administration and HR to maintain reliable divisional processes and coverage during field assignments.
  • Build strong relationships with clients, First Nations, municipalities, marina operators, engineers, consultants and project partners, and apply lessons learned to future projects.



WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR

  • 10+ years of progressively responsible experience in marine construction, waterfront infrastructure, heavy civil construction or a closely related field is preferred.
  • Direct marina or waterfront experience is strongly preferred, particularly with floating structures, piling, marine access, breakwaters or related infrastructure.
  • Demonstrated ability to lead direct reports and coordinate multiple functions, with responsibility for staffing, priorities and performance.
  • Strong project management experience from planning and design coordination through fabrication, field execution and closeout.
  • Sound financial and commercial judgment, including managing budgets, costs, margins, forecasts, contracts and changes.
  • Practical knowledge of marine construction methods and waterfront conditions, including dock systems, piling, anchoring, flotation, access structures, wave protection and marine equipment.
  • Ability to read drawings and specifications, identify constructability concerns and recognize when engineering, environmental or other specialist input is needed.
  • Excellent communication and organizational skills, with the ability to build trust, resolve issues and balance divisional management with project and field demands.
  • Strong office administration and computer skills, including Microsoft Office, purchasing approvals, timesheet review, project records and reporting. Experience with project-management, scheduling or cost-control software is an asset.
  • A practical, respectful leadership style, sound judgment and a strong commitment to workplace safety, environmental responsibility and quality.
  • Valid BC Class 5 Driver’s Licence with a clean driving record.
  • Willingness to work on active job sites and travel throughout British Columbia, including overnight travel, as project requirements demand.



EDUCATION AND EXPERIENCE PATHWAYS

Landmark values practical construction knowledge and recognizes that strong leaders enter the profession through different pathways. Candidates may qualify through either:

  • Relevant post-secondary education in construction management, engineering technology, engineering, business or a related discipline, together with relevant construction and leadership experience; OR
  • An equivalent combination of substantial marine or waterfront construction, field, trade, supervisory, project management and operations leadership experience.

Experienced professionals who have progressed into management through field, trade or construction leadership roles are encouraged to apply.



WHAT WE PROVIDE

Landmark is centrally located in the city of Salmon Arm, on beautiful Shuswap Lake in the BC interior. The area offers an abundance of outdoor recreation opportunities, including lakes, hiking trails, camping, fly fishing, mountain biking and skiing. It’s a great place to live, work and play.

We provide:

  • Salary ranges from $100,000 to $120,000 per year, depending on qualifications and experience.
  • Health Spending Plan.
  • Company matched RRSP program.
  • Flexible time off.
  • Career growth and professional development.
  • The opportunity to lead and develop a Marine Division within a growing multidisciplinary company.
  • Direct involvement in marine and waterfront projects from early planning through installation.
  • A collaborative environment with direct access to project and company leadership.



WORK ELIGIBILITY

Applicants must be legally entitled to work in Canada. Landmark is not offering immigration sponsorship for this position.

HOW TO APPLY

Please submit your resume and a brief cover letter through Landmark Solutions’ online careers portal: https://www.landmark-solutions.ca/careers/ All resumes will be handled in confidence.

In your application, highlight the marine or waterfront projects you have delivered, the teams or departments you have led, and your experience managing budgets, fabrication and field operations.

Deadline to apply: Available immediately, open until filled.

For more information on who we are and examples of the work we do, visit our website at www.landmark-solutions.ca

We thank all those who apply; however, only those applicants selected for interviews will be contacted.

title: Data Analyst
description:
Job Description

    To lead the collection, analysis and reporting of data across the Archdiocese's family of Catholic schools and academies, providing timely, accurate and insightful information that supports school improvement, strategic decision-making and statutory obligations.

    The postholder line manages the department's data function, championing high standards of data quality, integrity and compliance, and building the confidence of colleagues and school leaders in the information they rely upon.


    Key responsibilities

    Data analysis & reporting

    • Collect, cleanse, analyse and interpret data from a range of sources to identify trends, patterns and areas for attention.
    • Produce clear reports, dashboards and visualisations that translate complex data into meaningful insight for varied audiences, including senior leadership, trustees and school leaders.
    • Support school improvement and strategic planning by providing robust, evidence-based analysis.

    Data management & systems

    • Maintain accurate, well-organised datasets and ensure the integrity, security and appropriate use of information held by the department.
    • Oversee statutory and periodic data returns, ensuring they are accurate, complete and submitted to deadline.
    • Review and improve data-collection and reporting processes, introducing automation and efficiencies where appropriate.
    • Ensure all handling of data complies with UK GDPR, the Data Protection Act 2018 and the Archdiocese's own policies.

    Line management

    • Line manage, support and develop the department's data staff, setting clear objectives and priorities.
    • Manage workloads, allocate tasks and monitor performance, providing regular feedback and supervision.
    • Foster a positive, collaborative and professional team culture, and support the wellbeing and development of team members.

    Collaboration & stakeholder engagement

    • Work closely with colleagues across the Education Department and wider Archdiocese to understand and meet their information needs.
    • Build effective working relationships with schools, academy trusts and external partners.
    • Respond to data queries and requests promptly, accurately and helpfully.

    General

    • Keep up to date with relevant developments in data practice, the education sector and data-protection law.
    • Undertake any other reasonable duties commensurate with the role, as required.


    Person specification


    Qualifications

    Essential

    • Degree, or equivalent qualification, in a numerate, data or information-related discipline — or equivalent demonstrable experience
    • Evidence of continued professional development

    Desirable

    • Professional qualification or accreditation in data analysis, statistics or a related field
    • Certification in data tools such as Power BI or SQL


    Experience

    Essential

    • Substantial experience of collecting, cleansing, analysing and interpreting large and complex datasets
    • Experience of producing clear reports, dashboards and visualisations for a range of audiences
    • Experience of line managing, supervising or coordinating the work of others

    Desirable

    • Experience of working within an education, charitable or not-for-profit setting
    • Experience of school performance or pupil data, and of statutory returns such as the School Census


    Skills & abilities

    Essential

    • Advanced Excel skills and proficiency with data and reporting tools (for example Power BI, SQL or equivalent)
    • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with a high level of accuracy and attention to detail
    • Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to present complex data clearly and simply
    • Ability to lead, motivate and develop a small team, and to manage competing priorities to deadline

    Desirable

    • Ability to design and automate reporting processes to improve efficiency


    Knowledge

    Essential

    • Sound understanding of data protection obligations, including UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018
    • Working knowledge of data analysis techniques and data-visualisation good practice

    Desirable

    • Knowledge of the education sector, including academies, multi-academy trusts and the Ofsted framework
    • Awareness of DfE and Catholic Education Service (CES) data requirements


    Personal Qualities

    Essential

      • Respect for, and a willingness to support, the ethos, mission and values of the Catholic Church and of Catholic education
      • Discretion, integrity and sound judgement when handling confidential and sensitive information
      • A collaborative, professional and solution-focused approach


      Other Requirements

      Essential

      • Willingness to travel across the Archdiocese as the role requires
      • Satisfactory references, and any pre-employment checks appropriate to the post
      • The right to work in the United Kingdom (see statement below)


      Safeguarding

      The Archdiocese of Southwark is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children, young people and adults at risk, and expects all staff and volunteers to share this commitment. The successful candidate will be required to undertake the pre-employment checks appropriate to this post.


      Right to work & visa sponsorship

      Applicants must have the right to work in the United Kingdom. The Archdiocese of Southwark is unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role, and candidates must be able to evidence their right to work in the UK before an appointment can be confirmed.


      This job description reflects the current requirements of the role. It is not exhaustive and may be reviewed and amended, in consultation with the postholder, to meet the changing needs of the department.


      We are unable to offer visa sponsorship for this role. Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK without the need for sponsorship, and will be asked to provide evidence of their right to work.

title: Campaign Assistant
description:
The Campaign Assistant will serve as an integral member of the Campaign team and the primary support staff for the Director of Development and larger campaign team. They support the creation of campaign materials & reports; support individual and group cultivation, solicitation and stewardship; help manage campaign-related meetings and committees; and assist with general campaign projects. The Campaign Assistant helps ensure that the Campaign Team provides the necessary support to the Head of School, other key administrators, the Campaign Chairs, and other campaign volunteers. Serving as the primary liaison between the campaign team, committees, and advancement services, the Campaign Assistant is a highly focused project manager who thrives on managing timelines, ensuring accuracy, and producing materials that reflect a high set of standards, ultimately helping drive the campaign forward.

title: Bilingual Classroom Aide
description:
Job Title: Bilingual Classroom Aide

Direct Supervisor: Bilingual Program Coordinator/School Manager

Summary of Position:

The Classroom Aide works alongside our trained guides/teachers, primary classroom assistant(s), floating classroom assistants, and other team members in our Montessori Program. They will support a primary classroom of children ages 3-5 at our tuition free full day Montessori program. The Classroom Aide will be responsible for handling a variety of tasks both inside and outside of the classroom. The Classroom Aide is a supplemental and vital member of the classroom educational environment and will spend their day creating a positive educational experience for each student.


This position will be also assigned specific children for additional support throughout the school day related to that child's special educational needs. This will include using interventions recommended on the child's IFSP and high level of patience and care

This is a full-time non-exempt position based on a school year/school day schedule. Occasional evening or weekend work may be required as it relates to annual or specialized training or school events. Monday through Friday 7am-3pm on all school days. This position will require enrolling and completing assigned Montessori assistant training, or 2 months of work experience within a Montessori Primary Classroom and will require immediate and ongoing training throughout employment. At this time we can only promise this position to continue through the 26-27 school year, and we are opening new classrooms in Fall 2027.

Job Purpose:

On day-to-day activities this position will report to and works with the classroom lead teachers/guides, with the Bilingual Program Coordinator being their formal supervisor to assign new duties or areas of responsibility. Responsible for assisting the lead teachers in classroom preparation & management and children’s learning. They will also work closely with the full classroom team, floating classroom assistants and other members of the AEME team to support students. Responsible for for active hands-on support to assigned students with special needs care.

Minimum Requirements Include:

  • Updated: Verified with documentation in place that they age 18 or older and meet Oregon Office of Childcare Aide 1 or Aide 2 qualification (240 documented hours of experience as Aide, which will include 80 hours with an AEME classroom).
  • Enrollment in the Oregon Central Background Registry verified prior to start date
  • Attain and maintain Current CPR/1st Aid, RRCAN, and Food Handlers certificate. And complete other mandated training by hire or within week 1 of the start date.
  • Meet State of Oregon ORO Step level requirements for Preschool For All funding. Step 4 or higher. At minimum must have ORO Step 2 and will be able to complete all training hours to attain Step 4 within school year of hire.

And,

  • Some experience working within a Montessori primary classroom and assessed to have the skills and personal attributes to perform this role consistently.
  • Fluency in Spanish/English – written and verbal (or other specific language needed for that classroom placement).
  • Experience (and joy in!) working with young children, including children with delays, disabilities or behaviors that are impacting learning
  • Compassionate communication style and positive attitude
  • Highly dependable- will consistently arrive on time and complete work tasks.
  • Must have a High School Degree or GED or skills necessary to perform this role well.
  • Personal dedication to continual self-improvement and skills growth.
  • Significant physical abilities including mobility in the classroom/outdoor areas, lifting/carrying, reaching/handling, talking/haring conversations, near/far visual acuity/depth perception/accommodation/field of vision.


Preference for Applicants with

  • Direct experience within our Montessori classrooms, OR 1+ years experience in a Montessori Primary or Infant/Toddler classroom.
  • Current enrollment in Oregon Central Background Registry, and up to date with CPR/1st Aid, Food Handlers, and other required training with an AIDE 2 status.
  • ORO Step 5 or above

Daily Responsibilities:

  1. Working with the teacher, other assistants, and AEME staff to create an environment that demonstrates rapport with, and respect and kindness for, all students, as well as positive relationships between students. The aide models and teaches with dedication to equity, diversity and inclusion, integrating in age-appropriate conflict resolution and problem-solving strategies in the classroom.
  2. Provide assistance to assigned child(ren) during the school day to help them fully benefit from the Montessori classroom.
  3. Work as a team to promote positive work dynamics and care of the children/classroom.
  4. The aide pays close attention to the safety of the children. No child should ever be left unsupervised either inside or outside the classroom. Adhere to staff/student ratios of 1/10 and always sign-in and out of the classroom as well as verbally communicate with team to ensure ratio is met before leaving the classroom or playground space for other work tasks or breaks. Aide 1 staff are not to be unsupervised with children.
  5. Support the teacher with interpretation or translation of information to support student learning within the classroom.
  6. Remains open to coaching and continued skill development and refreshing of skills and best practices to support our classrooms high quality standards.
  7. Classroom Preparation, including daily general cleaning, inventory of supplies (pencils, paper, etc.), helping to arrange the furniture and activities, material making, etc.
  8. Assisting the children in the development of independence. This will include supporting children in choosing purposeful activities; dispensing supplies; greeting late arrivals; assisting children with their communication or helping them resolve conflicts; indicating where to wait for the Guide when necessary; reporting any abnormal or unusual situations to the Guide; helping a child who is injured to take care of herself.
  9. Communicate promptly information shared by a parent/guardian with the Lead Teacher or School site lead as appropriate.
  10. Provide toileting support and active assistance to a child when a toileting accident occurs. This may include changing diapers or pull ups for a child throughout the year.
  11. Developing and maintaining a positive and supportive relationship with each child, while respecting and fostering her/his independence. Using positive language phrases and words with the children. Providing emotional support and understanding through active listening and feedback.
  12. Setting up and putting away napping cots and linens.
  13. Washing and caring for bed and classroom linens for program/classrooms.
  14. Food preparation and nutritional program support, which may include cooking or transferring of meals between cafeteria and classroom.
  15. Perform all other duties as assigned.

Other Responsibilities:

  1. Work collaboratively with the guide/teacher to prepare an environment that meets the sensitive period/plane of development of the children within the classroom.
  2. Learn the first name or preferred name of each student as well as their parent/guardian for daily greeting and building positive relationships.
  3. Assisting or inventorying the classroom materials and supplies and communicating with the teacher and manager/director on items needing replacement or repair.
  4. Remain eager to learn and grow skills within the classroom environment. Ask the teacher to provide training and coaching in providing lessons or classroom tasks.
  5. Making classroom materials under the guidance of the Lead Guide/Primary Classroom Assistant.
  6. Escorting and supervision of students using our bus transportation services and following protocols and demonstrating professional judgment in situations as they arise.
  7. The aid may be asked to support and participate in school functions, including but not limited to open houses, performances and celebrations, parent orientations, parent events and information nights, and school picnics.
  8. Have a firm commitment to upholding our mission and anti-bias/anti-racist pedagogy.

Physical Requirements:

Must have the ability to:

  • Lift up to 50 lbs.
  • Be able to perform repetitive bending, stretching, and stooping.
  • Have the personal mobility required to ensure the safety of the children.
  • Flexibility to be able to work with children on the floor.
  • Lead physical education or outdoor activities in all seasons.
  • Perform light duty cleaning regularly.
  • Visually monitor students and classroom activities for safety, hygiene, and learning.
  • Handle strong smells.

ORO Step 4 – requires a minimum of 50 hours of ORO approved training hours in early childhood education. Step 4 requires 4 hours in Human Growth & Development; 4 hours in Understanding and Guiding Behavior; and at least 4 other training hours in the other 8 core knowledge categories. A college quarter credit option is also available with specific requirements. All training must be uploaded and accepted by ORO in the State Portal.

title: Administrative Director Federated Humane Societies of PA
description:
Purpose:

Federated Humane Societies of Pennsylvania (Federated) connects and represents Pennsylvania animal shelters and rescues, strengthens collaboration and professional resources, and advances informed statewide discussions about shelter services, municipal responsibilities, sustainable funding, and the importance of the essential animal services provided.

Position Overview:

The Administrative Director manages Federated's daily operations and implements strategic priorities under the direction of the President and Executive Committee. The role combines association administration duties, membership development, statewide outreach, public education, event management and coordination, legislative relationship-building, research, communications, fundraising support, and financial oversight. The Administrative Director serves as a primary point of contact for shelters, rescues, municipal associations, policymakers, funders, and partner organizations.

Federated is currently housed within the York County SPCA, which provides the organizational infrastructure, resources, and administrative support necessary to help the association grow and thrive. The Administrative Director will benefit from the experience, expertise, and operational support of the York County SPCA team, ensuring the tools and resources needed to successfully fulfill responsibilities while advancing Federated’s mission are provided. This relationship is designed to be a launching pad, with the long-term goal of establishing Federated as an independent entity once key strategic and financial milestones have been achieved.

York County SPCA and Federated’s member agencies are deeply committed to nurturing the association through its formative years and positioning it for long-term sustainability and success. For the right candidate, this is a rare and exciting opportunity to help build something truly special from the ground up. This position will be fundamental in shaping the direction of a growing statewide association, strengthening collaboration among animal welfare organizations, and creating a lasting impact for shelters, rescues, advocacy organizations, and the animals and communities they serve across Pennsylvania.

Essential Functions:

Organizational Administration and Daily Operations

  • Manage the day-to-day administrative operations of Federated, ensuring that organizational activities, deadlines, communications, and projects are completed efficiently.
  • Coordinate and schedule all meetings involving Federated, including Executive Committee meetings, outside agency meetings, and other stakeholder meetings.
  • Serve as the primary administrative point of contact for members, prospective members, partner organizations, vendors, and the general public.
  • Manage organizational email, telephone inquiries, correspondence, and incoming requests, directing matters to appropriate leadership when necessary.
  • Provide regular progress updates to the President and Executive Committee, identifying completed activities, upcoming priorities, outstanding decisions, and potential challenges.

Membership Development and Member Services

  • Develop, implement, and administer Federated's statewide membership program for Pennsylvania animal shelters.
  • Maintain an accurate membership database and directory, including organizational contacts, geographic representation, membership status, and renewal dates.
  • Develop recruitment materials, membership communications, informational packets, and presentations explaining the value of Federated membership.
  • Coordinate member surveys, listening sessions, and individual conversations to identify operational challenges, resource needs, and legislative concerns.
  • Establish and maintain opportunities for shelter-to-shelter communication, networking, information sharing, and professional collaboration.
  • Identify and develop meaningful membership benefits, including educational opportunities, professional resources, partnerships, discounts, and access to relevant information.
  • Monitor membership growth, retention, participation, and satisfaction, providing regular reports and recommendations to leadership.
  • Assist with the implementation and administration of membership standards, ethical requirements, and organizational policies.

External Relations, Partnerships, and Statewide Outreach

  • Represent Federated professionally in meetings, conferences, educational events, and discussions with organizations throughout Pennsylvania.
  • Establish and maintain relationships with statewide municipal and professional associations, including organizations representing townships, boroughs, municipal managers, and other local government officials.
  • Develop relationships with animal welfare associations, professional organizations, veterinary groups, academic institutions, and other potential partners.
  • Identify organizations and individuals whose interests intersect with animal sheltering, animal control, municipal services, public health, and animal welfare.
  • Initiate contact with prospective partners, arrange introductory meetings, and maintain consistent follow-up communications.
  • Educate stakeholders about Federated's mission, Pennsylvania's animal sheltering system, and the services shelters provide to communities.
  • Identify opportunities for collaborative projects, educational partnerships, shared resources, and organizational sponsorships.
  • Maintain an organized stakeholder contact database documenting relationships, meeting histories, opportunities, and required follow-up.
  • Coordinate participation in professional conferences, regional meetings, association gatherings, and other statewide networking opportunities.
  • Develop relationships that increase Federated's visibility, credibility, membership participation, and opportunities for long-term organizational support.

Legislative Relations, Government Affairs, and Advocacy Support

  • Establish and maintain professional, nonpartisan working relationships with Pennsylvania legislators, legislative staff, relevant committees, commissions, state agencies, and municipal officials.
  • Coordinate introductory meetings and educational briefings with government officials to increase awareness of Pennsylvania's animal sheltering system.
  • Monitor relevant legislation, policy discussions, government initiatives, and administrative developments affecting animal shelters and rescues.
  • Research legislative proposals and prepare summaries, background materials, and informational reports for the President, Executive Committee, and Board.
  • Maintain organized legislative files, including bill information, committee activity, stakeholder correspondence, research materials, and meeting notes.
  • Coordinate with shelter leaders and other stakeholders to collect operational information, examples, and perspectives relevant to legislative discussions.
  • Support leadership in identifying, developing, and implementing Federated's annual legislative priorities and organizational positions.
  • Arrange meetings with legislative committees, research commissions, municipal associations, and other government-related organizations.
  • Prepare educational presentations, briefing documents, testimony drafts, correspondence, and other materials for leadership review and approval.
  • Coordinate approved advocacy activities, member communications, and stakeholder outreach in accordance with organizational policies and delegated authority.
  • Explore opportunities for educational forums, legislative briefings, and collaborative discussions concerning animal sheltering and municipal responsibilities.
  • Maintain accurate records of legislative outreach, meetings, correspondence, commitments, and follow-up activities.

Communications, Public Education, and Professional Presentations

  • Manage Federated's public-facing communications to ensure consistent, accurate, professional messaging.
  • Maintain and update the organizational website, including membership information, resources, organizational news, events, and educational materials.
  • Manage social media platforms, develop content, monitor engagement, and coordinate responses to public inquiries.
  • Prepare and distribute legislative updates, organizational announcements, and other recurring communications.
  • Develop professional presentations, reports, educational materials, and informational resources for animal shelters, public education, legislators, municipalities, county representatives, and other associations.
  • Coordinate media inquiries, interviews, public statements, and other external communications with organizational leadership.
  • Develop materials that communicate the role of Pennsylvania animal shelters, their operational challenges, community services, and funding needs.
  • Maintain a library of approved presentations, talking points, photographs, graphics, organizational branding, and communications templates.
  • Monitor the effectiveness of communications and outreach efforts and recommend improvements.

Research, Data Collection, and Organizational Resources

  • Conduct research concerning Pennsylvania animal shelter operations, municipal animal services, public funding, relevant legislation, and related statewide issues.
  • Maintain and expand Federated's research materials, including state comparisons, policy summaries, reports, and informational resources.
  • Develop and administer surveys and other methods for collecting information from shelters, rescues, municipalities, and relevant stakeholders.
  • Compile and organize data concerning shelter services, operating expenses, municipal contracts, public funding, staffing, and other organizational needs.
  • Review animal shelter and legislative data driving position statements and legislative priorities for accuracy, consistency, and appropriate documentation before distribution or publication.
  • Prepare research summaries, informational reports, presentations, and briefing materials for leadership, members, funders, and other stakeholders.
  • Identify gaps in available information and recommend additional research or data collection.
  • Develop practical resources for member organizations, including templates, educational materials, professional guidance, and relevant funding information.
  • Coordinate with subject-matter experts, professional associations, and partner organizations to strengthen research quality and resource development.
  • Maintain an accessible organizational library of research, reference materials, and approved publications.

Financial Administration, Fundraising, and Organizational Development

  • Work with the President, Treasurer, York County SPCA’s Finance Director, and Executive Committee to prepare, maintain, and monitor Federated's annual operating budget.
  • Track organizational revenue, expenses, financial commitments, and progress toward established financial goals.
  • Coordinate membership dues, donations, sponsorships, grants, event revenue, and other organizational income.
  • Process approved invoices, reimbursements, and payments while maintaining accurate supporting documentation.
  • Prepare regular financial summaries, budget comparisons, and reports for leadership review.
  • Coordinate with York County SPCA’s Finance Director and Federated’s contracted CPO/ business consultants concerning bookkeeping, tax filings, financial reviews, audits, and reporting requirements.
  • Maintain required organizational registrations, charitable filings, licenses, and related administrative records.
  • Research potential grant opportunities and determine eligibility, deadlines, funding priorities, and application requirements.
  • Prepare grant proposals, letters of inquiry, budgets, supporting documentation, and required reports with support of York County SPCA’s Grant Writer
  • Identify prospective donors, sponsors, foundations, and other funding partners.
  • Develop and maintain relationships with individuals and organizations interested in supporting Federated's mission.
  • Assist in developing sustainable revenue opportunities, including membership growth, sponsorships, donations, educational programming, grants, and other approved initiatives.
  • Monitor the financial performance of organizational programs and events and recommend adjustments when necessary.
  • Support long-term financial planning and organizational sustainability.

Governance, Strategic Planning, and Events

  • Maintain organizational governance records, including bylaws, policies, Board rosters, committee assignments, and meeting documentation.
  • Assist leadership with Board recruitment, orientation, committee development, and organizational governance procedures.
  • Support the development, implementation, and regular review of Federated's Strategic Plan.
  • Translate strategic objectives into actionable projects, timelines, and measurable performance goals.
  • Monitor progress toward membership, outreach, financial, partnership, and program-development objectives.
  • Prepare quarterly strategic progress reports and recommend adjustments to organizational priorities.
  • Coordinate the planning and execution of Federated's statewide annual summit, educational programs, regional meetings, and other approved events.

title: Enterprise Instructional Designer
description:
Position Summary

The Instructional Designer transforms organizational concepts, business processes, and operational workflows into engaging, learner-centered training experiences. This role is responsible for designing, developing, and maintaining e-learning modules, instructor-led training materials, and blended learning programs. All learning solutions must align with adult learning principles, enterprise standards, and the company's culture and branding.



Duties and Responsibilities


Curriculum Design and Development

  • Design and develop instructional materials, including interactive e-learning modules, job aids, lesson plans, and facilitator guides for instructor-led, virtual, and self-paced training.
  • Create clear, structured learning experiences that support employee development and operational effectiveness.

Instructional Strategy and Multimedia Integration

  • Apply established instructional design methodologies, including ADDIE and SAM, to develop effective learning solutions.
  • Use modern authoring tools and multimedia elements to create engaging, interactive content that improves learner participation and knowledge retention.

  • Partner with internal subject matter experts, project leads, and stakeholders to translate technical information, operational procedures, and leadership standards into clear, accessible training materials.

  • Develop, publish, and maintain interactive learning modules using industry-standard tools, including Articulate 360, Microsoft Office, and Adobe Creative Cloud.
  • Ensure training materials are compatible with learning management systems (LMS) and cloud-based platforms.

Needs Analysis and Assessment

  • Conduct training needs assessments to identify learning gaps and development opportunities.
  • Create knowledge checks, quizzes, and practical assessments to evaluate learner comprehension, training effectiveness, and knowledge application.

Branding and Content Standards

  • Ensure all training materials, visual assets, and instructional documentation follow FDOT and Florida’s Turnpike Enterprise branding and style guidelines.
  • Maintain a consistent, professional look and feel across all learning materials.

Cloud and Asset Management

  • Organize, maintain, and version-control course files, source materials, media assets, and published training packages within secure cloud storage environments.
  • Maintain accurate documentation and ensure learning assets are accessible and organized for future updates.

Quality Assurance and Prototyping

  • Develop course storyboards, prototypes, and pilot materials to validate instructional approaches before full deployment.
  • Gather stakeholder and learner feedback, test course functionality, and make revisions to improve usability and effectiveness.

Project Management and Stakeholder Communication

  • Manage instructional design projects from initial planning through development, testing, and deployment.
  • Track project milestones, manage competing priorities, meet established deadlines, and provide regular status updates to leadership and stakeholders.

Continuous Improvement

  • Research and incorporate emerging trends in instructional design, learning technology, and adult learning principles.
  • Identify opportunities to improve training content, delivery methods, and the overall learning experience.



Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities

  • Strong knowledge of instructional design theories, adult learning principles, and curriculum development methodologies.
  • Demonstrated experience with e-learning authoring tools, including Articulate 360, Microsoft Office, and Adobe Creative Cloud.
  • Understanding of user experience (UX) principles as they apply to digital learning interfaces and virtual training platforms.
  • Ability to collaborate with subject matter experts and translate complex technical or operational information into clear, engaging learning content.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications for documentation, presentations, and instructional material development.
  • Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage multiple projects, prioritize tasks, and meet deadlines.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including instructional writing and the ability to tailor content to diverse audiences.
  • Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a collaborative learning and development team.
  • Strong attention to detail, problem-solving skills, and a commitment to producing high-quality training materials.


Position Requirements


Education

Bachelor’s degree in Instructional Technology, Computer Science, Information Systems, Education, or a related field, or equivalent relevant work experience.


Experience

A minimum of three years of experience in training, including instructional content development and training delivery.

description:
Role overview :

Crowes Microsoft Consulting Practice is hiring an Agentic Business Process Analyst to help clients rethink how work gets done in the AI era. This is not a traditional business analyst role focused only on documenting requirements, writing user stories, or mapping current-state processes. This role is for someone who can diagnose business problems, understand root causes, redesign processes, and identify where AI agents, automation, data, and human judgment should come together.

The ideal candidate is deeply functional, process-oriented, and comfortable enough with technology to work side by side with engineers, architects, and client IT teams. This person should be able to bridge business and technology, helping clients move from legacy workflows to intelligent, agent-enabled processes.

This role also has an internal transformation mandate. The person will help upskill Crowe Consulting teams that may be used to traditional ERP, CRM, or business application delivery. They will help consultants develop a more modern mindset : start with problems, then processes, then technology.

What you will do :

- Lead discovery sessions with clients to understand business goals, pain points, process breakdowns, data issues, user needs, controls, and operating constraints.

- Map end-to-end business processes, including inputs, outputs, roles, systems, decisions, handoffs, exceptions, controls, and performance measures.

- Diagnose root causes across people, process, data, and technology before recommending solutions.

- Identify opportunities for AI assistance, agentic augmentation, workflow orchestration, automation, knowledge retrieval, decision support, and process improvement.

- Partner with technical architects and engineers to translate process opportunities into solution designs, prototypes, functional specifications, user stories, and delivery roadmaps.

- Define business value measures for agentic solutions, such as time saved, cycle time reduction, first-time-right rate, SLA performance, adoption, override rate, CSAT, cost per transaction, revenue lift, and compliance improvement.

- Help clients decide where humans should stay in control, where AI should assist, and where agents can safely orchestrate or automate work.

- Support workshops, demos, process redesign sessions, executive presentations, and change management conversations.

- Create reusable playbooks, templates, process models, and training materials to help Crowe teams adopt an agentic business analysis approach.

- Coach Crowe consultants on how to move beyond legacy requirements gathering into diagnostic, value-led, AI-enabled transformation work.

What success looks like :

- You can walk into a messy client process and make sense of it quickly.

- You can separate symptoms from root causes.

- You know when the right answer is process redesign, data cleanup, integration, training, governance, automation, or AI.

- You can help clients and internal teams understand what agents should do, what humans should do, and how to measure whether the new process is better.

- You make technical teams sharper by giving them better process context, and you make business teams more confident by helping them understand what technology can realistically do.

Required experience :

- 6 or more years of experience as a business analyst, functional consultant, process consultant, product owner, transformation consultant, or similar role.

- Strong experience mapping, analyzing, and redesigning business processes.

- Experience working on enterprise technology implementations, preferably involving Microsoft Dynamics 365, CRM, ERP, Power Platform, data platforms, workflow automation, or related business applications.

- Ability to facilitate workshops with business users, technical teams, and senior stakeholders.

- Strong understanding of process metrics, business value measurement, operational KPIs, and adoption measures.

- Ability to write clear functional requirements, user stories, process flows, acceptance criteria, solution narratives, and executive-ready recommendations.

- Comfort working with technical teams on AI, automation, data, integration, and system design topics.

- Ability to mentor other consultants and help teams adopt new ways of working.

Preferred experience :

- Experience with Dynamics 365 Sales, Customer Service, Field Service, Customer Insights, Project Operations, Finance, or Supply Chain.

- Experience with Power Platform, Copilot Studio, process mining, business process catalogs, customer journey mapping, service design, or operating model transformation.

- Experience identifying AI use cases, automation candidates, decision support opportunities, or agentic process patterns.

- Experience in consulting or professional services.

- Exposure to responsible AI, governance, risk, compliance, controls, or regulated industry environments.

Mindset we need :

- This person should not be a note-taker or requirements scribe. They should be a transformation-oriented business analyst who can challenge assumptions, ask better questions, and guide clients toward the right solution.

- They should be able to say, The issue is not that you need a chatbot. The issue is that your agents do not have customer history, your systems are disconnected, and your routing rules are inconsistent. That is the mindset Crowe needs to scale.
